title: Jeremiah 11:19
text:
A lamb--brought to the slaughter; unresisting and unconscious of its fate. 
 
  I knew not; that is, before Jehovah revealed it to me.

title: Jeremiah 11:21
text: Anathoth; the birthplace and home of Jeremiah.   Jeremiah 1:1

title: Jeremiah 12:1
text: God does not forbid us to plead with him concerning his dealings, if it be done in the spirit of deep reverence and childlike confidence.  Exodus 32:11-14 Numbers 14:13-21 Isaiah 63:17-19 Isaiah 64:9-12 Acts 22:17-21

title: Jeremiah 12:3
text: When we are tempted to envy the wicked for their prosperity, we should look beyond present appearances and consider their latter end.  Psalms 73:17-20 Luke 16:19-31

title: Jeremiah 12:5
text:
If thou hast run--the swelling of Jordan; Jehovah's answer to the prophet, rebuking his impatience, and bidding him prepare for severer trials.  "The swelling of Jordan," is literally, "the pride of Jordan." Whether we understand this of its swollen flood, which the traveller is compelled to ford, or of the thickets which line its banks and are the habitation of wild beasts,  Jeremiah 49:19 , it is a figure for great difficulties and dangers. 
 
It does not become those whom God has commissioned to preach his word, to faint and be discouraged on account of the persecutions which they endure for the truth's sake.  Rather should they make their present trials the occasion of fortifying themselves for trials in the future.

title: Jeremiah 12:6
text:
Even thy brethren; the men of Anathoth.  If even they have dealt treacherously with thee, prepare to enocunter still greater trials from the rulers of Jerusalem. 
 
In all ages of the world, the wickedness of the human heart has often overcome the closest ties of blood, so that the bitterest foes of the servant of God have been they of his own household.

title: Jeremiah 12:9
text:
A speckled bird; a bird of prey with varigated colors, which is an object of hatred and persecution to the other birds. 
 
  Come ye; a call to the nations to destroy Jerusalem.

title: Jeremiah 12:10
text: Pastors; here heathen rulers, the same as "spoilers,"  Jeremiah 12:2

title: Jeremiah 12:13
text:
They have sown; that is, the Jews.  These words describe the disappointment of all their hopes, especially their trust on alliances with the heathen. 
 
  Your revenues; the result of your vain endeavors.

title: Jeremiah 12:14
text:
Mine evil neighbors; Jehovah calls the surrounding heathen nations his neighbors, because his dwelling-place was in Jerusalem. 
 
  I will pluck them out of their land; by causing them to be carried into captivity. 
 
  From among them; from being among them: I will remove my people from the midst of these nations to Babylon.  The captivity of Judah was followed by that of the surrounding nations that had hated and persecuted her. 
 
Though God employs wicked men as the instruments of chastising his people, he will in the end remember and punish their iniquities.  Isaiah 10:5-19

title: Jeremiah 12:16
text:
If they; these heathen nations. 
 
  Learn the ways of my people; become proselytes to their religion.  Ephesians 2:15-22

title: Jeremiah 13:1
text:
Put it not in water; a direction signifying that God's covenant people are unclean in their hearts and lives. 
 
vv 1-14. 
 
Those who put their trust in outward privileges, and neglect holiness of heart and life, God will disown and put to shame, both in this world and that which is to come.   Matthew 21:43 Matthew 7:21-23

title: Jeremiah 13:4
text: Go to Euphrates--hide it there; a symbol of the humiliation of God's people by their removal to Babylon in a state of captivity.

title: Jeremiah 13:13
text: I will fill all the inhabitants of this land--with drunkenness; strong drink, which causes bewilderment and reeling, is a frequent figure for God's judgments.   Jeremiah 25:15-28 Isaiah 51:17

title: Jeremiah 13:16
text: To nations, as well as individuals, God graciously gives a day of light and mercy, which they may improve for their salvation; but if they neglect this, and harden their hearts in sin, the sun of their day will set to rise no more.   Luke 19:41-42

title: Jeremiah 13:17
text: God's faithful servants are deeply moved at the rejection of their messages, for they foresee the ruin that must follow.

title: Jeremiah 13:18
text: As unfaithful rulers and teachers are first in leading God's people into sin, so shall they be first in suffering his judgments.

title: Jeremiah 13:20
text:
Them that come from the north; the invading armies of the enemy.  Jeremiah 6:22  
 
  Where is the flock; the rulers of Jerusalem are rebuked for causing the Lord's flock to perish through their sins.  Compare  Ezekiel 34:4-6

title: Jeremiah 13:21
text: Hast taught them; the heathen nations, by seeking their aid and alliance, and imitating their idolatries.

title: Jeremiah 13:23
text: Nothing but divine grace is strong enough to break the fetters of sinful habit which has from the first held sway in the soul, and to set it free from "the law of sin" which is in the members.   Romans 7:24-25

title: Jeremiah 13:25
text: The portion of thy measures; the portion of punishment measured out to thee by me.

title: Jeremiah 14:1
text:
vv 1-6. 
 
God has all the powers of nature under his control.  When he chooses through them to punish nations for their sins, they can neither resist nor endure his hand.

title: Jeremiah 14:2
text: They are black unto the ground; they lie upon the ground in a squalid and mourning condition.

title: Jeremiah 14:6
text: They snuffed up the wind; in their endeavors to find water, the direction of which these animals ascertain by the scent.

title: Jeremiah 14:7
text:
vv 7-9. 
 
In the deepest distress God is able to hear and deliver us; and though on the ground of our own righteousness we can expect nothing but destruction, we may for his name's sake hope that he will save us, when we heartily repent of our iniquities.   Jeremiah 14:20-21

title: Jeremiah 14:8
text: A stranger--a wayfaring man; who only passes through a country without concerning himself with its interests.

title: Jeremiah 14:9
text: A man astonished--a mighty man; who has heretofore wrought wonders, but whose wisdom and strength now fail him.

title: Jeremiah 14:10
text:
vv 10-11. 
 
Both nations and individuals may go to such lengths in rebellion and iniquity, that God will hear no intercessory prayer in their behalf.  Jeremiah 15:1 I John 5:16

title: Jeremiah 14:11
text: Pray not; see note on  Jeremiah 14:22 .

title: Jeremiah 14:13
text:
vv 13-16. 
 
Men's readiness, everywhere and in all ages, to listen to those who flatter them and promise them peace and prosperity in sin, is a sad proof of the desperate deceitfulness and wickedness of the human heart.

title: Jeremiah 14:17
text:
vv 17-19. 
 
The prevalence of national iniquity fills the good man's soul with the deepest grief, both for the glory of God's name, and for the certain ruin, temporal and spiritual, which such iniquity occasions.

title: Jeremiah 14:18
text: Go about; wander into exile.

title: Jeremiah 14:21
text: Do not disgrace the throne of thy glory; by giving occasion to thine enemies to blaspheme thy name as unable to save thy people. Compare  Numbers 14:13-16 .

title: Jeremiah 14:22
text:
Can the heavens give showers? that is, of their own proper power. They are God's workmanship, and he alone can control their action. 
 
  All these things; heaven and earth. 
 
In the last four verses of this chapter the prophet speaks in the name of the pious remnant.  From this it is plain that God's command, "Pray not for this people for their good,"  Jeremiah 14:11 , was not absolute, but a declaration that, while the mass of the people continued impenitent, no prayer could avert his judgments. 
 
To sin against the Author of nature, and then look to the powers of nature for help and deliverance, is the extreme of madness and folly.

title: Jeremiah 15:1
text:
Then said the Lord; in answer to the prayer just preceding. 
 
  Stood before me; were now to stand before me, and intercede with me, as they did of old.   Exodus 32:11-14 Numbers 14:13-19 I Samuel 7:8-9  
 
  Cast them out of my sight; declare my purpose to cast them out. Compare  Isaiah 6:10 .

title: Jeremiah 15:3
text: Four kinds; of plagues: the first destroys life, and the other three devour the carcasses of the slain.

title: Jeremiah 15:4
text: Because of Manasseh;  II Kings 21:1-16

title: Jeremiah 15:5
text:
Go aside; turn from his course, as one does to visit the sick. 
 
When God is against a people for their multilplied transgressions, no human sympathy or help can deliver them.

title: Jeremiah 15:6
text:
vv 6-9. 
 
The terrible desolations which God brings upon wicked nations, are both a public manifestation of his displeasure against sin, and a solemn symbol of the utter and everlasting ruin which awaits the souls of sinners after death.   Jeremiah 15:13-14 Jeremiah 17:4 Jeremiah 17:27

title: Jeremiah 15:7
text: The gates of the land; these are put figuratively for the paths which lead out of its borders.  Here God will stand with his fan, and scatter them like chaff into exile.

title: Jeremiah 15:8
text: A spoiler at noonday; one who spoils with open and resistless force.

title: Jeremiah 15:9
text:
Her sun is gone down; her hopes are extinguished by the loss of her sons. 
 
  While it was yet day; prematurely, by their sudden death in youth.

title: Jeremiah 15:10
text:
A man of strife--of contention to the whole earth; a man with whom all men strive and contend. 
 
  I have neither lent--nor men have lent; I have been neither a hardhearted lender nor a fraudulent borrower; no wrong-doing of mine has given occasion to my fellow-men to hate me. 
 
He who faithfully delivers God's messages to sinners, must not expect to escape their reproaches and persecutions.  Experience shows that they who do not relent under God's rebukes, will seek to avenge themselves on his messengers.

title: Jeremiah 15:11
text: To entreat thee well in the time of evil; Jehovah encourages his desponding servant by a promise.  The fulfilment see in  Jeremiah 39:11-12 Jeremiah 40:1-4 .

title: Jeremiah 15:12
text:
Shall iron break the northern iron; or, "Shall iron be broken, even the northern iron?  Iron represents the warlike equipments and power of the enemy, which are invincible. 
 
God arms the executioners of his vengeance with resistless power.

title: Jeremiah 15:13
text: Thy substance; addressed to Judah.

title: Jeremiah 15:15
text:
Thou knowest; my case.  The prophet again prays for deliverance from his persecutors. 
 
vv 15-21. 
 
God promises his servants help and support in persecution, not freedom from it.  When they allow their faith and patience to be overcome by the opposition of unreasonable men, they must expect to receive from him sharp rebukes.

title: Jeremiah 15:16
text: Did eat them; received them with a willing and glad mind, as is explained in the next clause.

title: Jeremiah 15:17
text:
Because of thy hand; because thy hand was upon me; that is, thy Spirit constrained me to deliver thy messages.  Compare  Ezekiel 1:3 Ezekiel 3:22 Ezekiel 8:1 Ezekiel 33:22 . 
 
  With indignation; according to some, indignation here denotes the messages of wrath which the prophet was commissioned to deliver to the people.  Compare  Jeremiah 6:11 .  According to others, it means the indignation of the people, which was excited against him by those messages.  Thus he was made to sit solitary and oppressed with grief.

title: Jeremiah 15:18
text:
Pain--wound; his suffering for the truth's sake. 
 
  As a liar--waters that fail; it seemed to the prophet as if God failed to fulfil to him his promise of help against his foes.

title: Jeremiah 15:19
text:
If thou return; from thy impatience.  This is God's answer to the prophet. 
 
  Bring thee again; to thy prophetical work, and support thee in it. 
 
  Take forth the precious from the vile; discriminate between the righteous and the wicked.

title: Jeremiah 16:1
text: When the Jews sinned against God, he did not spare them because they were outwardly his covenant people, but visited them with his desolating judgments.  So will he deal with every branch of his visible church that proves unfaithful to its high calling; but in such a way that his chastisements shall contribute to the purification and increase of the true Israel, until all nations come to the knowledge and obedience of Christ.   Isaiah 59:16-21

title: Jeremiah 16:2
text: Shalt not take thee a wife, neither shalt thou have sons nor daughters; because the days are coming when it will be better to be childless, than to have children to perish by the sword and by famine. Compare  Matthew 24:19 Luke 23:29 .

title: Jeremiah 16:5
text:
vv 5-7. 
 
  Enter not into the house of mourning--neither shall men give them the cup of consolation; he is forbidden to mourn for the dead of his people, as a sign that God will destroy them, and the multitude of the slain will be so great that the customary funeral rites will be impossible.   Jeremiah 25:33

title: Jeremiah 16:14
text:
Behold, the days come; after the usual manner of the prophets, Jeremiah annexes to these terrible threatenings a glorious promise. 
 
  It shall no more be said; see note on  Jeremiah 3:16 .

title: Jeremiah 16:16
text: Many fishers--many hunters; the armies of their enemies.  The prophet now returns to he denunciation of God's vengeance upon his people.

title: Jeremiah 16:18
text: First; that is, before I have mercy upon them as promised.  Jeremiah 16:14-15

title: Jeremiah 16:19
text: The Gentiles shall come unto thee; with the captivity of God's covenant people, and their subsequent restoration, the prophet connects the conversion of the Gentiles.  Compare  Romans 11:12-15 .

title: Jeremiah 16:21
text: Cause them to know; cause my people to know.  By his judgments God will teach his people the folly of idolatry, and thus prepare them or deliverance and enlargement.

title: Jeremiah 17:1
text:
Upon the horns of your altars; your idolatrous altars.  The allusion is to the blood of their idol-offerings, sprinkled upon the horns of their altars, which was a fit symbol of their inveterate inward love of idolatry. 
 
vv 1-2. 
 
So deep and indelible is the handwriting of sin upon the human soul, that nothing can efface it but the power of divine grace.

title: Jeremiah 17:2
text: Groves; rather, "images of Astarte," a female deity.  These, as well as their idolatrous altars, were erected on high hills and under green trees.

title: Jeremiah 17:3
text: My mountain in the field; Jerusalem, probably so called because it stands on a mountain, with valleys on either side and a plain on the south-west.

title: Jeremiah 17:4
text: Even thyself; literally, "even in thyself," that is, through thine own fault.

title: Jeremiah 17:5
text:
vv 5-6. 
 
The original and universal sin of the human heart is departing from God and making flesh its confidence.  This idolatry of earthly things is the source of the wickedness and misery with which the earth is filled.  Jeremiah 17:13

title: Jeremiah 17:6
text: Shall not see when good cometh; shall have no share in it.

title: Jeremiah 17:7
text:
vv 7-8. 
 
They who put their trust in the living God, continually receive from him light and life and prosperity.  The heavenly joy and peace which fill their souls keep them in the way of holiness, and prevent them from turning aside after the sinful delights of the wicked.  Jeremiah 17:14

title: Jeremiah 17:8
text: Shall not see when heat cometh; shall not feel its withering power.

title: Jeremiah 17:9
text:
vv 9-10. 
 
A deep and habitual distrust of ourselves, with earnest prayer to God to show us what is in our hearts, and keep us from being deluded and destroyed by their desperate deceitfulness and wickedness--this is the beginning of all true wisdom and safety.

title: Jeremiah 17:11
text:
Sitteth on eggs, and hatcheth them not; rather, "gathereth" eggs "which she hath not laid:" thus she loses her labor; for the young birds, when hatched, forsake her. 
 
Unjust gain does not profit its owner: he must soon part with it, and go to receive the reward of his folly and wickedness.

title: Jeremiah 17:13
text: Written in the earth; in the dust of the grave; that is, be enrolled as its inhabitants.

title: Jeremiah 17:14
text: Heal me, O Lord; here begins the prophet's prayer against his persecutors.

title: Jeremiah 17:16
text:
Hastened; eagerly withdrawn myself. 
 
  From being a pastor to follow thee; literally, "from being a pastor after thee;" that is, from performing the duties of a prophet in obedience to thee.

title: Jeremiah 17:18
text: God will consider the persecution which his faithful servants receive for the truth's sake as an injury done to himself; and if it be not repented of, will punish it accordingly.

title: Jeremiah 17:19
text: The Sabbath is an indispensable bulwark of religion and good morals. Every nation that habitually profanes it must speedily sink into corruption, and become a vessel of wrath fitted for destruction.

title: Jeremiah 17:26
text: The plain; the low country along the Mediterranean, from Joppa to Gaza.  The meaning of these enumerations is, that they shall come from all parts of the land.

title: Jeremiah 18:6
text: The mightiest nations, not less than the weakest individuals, are at God's disposal, and he can prosper them or overthrow them.

title: Jeremiah 18:7
text:
vv 7-10. 
 
The sins of the fathers will not be reckoned to the nation that forsakes them, and turns to God with true obedience; and the virtues of the fathers will not profit degenerate children who refuse to imitate them.

title: Jeremiah 18:12
text:
There is no hope; our case is desperate: reformation can avail nothing.  The words express a desperate determination to persevere in sin. 
 
When men have gone so far in sin that they obstinately refuse all invitations to repentance, their measure of iniquity is full, and their destruction is at hand.   Proverbs 29:1

title: Jeremiah 18:13
text:
vv 13-17. 
 
No folly is comparable to that of forsaking the living God, who is able and willing to bestow upon us all needful good, for earthly vanities, that cannot help us, and that flatter only to deceive and ruin us.

title: Jeremiah 18:14
text:
The snow of Lebanon; that is, the cool refreshing waters which come from its melting. 
 
  From the rock of the field; from the rocky heights that overhang the adjacent fields. 
 
  That come from another place; literally, "foreign" water--water that has its origin on the remote heights of Lebanon.  Many render this difficult verse thus: "Shall the snow of Lebanon fail from the rock of the field?  Shall the cold flowing waters that come from afar be dried up?

title: Jeremiah 18:17
text: Will show them the back, and not the face; will turn my back upon their prayers; that is, refuse to hear them.

title: Jeremiah 18:18
text:
The law shall not perish--the word from the prophet; relying upon their own corrupt priests, counsellors, and prophets, they despise God's threatenings by the mouth of Jeremiah. 
 
Wicked men love those who flatter them with false promises, and hate those who faithfully labor to show them their guilt and danger.

title: Jeremiah 18:20
text: None deserve so well of their fellow men as faithful reprovers, and none are more liable to be rewarded with hatred and persecution.

title: Jeremiah 18:21
text:
vv 21-23. 
 
  Deliver up their children--deal thus with them; this is a prophetic imprecation, to be explained like those which occur in the book of Psalms.  See note on  Psalms 35:4 . 
 
They who persecute God's faithful servants for the truth's sake, array themselves against God himself, and expose themselves to his severest judgments.

title: Jeremiah 19:1
text:
Ancients; elders. 
 
vv 1-4. 
 
No image is too strong to set forth God's absolute power over wicked nations, and the irremediable ruin which he will bring upon them if they persist in provoking him to anger by their iniquities.  Jeremiah 19:10-11

title: Jeremiah 19:2
text:
Valley of the son of Hinnom; which borders Jerusalem on the south-west and south. 
 
  The east gate; or, "the pottery gate."

title: Jeremiah 19:5
text:
vv 5,12. 
 
The gods of the heathen are demons, cruel and licentious, and the services which they demand of their worshippers extinguish alike all purity and all natural affection.  The services which God requires never violate, but always purify and ennoble the natural affections.

title: Jeremiah 19:6
text: Tophet; this seems to have been the name of that part of the valley where human sacrifices were offered.

title: Jeremiah 20:2
text:
The stocks; a wooden frame in which the hands, feet, and neck were confined, and thus the body kept in a bent and painful position. 
 
  High gate; upper gate. 
 
It is very common with wicked men to show their enmity to God's messages by persecuting those who deliver them.

title: Jeremiah 20:4
text: vv 4-5. God's threatened wrath upon sinners can be averted only by repentance and amendment.  To hate and maltreat his servants, who forewarn them of coming judgments, will only involve them in deeper guilt and ruin.

title: Jeremiah 20:6
text: The maglignant persecutors of God's people generally come to an ignominious and miserable end.

title: Jeremiah 20:7
text:
Deceived me; persuaded me to undertake the prophetical office, and thus brought upon me such contempt and suffering as I did not foresee. These words are inconsiderate and impatient: God had fully forewarned him at the beginning ofhis ministry of the persecution which he should encounter. 
 
  Stronger than I, and hast prevailed; how, is explained in  Jeremiah 20:9 . 
 
vv 7-8. 
 
To endure derision and abuse for the truth's sake, with few or none to countenance and encourage us, is a sore trial.  Under its pressure the best of men are liable to lose their patience, and indulge in unbecoming complaints concerning God's providence.

title: Jeremiah 20:9
text: To withhold any part of God's counsel through fear of man causes a servant of God deep distress, and he cannot rest till he has faithfully declared it all, whether men will hear or whether they will forbear.

title: Jeremiah 20:10
text:
Report; inform against him to the rulers.   Jeremiah 36:11-26  
 
A common artifice of persecutors is, to entice the righteous from the path of duty, that they may thus prevail against them.

title: Jeremiah 20:11
text:
vv 11-13. 
 
In the deepest distress God's faithful servants have an almighty Helper ever at hand, who will not fail in due time to deliver them and overthrow their adversaries.

title: Jeremiah 20:14
text:
vv 14-18. 
 
  Cursed be the day--consumed with shame; a very remarkable transition from faith and thanksgiving to unbelief and irrational passion, such as is not uncommon in the experience of even eminent believers, and which they only can fully understand who have been tried as was the prophet for the truth's sake. 
 
To curse the day of our birth on account of any outward trials, is the extreme of rashness and folly.  Yet it is a sin from which nothing but abundant supplies of divine grace can preserve even good men, in the hour of strong temptation.   Job 3:1

title: Jeremiah 21:1
text: Zedekiah; the last king of Judah.  This was during the final siege of the city by Nebuchadnezzar, near the close of his reign.

title: Jeremiah 21:2
text: God's wondrous works in days past afford no ground of encouragement to wicked and corrupt rulers in he visible church, since the effect of his interposition in her behalf must be not their salvation, but their destruction.

title: Jeremiah 21:3
text: God's servants must return to those who consult them, of whatever rank or station, not such answers as will be pleasing to them, but such as are in accordance with truth.  To those who persist in sin there can be no message of peace.   II Chronicles 18:7

title: Jeremiah 21:8
text:
vv 8-10. 
 
The only path of safety for nations or individuals lies in submission to God's declared will, however humbling it may be to their pride.

title: Jeremiah 21:12
text:
In the morning; every morning; that is, promptly and habitually. The morning was the regular time for the administration of justice. 
 
For rulers and people there is but one law--righteousness and prosperity, or wickedness and ruin.

title: Jeremiah 21:13
text:
O inhabitant of the valley--rock of the plain; the same as "my mountain in the field,"  Jeremiah 17:3 . 
 
  Shall come down; from the higher hills in the vicinity, where the armies of the enemy were encamped.

title: Jeremiah 22:1
text: According to some, the prophet addressed the words of this chapter to Zedekiah, and embodied in them his former predictions concerning Shallum, Jehoiakim, and Coniah.  Thus the denunciation in hte last verse would refer to Zedekiah.  But we may better refer the prophecy, at least as far as verse 19, to the reign of Jehoiakim; what follows concerning Coniah being either spoken in anticipation of his disastrous reign, or written during it at a later date.

title: Jeremiah 22:6
text:
Gilead--the head of Lebanon; Gilead was the mountainous region on the east of Jordan, south of the river Jabbok.  Like Lebanon it was celebrated for its majesty and beauty.  The meaning is, that however precious to God is the royal house of David, with the kingdom intrusted to it, God will make both utterly desolate for their sins. 
 
No outward nearness or sacredness of relation to God will screen men from his wrath when they persist in trampling under foot his laws.  Romans 2:1-11

title: Jeremiah 22:8
text:
vv 8-9. 
 
As God has distinguished his covenant people above all nations of the earth by his wonderful interpositions in their behalf, so will he make their punishment in like manner conspicuous when they sin against him, that the inhabitants of the world may see it and fear before him.

title: Jeremiah 22:10
text:
For the dead; the reference seems to be to Josiah. 
 
  Him that goeth away; that is, Shallum.   Jeremiah 22:11  
 
The dead are beyond the reach of our prayers and sympathies, and immoderate grief for them is forbidden by the spirit of true religion; the living who are in distress may rather claim our tears and supplications in their behalf.

title: Jeremiah 22:11
text:
Shallum; generally supposed to have been the same as Jehoahaz, whom Pharaoh-Necho carried captive into Egypt, after a reign of three months.   II Kings 23:31-34 II Chronicles 36:1-4   He was a younger brother, but "the people of the land" preferred him before Jehoiakim.  His name was probably changed upon his accession to the throne, as was that of Jehoiakim,  II Chronicles 36:4 ; and Zedekiah,  II Kings 24:17 . 
 
God will not spare wicked children for the piety of their fathers.  Ezekiel 18:10-13

title: Jeremiah 22:13
text:
That buildeth his house by unrighteousness; the reference is to Jehoiakim, the son of Josiah and successor of Jehoahaz.  That the reigning monarch is addressed is plain, from  Jeremiah 22:15 .  He was an avaricious, luxurious, and unrighteous king, who oppressed and plundered the people for his own aggrandizement. 
 
vv 13-19. 
 
Rulers who rob and oppress the people for their own aggrandizement, are alike odious to God and man, and they generally come to an ignominious end, with none to mourn for them or honor them in death.

title: Jeremiah 22:18
text:
For him; that is, for him and the members of his family, as the words, "Ah, sister," show. 
 
  Ah, sister; this probably refers to his queen, who was afterwards carried captive to Babylon with Jehoiachin her son.   II Kings 24:12

title: Jeremiah 22:19
text:
Buried with the burial of an ass; that is, shall be left unburied.  Jeremiah 36:30  
 
  Drawn and cast forth; that is, which is drawn and cast forth, the words referring to the body of the ass, not to Jehoiakim, who probably died in Babylon.   II Chronicles 36:6

title: Jeremiah 22:20
text:
Go up to Lebanon--in Bashon; the address is to "the daughter of Zion."  Let her cry from the mountain-tops, that all may hear her wailings. 
 
  From the passages; either, from the passages that lead out of the land to Babylon; or better, "from Abarim," a mountainous ridge east of the lower Jordan and the Dead sea.   Numbers 27:12 Deuteronomy 32:49  
 
  Thy lovers; the foreign nations to whom thou trustedst for help.

title: Jeremiah 22:22
text: The alliances of God's ancient people with their heathen neighbors ended in disappointment and ruin; so will it ever be with those who forsake the living God for earthly confidences.

title: Jeremiah 22:23
text:
Inhabitant of Lebanon--makest thy nest in the cedars; a double reference to the beauty of mount Zion, which rivalled that of Lebanon; and to the palaces built with cedar-wood from Lebanon, that adorned its heights. 
 
  How gracious; rather, "how much to be commiserated."

title: Jeremiah 22:24
text: Coniah; elsewhere called Jeconiah,  I Chronicles 3:16 ; and Jehoiachin,  II Kings 24:8 II Chronicles 36:8-9 .

title: Jeremiah 22:28
text:
Idol; rather, "earthen vessel."  The question of the prophet expresses astonishment at his fate. 
 
  Wherefore are they cast out; the prophet leaves the people to infer the answer.

title: Jeremiah 22:29
text: O earth, earth, earth; he solemnly calls upon the earth to witness his prediction.  Compare De 32.1; Isa 1.2.

title: Jeremiah 22:30
text:
This man; Coniah. 
 
  Childless; not in the absolute sense, for he had children,  I Chronicles 3:17-18 , one of whom is named in our Lord's genealogy,  Matthew 1:12 , and this is implied in the words following: "No man of his seed shall prosper."  But he was childless in the sense immediately explained, that none of his seed should occupy the throne of David in Jerusalem.  Zedekiah, who reigned after him, was his brother.  The prophet her refers to the earthly throne of David. 
 
The earthly kingdom of David began with righteous rulers, and gained strength and glory by obedience to God's laws; it was destroyed by wicked and corrupt rulers, leading a wicked and corrupt people in iniquity and rebellion against God.  Herein is it set forth as an example to all nations.

title: Jeremiah 23:1
text:
Pastors; Jewish rulers and teachers.  Compare  Ezekiel 34:1-31 , with which this passage strikingly agrees. 
 
vv 1-4. 
 
The Lord knows how to deliver his flock out of the hand of unfaithful pastors, while he punishes them for their pride and selfishness.

title: Jeremiah 23:5
text:
A righteous Branch--a King; the Messiah.  See  Isaiah 4:2 , and note. 
 
The hope and strength and salvation of the church are in the Lord Jesus Christ, "that great Shepherd of the sheep," whom God has raised up to her according to his ancient promise.  All power in heaven and earth is in his hands, and he will use it for the overthrow of all her enemies and her perpetual enlargement from age to age.

title: Jeremiah 23:6
text: Christ is named "the LORD OUR RIGHTEOUSNESS," because he alone gives justifying righteousness to us sinners, and thus restores us to peace with God.   Romans 5:1

title: Jeremiah 23:7
text:
vv 7-8. 
 
  They shall no more say--dwell in their own land; compare  Jeremiah 3:16 , and note.  The return of the Jews from Babylon was an earnest of the higher fulfilment of this prophecy, which is reserved for "the last days."  Compare  Ezekiel 34:1-31 , throughout. 
 
However great the glory of past deliverances which God has vouchsafed to his people, a brighter glory remains for the latter days of their prosperity and triumph.

title: Jeremiah 23:9
text:
Is broken; in  Jeremiah 23:3 , the prophet had passed from threatenings to promises; he now returns from promises to threatenings. This is the usual manner of the prophets. Compare  Isaiah 4:1-2 Isaiah 59:15-16 Amos 9:10-11 Zephaniah 3:7-8 . 
 
  Because of the Lord--the words of his holiness; that is, of his messages of wrath committed to me; these fill the prophet's mind with awe.

title: Jeremiah 23:10
text: Swearing; that is, false swearing.  But we may better render, "because of the curse;" that is, the divine curse.

title: Jeremiah 23:13
text:
In Baal; in Baal's name. 
 
vv 13-14. 
 
When the spiritual guides of a people are wicked, and teachers of falsehood, the whole community sinks rapidly into corruption and ruin.

title: Jeremiah 23:15
text: Since none do so much as false teachers to strengthen the hands of evil-doers, none shall receive such punishment at God's hand.

title: Jeremiah 23:17
text: False teachers may be known by these two marks: their lives are corrupt, and their doctrines flatter men with the hope of impunity and prosperity in sin.   Matthew 7:15-16

title: Jeremiah 23:18
text:
Who; who among these false prophets. 
 
  Hath stood in the counsel of the Lord; hath been admitted to his secret counsel, so as to hear his words and understand his will.

title: Jeremiah 23:20
text:
In the latter days; when the promises of the false prophets have failed, and the threatenings of the true prophets have been fulfilled. 
 
  Shall consider it; your folly in hearkening to lies.

title: Jeremiah 23:22
text: When God's ministers as a body are faithful to their high office, his church is in a healthful condition, and abounding in the fruits of holiness.

title: Jeremiah 23:23
text:
A God at hand; a God who can, like men, be present only in one place at a time, and see and act there only? 
 
vv 23-24. 
 
To God's omnipresence there can be no distance; wherever we are, his omnipotence and omniscience compass us on every side.

title: Jeremiah 23:28
text:
A dream; a true dream, a revelation received from God in a dream. 
 
  Let him tell a dream; as much as to say, Let him only that has received a dream from me tell it. 
 
  What is the chaff to the wheat? or, "What has the chaff to do with the wheat?"  Why mingle human devices with my revelations? 
 
It should be the chief aim of God's messengers to declare his word faithfully, without any admixture of human devices.

title: Jeremiah 23:29
text:
A fire--a hammer; God contrasts the efficacy of his word with the powerlessness of false revelations. 
 
God's truth, when faithfully preached and applied by his Spirit to men's hearts and consciences, has a divine efficacy, which distinguished it from all human systems of religion.  These last are powerless for convincing men of sin and turning them to righteousness.

title: Jeremiah 23:30
text: Steal my words every one from his neighbor; the reference seems to be to pretended prophets, who borrowed from their neighbors, the true prophets, certain forms and phrases, which they mixed with their own vain imaginings.

title: Jeremiah 23:33
text:
What is the burden of the Lord? in the original Hebrew, the same word means both "burden" and "oracle."  The prophet's oracles were mainly occupied with denunciations of God's wrath, which he laid upon the people as a heavy burden.  Hence they asked him, "What is the burden of the Lord?"  What load of punishment does he next lay upon us? 
 
  What burden? their question was scoffingly asked; God will answer it earnestly, with a true burden. 
 
vv 33-40. 
 
They who deride God's threatenings will soon be made to feel in their own persons their irresistible and terrible power.

title: Jeremiah 23:36
text:
Shall ye mention no more; because of the derision to which this form, "The burden of the Lord," had been exposed, God forbids the people its use. 
 
  Every man's word shall be his burden; the scoffing use of these words, "The burden of the Lord," shall bring upon every one who employs them a burden of divine wrath.

title: Jeremiah 24:1
text: The true character of men cannot always be determined by God's outward dealings with them.  The heaviest trials often prove the occasion of great prosperity, spiritual and temporal, and exemption from them to be a heavy judgment.

title: Jeremiah 24:2
text: Very good figs--very naughty figs; the two baskets of figs represent the two classes of Jews, in respect to both condition and character. Nebuchadnezzar took away the better class of the people. Those whom he left were not merely the poorer, but the baser sort.  Isaiah 3:1-7 , compared with  II Kings 24:14 Jeremiah 40:7 .  Moreover, God raised up for the captives in Babylon eminent prophets, as Daniel and Ezekiel, whose labors were greatly blessed; so that at the expiration of their captivity, they returned to Judea thoroughly purified from idolatry.  Those who remained in the land were, on the contrary, abandoned to wickedness, anarchy, and misery, as is manifest from Jeremiah's account of their proceedings.   Jeremiah 40:1-44:30

title: Jeremiah 25:1
text: The fourth year of Jehoiakim--the first year of Nebuchadrezzar; the first year of Nebuchadnezzar seems to have corresponded partly with the third and partly with the fourth year of Jehoiakim. Compare  Daniel 1:1 . This prophecy was delivered earlier than that recorded in the preceding chapter, the arrangement of the writings of Jeremiah, here and elsewhere, not preserving the chronological order.

title: Jeremiah 25:8
text:
vv 8,11. 
 
Though God's judgments be long delayed, they will come at last upon the incorrigibly impenitent, and their severity will be in proportion to the exhortations and warnings that have been despised.

title: Jeremiah 25:9
text: These nations round about; the nations afterwards enumerated,  Jeremiah 25:19-26 .

title: Jeremiah 25:10
text: The sound of the millstones; the millstones of the hand-mill, in which the people of the East daily grind their meal.

title: Jeremiah 25:11
text: Seventy years; generally reckoned from the first invasion of the land by Nebuchadnezzar during the reign of Jehoiakim, when the process of transportation to Babylon began.

title: Jeremiah 25:12
text: However sore the chastisement which God inflicts upon his people, he remembers them at the appointed time in mercy; and their cruel and relentless persecutors he destroys.

title: Jeremiah 25:13
text: This book--against all the nations; "this book" seems to refer to the whole connection of Jeremiah's writings.  The more distinguished prophecies "against all the nations" now stand in the last part of the book.  We must suppose either that they were originally written at an earlier date, or, what is more probable, that the present clause was added in arranging the whole volume.

title: Jeremiah 25:15
text:
The wine-cup of this fury; here, as often elsewhere, God's wrath is compared to an intoxicating wine-cup, which makes those who drink it mad, and causes them to stagger and fall.  Psalms 75:8 Isaiah 51:21-23   Zechariah 12:2  
 
vv 15-28, 30-33. 
 
God's power over the human family is unlimited; it is as easy for him to send forth desolating calamities from nation to nation over all the earth, as to punish the weakest transgressor of his laws.

title: Jeremiah 25:16
text: Be moved; reel.

title: Jeremiah 25:17
text: Then took I the cup; this was plainly done only in prophetic vision.  He makes the nations to drink by announcing God's wrath that is coming upon them.

title: Jeremiah 25:18
text:
vv 18-26. 
 
  Jerusalem--all the kings of the Medes; all these nations were to be destroyed by Nebuchadnezzar. 
 
  The mingled people; probably here, as in  Ezekiel 30:5 , the mixed mass of foreigners serving the Egyptians. 
 
  Uz; probably situated in the northern part of Arabia. 
 
  The isles--beyond the sea; the western islands of the Mediterranean, with the adjacent coasts. 
 
Dedan, and Tema, and Buz; in the northern part of Arabia. 
 
  All--in the utmost corners; see note on  Jeremiah 9:26 . 
 
  Zimri; an unknown tribe, probably lying in the direction of Persia and Media. 
 
  Elam; Persia. 
 
  The Medes; northeast of Persia, and south and west of the Captain. 
 
  All the kings of the north; the Scythian tribes north of the Euxine and Black sea. 
 
  All the kingdoms of the world; in a general sense.  Compare  Luke 2:1 . 
 
  Sheshach; a name for Babylon.   Jeremiah 51:41   After God has used the king of Babylon as the minister of his wrath upon these nations, he shall in turn be destroyed.  Compare what is said of Assyria,  Isaiah 10:12 .

title: Jeremiah 25:29
text: The judgments which God brings upon his offending people are a solemn warning to the wicked of the more terrible vengeance which will one day fall upon them.   I Peter 4:17-18

title: Jeremiah 25:31
text: A noise shall come; the tumult of warlike hosts, under the marshalling of Jehovah.  Compare  Isaiah 13:4 .

title: Jeremiah 25:34
text:
Shepherds--principal of the flock; the nobles and rulers of the nations. 
 
  Are accomplished; have fully come.   Luke 2:6  
 
  Like a pleasant vessel; as a costly vessel falls and is dashed in pieces. 
 
vv 34-38. 
 
It is a righteous rule of divine Providence, that wicked leaders of the people, who are first in crime, should be first also in suffering, when he punishes nations for their sins.

title: Jeremiah 25:36
text: Spoiled their pasture; destroyed their land and people.

title: Jeremiah 25:37
text: Cut down; desolated.

title: Jeremiah 25:38
text: He hath forsaken; Jehovah, as the leader of the conquering hosts, who is here compared to a lion.   Jeremiah 25:30 .

title: Jeremiah 26:6
text: Like Shiloh; see note on  Jeremiah 7:12 .

title: Jeremiah 26:11
text: God's faithful servants generally receive the bitterest persecution from false and corrupt religious teachers.

title: Jeremiah 26:14
text: The true messenger of God will commit his cause to his divine Master, and prefer death rather than unfaithfulness.

title: Jeremiah 26:15
text: God regards the injury which his servants receive for the truth's sake as done to himself, and he will punish it accordingly.

title: Jeremiah 26:16
text:
vv 16-19. 
 
True nobleness of character is shown by listening to faithful reproofs and profiting by them; to hate and persecute those who administer them betrays equal baseness and wickedness.

title: Jeremiah 26:18
text: Zion shall be ploughed;  Micah 3:1

title: Jeremiah 26:19
text: Did Hezekiah--put him at all to death? this case is adduced by the princes as an argument why the king should spare Jeremiah.

title: Jeremiah 26:20
text:
Urijah; this case is adduced by the prophet to show the disposition of Jehoiakim, and the danger to which he was exposed. 
 
vv 20-23. 
 
To show fear of wicked men who are high in office and power, is oftentimes the most certain way to give them the mastery over us.

title: Jeremiah 26:24
text: It is easy for God to raise up friends and protectors for the defenceless, and he will do so for those who put their trust in him, as far as their good and the interests of his cause demand it.

title: Jeremiah 27:1
text:
Jehoiakim; many suppose that this should read, "Zedekiah," as in  Jeremiah 27:3 Jeremiah 27:12 Jeremiah 27:20 Jeremiah 28:1  
 
For the accomplishment of his own ends, God sometimes intrusts wicked and impious rulers with great power and authority; and then all resistance on the part of the neighboring nations proves vain.  But when he has fulfilled his purposes by them, he humbles them as easily as he had before exalted them.  Compare  Jeremiah 18:6-10 Daniel 7:1-8:27

title: Jeremiah 27:19
text: The pillars--the bases; see  I Kings 7:15 I Kings 7:21 I Kings 7:23 I Kings 7:27 II Chronicles 2:1-18 II Chronicles 2:12 II Chronicles 2:14 .

title: Jeremiah 28:2
text: It is a common custom of false teachers to flatter men with the assurance of impunity in the practice of sin.

title: Jeremiah 28:6
text: God's servants should manifest a tender and compassionate spirit, such as shall make it manifest to all that they take no delight in the messages of wrath which they deliver to the people in his name, and that it is the earnest desire of their hearts that by repentance and reformation the fulfilment of these threatenings may be averted.

title: Jeremiah 28:8
text: Of war--of pestilence; the prediction of God's approaching judgments, with the view of bringing the people to repentance, was one of the signs of a true prophet; while the false prophets occupied themselves with quieting the consciences of the people in the practice of sin.

title: Jeremiah 28:9
text:
Shall come to pass; see  Deuteronomy 18:22 . 
 
The awful destruction of the wicked will soon make manifest the folly of those who have flattered them with the hope of peace and safety in a course of iniquity.

title: Jeremiah 28:13
text:
For them; in their stead.  By encouraging the people in sin, Hananiah is making for them iron instead of wooden yokes; that is, aggravating the severity of their bondage. 
 
vv 13-17. 
 
God will not accommodate the course of his government to the wishes of corrupt rulers and false prophets who strengthen their hands in wickedness, but will destroy both together.

title: Jeremiah 29:5
text:
Build ye houses; the expectation of a speedy restoration to their own land would have prevented the captives from settling themselves in their new abode, and thus have proved an injury to them. 
 
vv 5-6. 
 
The true teacher will inculcate upon me cheerful submission under the afflictive dispensations of God's providence and the diligent performance of duty.  Thus present suffering will be greatly mitigated, and the way be prepared for future enlargement and deliverance.

title: Jeremiah 29:7
text: Since civil government is an ordinance of God, we are bound to seek the peace and welfare of the nation in which God's providence in any way appoints our residence, and to yield a willing obedience to all its laws, except only when they command what God forbids.  Romans 13:1 Acts 28:31

title: Jeremiah 29:8
text:
vv 8-9. 
 
The way of those who prophesy lies has always been, first to quiet men's consciences in sin until they fall into trouble, and then to encourage them to seek deliverance from it in some other way than by repentance and submission to God's will.

title: Jeremiah 29:10
text: If we bear with patience and meekness the trials which God lays upon us, he will, at the appointed time, grant us a glorious deliverance from them.

title: Jeremiah 29:11
text: An expected end; that happy issue which is the object of your hopes.

title: Jeremiah 29:13
text: Heartiness and sincerity in seeking God insure a gracious answer.

title: Jeremiah 29:15
text:
Prophets in Babylon; these were the false prophets who promised the captives a speedy return. 
 
vv 15-19. 
 
They who desire to be flattered in rebellion against God, will find false prophets ready to flatter them; but it will only be for their utter and irremediable ruin.

title: Jeremiah 29:22
text: None do so much as false teachers to corrupt and ruin a nation; and against none does God threaten such severe judgments.  Jeremiah 29:30-32

title: Jeremiah 29:23
text: Lying words in doctrine, and villany in practice, generally go together, as in the case of Ahab and Zedekiah.

title: Jeremiah 29:24
text: Thus shalt thou also speak; this prophecy was evidently delivered after the return of Zedekiah's messengers from Babylon.

title: Jeremiah 30:2
text:
All the words that I have spoken unto thee; namely, the words beginning with the fourth verse, and extending through this and the following chapter. 
 
  In a book; for the instruction and encouragement of those future ages to which they refer.

title: Jeremiah 30:3
text:
I will bring again the captivity of my people; we are to understand here, as in other like predictions, the restoration from the Babylonish captivity, with all the higher deliverances that follow it to the end of time, and of which it is both an earnest and a pledge.  See note on  Isaiah 55:12 . 
 
Since every chastisement which God sends upon his covenant people is designed not for their destruction, but their purification, he will certainly deliver them from it, and make it in the end conducive to their increase and prosperity.   Jeremiah 30:10-11

title: Jeremiah 30:5
text: A voice of trembling; in Jacob.  Compare  Isaiah 30:7 .

title: Jeremiah 30:7
text:
The time of Jacob's trouble; compare  Daniel 12:1 .  The great deliverances of God's church have been effected in "troublous times." So it was at the restoration from the Babylonish captivity, as we learn from the books of Ezra and Nehemiah; and the Scriptures frequently intimate that her final deliverance shall be connected with such times.  Isaiah 29:7-8 Matthew 24:21 Revelation of John 16:13 Revelation of John 19:19  
 
The seasons of sharpest conflict to Zion have been, in a peculiar sense, those of her spiritual enlargement and deliverance.

title: Jeremiah 30:12
text:
Thy bruise--wound; the calamities which thy sins have brought upon thee. 
 
vv 12-17. 
 
God's visible church has more than once been in the condition of an outcast; within diseased by sin and error, and without despised and trodden under foot by her enemies.  But for the glory of his own name he has interposed in her behalf, bound up her wounds, and restored her to spiritual health and strength.

title: Jeremiah 30:14
text: Thy lovers; the gentile nations, to whose alliance the Jews trusted for salvation.

title: Jeremiah 30:16
text: Therefore; because the end which I have had in view in afflicting thee for they sins was thy purification, not thy destruction.  The prophets often employ this word in passing from threatenings of present evil to promises of future good.

title: Jeremiah 30:18
text:
Heap; or, "hill." 
 
  Remain after the manner thereof; more exactly, "be inhibited after its manner;" that is, its former manner. 
 
vv 18-24. 
 
The future overthrow of the wicked is as certain as the perpetual increase and joy of God's people.

title: Jeremiah 30:21
text:
Their nobles; in the Hebrew, "their noble," or, "their glorious one," in the singular number, like the word that follows.  The reference is to the Messiah, as in the remainder of the verse, and to the Jewish rulers after the captivity only so far as their office, like that of David before the captivity, was typical of Christ's reign. 
 
  Of themselves; of their own nation, and not of foreign conquerors. This promise had only a partial and limited fulfilment in the restoration of the Jewish state after the captivity.  Its complete fulfilment is in Christ, the son of David, whom God has made Head over all things to the church.  He in an emphatic sense draws near to God as the one Mediator between God and man. 
 
  Who is this; an expression of admiring wonder.  Compare  Isaiah 60:8 . 
 
  Engaged his heart; literally, "pledged his heart."  These words are peculiarly applicable to the Redeemer, who has solemnly given himself to the work of intercession for men, and who continually approaches God in their behalf.   Hebrews 7:25

title: Jeremiah 30:23
text: The whirlwind--goeth forth; the deliverance of Zion is here as elsewhere connected with desolating judgments upon the wicked within and without her pale.

title: Jeremiah 31:1
text: All the families of Israel; all its tribes, whose restoration and conversion the prophets often foretell.   Ezekiel 37:1-28

title: Jeremiah 31:2
text: Which were left of the sword; whom the sword had spared.

title: Jeremiah 31:3
text: Our assurance of the perpetuity of God's church, and her continued increase from age to age, rests not on the stability of human counsels, but on God's everlasting love for her.  What he has undertaken, self-moved, for the manifestation of his own glory, he will carry on to perfection.

title: Jeremiah 31:6
text: Let us go up to Zion; these words predict the healing of the great schism between Judah and Israel.  Compare  I Kings 12:26-28 .

title: Jeremiah 31:9
text:
By the rivers of waters; compare  Isaiah 35:6-7 Revelation of John 7:17 . 
 
vv 9-14. 
 
When God's people repent of their sins, and seek his face with weeping and supplication, he will turn their tears to songs of joy.  Their condition is never so desperate that he cannot with infinite ease restore to them more than their former prosperity, and make their souls, by his grace, like a watered garden full of the fruits of righteousness.

title: Jeremiah 31:15
text:
Ramah--Rachel weeping; Rachel was "buried in the way to Ephrath, which is Bethlehem," as Jacob journeyed from the north.  That her grave was near Ramah, which lay a few miles north of Bethlehem, is plain from  I Samuel 10:2 .  Here she is represented, by a beautiful figure, as weeping from her tomb over her lost children. The words apply to any desolation of that region, and are peculiarly applicable to that which Herod made by the slaughter of the children in Bethlehem and its borders.   Matthew 2:16-18  
 
vv 15-17. 
 
Great and bitter bereavements often befall the church, and make her like a tender mother weeping for her lost children.  But God restores to her a spiritual offspring more abundant than the former, and thus her youth and vigor are renewed from age to age.   Psalms 22:30 Psalms 110:3   Isaiah 49:20-21 Isaiah 53:10-11

title: Jeremiah 31:18
text:
Ephraim; that is, Israel, so named from one of the principal tribes. 
 
vv 18-19. 
 
In the beginning divine chastisements commonly stir up the rebellion and opposition of the human heart; but in God's children, their final effect is to produce deep humiliation and self-abasement before him. This is the signal that they have accomplished their object and will be speedily removed.

title: Jeremiah 31:19
text:
After that I was turned; turned by God's grace from rebellion to obedience. 
 
  I repented; though conversion begins in repentance, and is always effected by God's grace, the deepest repentance comes after it.

title: Jeremiah 31:20
text: In the severest trials which God sends upon his children, he feels a fatherly compassion for them; he afflicts them for their profit, that they may be partakers of his holiness, and will in due time grant them a merciful deliverance.

title: Jeremiah 31:21
text: Waymarks; to mark out the road that leads from captivity home again.

title: Jeremiah 31:22
text:
Go about; wander about in the service of false gods. 
 
  A woman shall compass a man; commonly interpreted of our Lord's miraculous conception in the womb of the virgin Mary; and this agrees well with the context, for his incarnation was the highest pledge that God could give the church of his love for her, and his purpose to redeem her from the power of her enemies.

title: Jeremiah 31:26
text:
Awaked; from prophetic vision. 
 
  Beheld; considered the vision. 
 
  My sleep; that is, what was revealed to me in my sleep. 
 
God's precious promises concerning Zion have ever been the support and consolation of all her true children.

title: Jeremiah 31:28
text: God breaks down the kingdom of Satan to destroy it for ever; but when he breaks down the walls of Zion, it is that he may afterwards build them again of wider dimensions and in a nobler form.   Jeremiah 31:38-40

title: Jeremiah 31:31
text:
A new covenant; the gospel economy in contrast with the Mosaic. This new covenant is the carrying out of the original covenant made with Abraham.  Compare  Jeremiah 32:38-40 Ezekiel 37:24-28 Hebrews 8:8-13 . 
 
vv 31-34. 
 
The new covenant made by God in Christ is spiritual in its nature, and the evidence of our personal interest in it is to be sought, not in our outward relations, but in the inward state of our affections.  If God's law be written in our hearts, then its blessings are ours, but not otherwise.

title: Jeremiah 31:35
text:
vv 35-37. 
 
Nothing is so stable as God's promises.  The ordinances of heaven he established, and he can remove them.  But his word nothing can remove. It stands fast for ever and ever.

title: Jeremiah 31:37
text: Can be measured--searched out--I will also cast off; God's faithfulness to his covenant engagements is as infinite as his works.

title: Jeremiah 31:38
text: From the tower of Hananeel; the site of this, and of most of the other places named in connection with it, is uncertain.  But the general meaning is, that Jerusalem shall be greatly enlarged.  We may well believe that this shall be literally fulfilled when "all Israel shall be saved;" yet the enlarging of the literal Jerusalem must still be a sign of the enlargement of the church universal.

title: Jeremiah 32:1
text:
The tenth year of Zedekiah; within about a year of the final capture of the city.   Jeremiah 39:2  
 
vv 1-15. 
 
The purchase which Jeremiah made of Hanameel was a pledge from God to his covenant people, that though for a season excluded from the land of Canaan, they should yet be restored to the possession of it; so all the present partial and limited victories which God grants to his church over the kingdom of Satan, are earnests and pledges of the universal victory that is reserved for her in coming ages.

title: Jeremiah 32:2
text: Shut up in the court of the prison; see  Jeremiah 37:21 Jeremiah 38:28 .

title: Jeremiah 32:5
text:
There shall he be; that is, as a captive. 
 
  I visit him; see note on  Jeremiah 34:5 .

title: Jeremiah 32:7
text: The right of redemption is thine; the lands of the Israelites were inalienable; when a man had occasion to sell a field, his nearest kinsman had the right of purchasing it, and it returned to its former owner of his children at the year of jubilee.   Leviticus 25:34

title: Jeremiah 32:11
text: Sealed--open; two evidences of sale were prepared: the one sealed and carefully laid up for future use, in case of doubt or litigation; the other a copy not sealed and left open, that its contents might at any time be read.

title: Jeremiah 32:15
text: Shall be possessed again; that is, by the Jews in the way of regular sale and purchase, as was explained in  Jeremiah 32:44 .  This implied the peaceable repossession of their own land, from which Nebuchadnezzar was about to carry them into captivity.

title: Jeremiah 32:25
text:
For the city is given; rather, "and yet the city is given."  The present condition of affairs seems to the prophet inconsistent with God's promise. 
 
We should not judge of the prospects of God's cause by present appearances, but by his promises.  The darkest nights of the church's affliction lead to a glorious dawn.

title: Jeremiah 32:26
text:
vv 26-44. 
 
God knows how to pour out his wrath upon his visible church for her sins in such a manner that her present overthrow shall be the means of her purification and renovation, and the introduction of a new and more glorious era in her history.   Jeremiah 33:1-14

title: Jeremiah 32:33
text: Turned unto me the back, and not the face; gone away from me instead of coming to me.

title: Jeremiah 32:36
text: Ye say, It shall be delivered into the hand of the king of Babylon; the threatened delivery of Jerusalem into the hand of Nebuchadnezzar seemed to the people to be the extinction of all their hopes for the future.  God assures them that, though this shall take place, there shall be a future restoration.

title: Jeremiah 32:44
text: Buy fields--subscribe evidences; these words, as also  Jeremiah 32:15 , explain the import of the symbolic transaction between Jeremiah and Hanameel in  Jeremiah 32:6-14 .  It was in fact a prophecy in the shape of a symbol.

title: Jeremiah 33:1
text: To the Old Testament church, the promise of a coming Saviour was the highest possible pledge that the gates of hell should never prevail against her.  She could not perish, because of her was to come the Redeemer of men.  The victory gained by Christ over the prince of this world, and his exaltation to the right hand of God, are, in like manner, a perfect pledge to the Christian church that God will make her triumphant over all opposition.  Sooner shall heaven and earth pass away than Christ, to whom the Father has given all power in heaven and earth, fail of subduing all things to himself.   I Corinthians 15:24-26

title: Jeremiah 33:2
text: The maker thereof--that formed it; the words "thereof" and "it" seem to refer to God's gracious purpose concerning his covenant people that is revealed in the present chapter.

title: Jeremiah 33:5
text: To fill them; the houses mentioned in  Jeremiah 33:4 .

title: Jeremiah 33:6
text: I will bring it health and cure; God will not abate his present judgments upon Jerusalem, but he gives the gracious assurance of a future restoration.

title: Jeremiah 33:15
text: The Branch--unto David; the Messiah.  Compare  Isaiah 11:1 .

title: Jeremiah 33:17
text: David shall never want a man; literally, "there shall not be cut off to David a man;" that is, royal line shall not become extinct so that his kingdom can never be restored and perpetuated in his offspring.  For their chastisement, God prohibited David's children from the exercise of the kingly office through a long period of time,  II Samuel 7:14 ; but the kingdom itself was reserved for Christ the son of David.   Luke 1:32-33   Compare  Jeremiah 33:26 .

title: Jeremiah 33:18
text: Neither shall the priests the Levites want a man; after a temporary suspension, the Levitical priesthood was restored and continued till it was superseded by the perfect priesthood of Christ, which it typified.   Hebrews 7:1-3 Hebrews 7:11-12 Hebrews 7:15-16

title: Jeremiah 33:24
text:
This people; probably the Chaldeans, who were besieging the city. 
 
  The two families; Judah and Israel.

title: Jeremiah 34:1
text:
vv 1-7. 
 
They who persist in acting contrary to God's declared will, involve themselves in irremediable ruin.

title: Jeremiah 34:5
text: From a comparison of this verse with  Jeremiah 32:5 , it appears that Zedekiah, though never restored to his throne, was after some time released from close confinement, and treated with the honor due to his former dignity.  The same was true of Jehoiachin.   II Kings 25:27-30

title: Jeremiah 34:7
text: Lachish--Azekah; cities in the plain country of Judah, south-west of Jerusalem.

title: Jeremiah 34:8
text: To proclaim liberty unto them; that is, to the Hebrew man-servants and maid-servants, in compliance with the law of Moses.   Exodus 21:2  This proclamaiton seems to have been made under the pressure of the siege.  But afterwards, when the Chaldean army had temporarily departed from Jerusalem,  Jeremiah 34:21-22 , the princes and people again reduced to bondage their servants whom they had set free.   Jeremiah 34:11

title: Jeremiah 34:11
text: Those acts of duty upon which men enter unwillingly, under the influence of fear, are generally abandoned as soon as the outward pressure is removed.   Jeremiah 34:21

title: Jeremiah 34:13
text:
vv 13-14. 
 
By the law of Moses the Hebrews were forbidden to oppress their brethren, and reduce them to perpetual bondage.  The Christian religion has abolished the distinction between Jews and Gentiles.  It teaches us to regard all men as brethren,  Luke 10:36-37 , and to treat them accordingly.

title: Jeremiah 34:15
text:
vv 15-22. 
 
Perfidy in our dealings with men is a heinous sin, which God will punish; but its guilt is greatly aggravated when they whom we deceive by false promises are weak and unable to defend themselves.  Of all such God is the protector and avenger.   Proverbs 22:22-23 s

title: Jeremiah 34:16
text: Polluted my name; by violating their covenant made before God in his house; an act of shameless perjury.

title: Jeremiah 34:18
text: Passed between the parts; compare  Genesis 15:10 Genesis 15:17 .

title: Jeremiah 35:2
text: God employs every variety of method to bring men to repentance; not only his own direct authority, but also, as in this chapter, examples of obedience to parental commands.

title: Jeremiah 35:6
text:
Jonadab the son of Rechab; contemporary with Jehu, king of Israel,  II Kings 10:15 , and a descendant of the Kenites.   I Chronicles 2:55   He was not an Israelite,  Jeremiah 35:7 , but a worshipper of the true God, and an eminently wise and good man. 
 
  Ye shall drink no wine--nor your sons for ever; thus he took the best and most effectual means to secure his posterity against intemperance with all its attendant evils. 
 
vv 6-7. 
 
Temperance, frugality, and simplicity of manners, are a far better portion for this world than large estates and sumptuous mansions; and all wise parents will do what lies in their power to secure their children in the possession of such a noble inheritance.

title: Jeremiah 35:7
text: Neither shall ye build house--ye shall dwell in tents; he wished them not to effect wealth or luxury, but to live in tents after the manner of shepherds, which was favorable alike to independence and simplicity of manners.

title: Jeremiah 35:12
text:
vv 12-17. 
 
Since God's authority is infinitely higher than that of earthly parents, rebellion against him is beyond measure more heinous, and will be punished with corresponding severity.

title: Jeremiah 35:14
text: Unto this day; a period of about two hundred and eighty years.

title: Jeremiah 35:18
text: vv 18-19. Filial obedience is a virtue with which God has in a peculiar degree connected the reward of temporal prosperity.

title: Jeremiah 36:2
text:
vv 2-3. 
 
All God's dealings with his people are marked by sincerity and openness; he multiplies his endeavors to bring them to repentance, and sends not his chastisements upon them until he has abundantly warned them of their approach.

title: Jeremiah 36:5
text:
vv 5-6. 
 
Outward constraint does not hinder the faithful servant of God from continuing his labors as he has opportunity; and a prison has often afforded a most profitable field of activity.

title: Jeremiah 36:8
text: They who are not themselves preachers can often render most important aid to those who hold this office; and it is their duty to do so as they have opportunity.

title: Jeremiah 36:9
text: In the fifth year--in the ninth month; this delay of so many months seems to have had for its object to secure the most convenient time for reading the roll.

title: Jeremiah 36:16
text:
Were afraid both one and other; literally, "they feared one to another;" that is, looked upon one another with astonishment and fear. 
 
vv 16-19. 
 
The workings of conscience in the minds of irreligious men often second the preachers of the truth in so powerful a way that they are willing, to a certain extent, to countenance their labors and protect them from their enemies.

title: Jeremiah 36:19
text: Go, hide thee, thou and Jeremiah; though Jeremiah was under some sort of confinement,  Jeremiah 36:5 , yet with the favor and countenance of the princes, it would be easy for him and Baruch to secrete themselves.

title: Jeremiah 36:22
text:
In the ninth month; answering nearly to our January. 
 
  A fire on the hearth burning; more exactly, "the pot was burning before him."  The people of the East warm their rooms by means of a pot containing burning wood or charcoal.

title: Jeremiah 36:23
text:
Leaves; that is, columns into which the roll was divided. 
 
vv 23-26. 
 
Men in high stations, who are fully set in their sinful ways, will not bear faithful reproof; but will, so far as lies in their power, persecute its preachers, and destroy both them and their messages.

title: Jeremiah 36:27
text:
vv 27-31. 
 
Opposition to God's awful threatenings cannot hinder their execution; it can only provoke his anger, and involve us in deeper ruin.

title: Jeremiah 36:30
text: None to sit upon the throne of David; his son Jechoniah reigned only three months, and he had no successor of his own children.  See note on  Jeremiah 22:30 .

title: Jeremiah 36:32
text: In all ages of the world, wicked rulers and false teachers have combined to suppress and hinder the knowledge of God's word.  But he will in the final issue overthrow all who array themselves against it, and give it free course through the earth.

title: Jeremiah 37:1
text:
vv 1-3. 
 
To consult God's servants can profit us nothing, unless we obey the counsels which they deliver to us in his name.

title: Jeremiah 37:5
text:
vv 5-10. 
 
While men continue to practise iniquity, all their plans to obtain deliverance and salvation through their fellow sinners will prove vain.  Isaiah 30:3 Isaiah 31:3

title: Jeremiah 37:11
text:
vv 11-15. 
 
Hatred and prejudice make men ready to entertain unfounded suspicious against their neighbors, and to construe as crimes their most innocent acts.

title: Jeremiah 37:12
text:
To separate himself thence; or, according to some, to take his portion thence; that is, to receive from his patrimony in Anathoth what belonged to him. 
 
  In the midst of the people; along with the rest of the people.

title: Jeremiah 37:13
text: Fallest away to the Chaldeans; his predictions of the success of the Chaldeans, and his exhortations to the people to submit to their yoke, gave plausibility to this slander.

title: Jeremiah 37:17
text: Wicked men are often driven in their distress to seek counsel from those whom they are afraid openly to countenance and protect.

title: Jeremiah 37:19
text: False teachers may flatter their patrons with the hope of impunity in sin, but they cannot help them in the day of trouble.

title: Jeremiah 37:20
text:
vv 20-21. 
 
Whatever perils and sufferings come upon us in the discharge of our duty, we should meet with courage and alacrity.  At the same time, we ought to use all proper means to avoid needless exposure, since suffering for its own sake has neither goodness nor merit.

title: Jeremiah 38:1
text:
vv 1-4. 
 
Not they who encourage men in rebellion against God, but they who advise submission to his revealed will, are the true friends of their country; yet such men are often denounced and persecuted as its enemies.

title: Jeremiah 38:5
text:
vv 5-6. 
 
When weak and irresolute men, who have not courage to resist the importunities of wicked counsellors, are exalted to high stations, the enemies of good men have a great advantage over them, which they do not fail to improve for persecuting, and, if possible, destroying them.

title: Jeremiah 38:7
text:
vv 7-13. 
 
In the greatest extremities God is able to raise up for his servants efficient friends, by whom they are delivered, and their enemies frustrated.

title: Jeremiah 38:9
text: Like to die for hunger--no more bread in the city; the famine in the city being extreme, and Jeremiah out of sight, no one would carry him food, and thus he die of hunger.

title: Jeremiah 38:17
text:
vv 17-20. 
 
The unbelief of Zedekiah prevented him from taking the way of safety which God by his prophet had pointed out to him; and so he perished with his family and nobles.  Herein he is set forth as an example for the instruction and warning of all who imitate his want of faith.

title: Jeremiah 38:21
text:
vv 21-23. 
 
They who are deterred from doing their duty through fear of men, generally bring upon themselves the very evils which they dread, in more aggravated forms.

title: Jeremiah 38:22
text:
Brought forth; as captives. 
 
  Those women shall say; Zedekiah feared the reproach of his princes, but he should become an object of derision to the women of his palace. 
 
  Thy friends; thy false advisers. 
 
  Have set thee on; urged thee to contend with the king of Babylon, instead of submitting to him. 
 
  They are turned away back; thy friends have led thee into ruin, and then forsaken thee.

title: Jeremiah 38:27
text: Though falsehood and deceit are always wrong, we are yet not bound to reveal all the truth to those who have no right to know it, and who seek it from malicious motives.   I Samuel 16:2-5

title: Jeremiah 39:1
text:
vv 1-10. 
 
Though God's threatened judgments be long delayed, they wll come at last upon those who persist in their impenitence; and then the reality will be as terrible as the previous announcement of them.

title: Jeremiah 39:2
text: The city was broken up; a breach was made in its walls; probably in the northern wall of the lower city, which itself lay north of the upper city or Zion, for this was the side on which Jerusalem was most open to assault.

title: Jeremiah 39:3
text: The middle gate; probably the gate of the wall which separated the upper city from the lower.

title: Jeremiah 39:4
text:
The king's garden; in the south-east, near the place where the two valleys of Kedron and Hinnom meet. 
 
  The way of the plain; the way toward the plain of the Jordan.

title: Jeremiah 39:5
text: Riblah in the land of Hamath; north of Palestine, on the route from that country to Babylon.

title: Jeremiah 39:10
text: The poor of the people; compare  Isaiah 3:1-3 .

title: Jeremiah 39:11
text:
vv 11-14. 
 
In the overthrow of the wicked, God will provide for the safety of his faithful servants who put their trust in him.

title: Jeremiah 39:15
text:
vv 15-18. 
 
No act of faith and love can escape the notice of Jehovah.  In the present life God will generally reward it openly, and always in the life to come.

title: Jeremiah 40:1
text: The word which came to Jeremiah; these words refer to the prophecies that follow in  Jeremiah 42:1-22 , the history of the remnant of the Jews being first given by way of introduction.

title: Jeremiah 40:3
text: Great and long-continued disobedience in his people, God often punishes in such an exemplary way that even the unconverted are compelled to see and acknowledge his hand.

title: Jeremiah 40:4
text: When the visible church of God hates and persecutes his messengers, he often raises up for them defenders from without, under whose protection they are enabled to prosecute their labors in safety.

title: Jeremiah 40:5
text: While he was not yet gone back; the prophet seems to have hesitated respecting his future course, which gave occasion to Nebuzar-adan to put his proposition in a different form.

title: Jeremiah 40:7
text: Captains of the forces; leaders, of the scattered bands of the Jews.

title: Jeremiah 40:8
text: Mizpah; in the land of Benjamin, a short distance north-west from Jerusalem.

title: Jeremiah 40:13
text:
vv 13-16. 
 
Those who are conscious of their own integrity, are sometimes too unsuspecting with regard to their fellow men, and thus, by neglecting the warnings of friends, become involved, with those under their care, in calamity and death.

title: Jeremiah 41:1
text:
In the seventh month; of the year in which Jerusalem was taken.  Jeremiah 39:2  
 
Times of anarchy and confusion are prolific in crime.  When the outward restraints of civil government are removed, no limit can be set to the atrocities which wicked men will commit for the sake of power and plunder.  Yet even in such dark days God is able to limit the wrath of man, and raise up for his people deliverers and defenders.

title: Jeremiah 41:5
text:
Their beards shaven--cut themselves; these were signs of mourning for the destruction of the holy city and temple. 
 
  To the house of the Lord; that is, to the place where it had stood, and which they regarded as still holy.

title: Jeremiah 41:6
text: Weeping--as he went; in pretended sympathy with them.

title: Jeremiah 41:12
text: The great waters--in Gibeon; a copious fountain with large reservoirs, one of which, and the ruins of the other, still remain. Compare  II Samuel 2:13 .

title: Jeremiah 41:17
text: To go to enter into Egypt; they made a temporary soujourn at Chimham, on their way to Egypt.

title: Jeremiah 42:1
text: Wicked men have a general conviction of the necessity of God's favor and protection, that they may be safe from danger and prospered in their undertakings; and they are often ready to seek counsel from his servants with much apparent earnestness and humility, and with many professions of an obedient spirit.  But they have no true regard to God's authority, and when his commands interfere with their cherished desires and purposes, they will rebel against him, saying, "Who is the Lord, that we should obey his voice?"

title: Jeremiah 42:12
text: Cause you to return to you own land; most of the people whom Jeremiah addressed had been dispersed among the surrounding nations, and they were now in an unsettled state and on their way to Egypt.  The prophet's meaning is, that if they will obey God, Nebuchadnezzar shall give them quiet possission of their own land.

title: Jeremiah 42:14
text: We will go into the land of Egypt; the spirit that prompted them to this course was sinful reliance on the help of man, rather than on God's promises.  Compare  Isaiah 30:1-5 Isaiah 31:1-3 .

title: Jeremiah 43:1
text:
vv 1-7. 
 
They who best understand the deceitfulness and desperate wickedness of the human heart, will be slow to rely upon the promises of wicked men to receive and obey God's counsels, and will prepare themselves to encounter reproach and persecution whenever their answers are not agreeable to the feelings and wishes of wicked men who consult them.

title: Jeremiah 43:7
text: Tahpanhes; on the frontier of Egypt, towards Palestine.

title: Jeremiah 43:8
text:
vv 8-13. 
 
It is vain to seek safety by disobeying God's commands.  His wrath will follow sinners into all their false refuges, and destroy them and their hiding places together.

title: Jeremiah 43:10
text: My servant; as executing God's purposes, though he knew it not.

title: Jeremiah 44:1
text:
Migdol; on the north-eastern frontier of Egypt towards Palestine.  Exodus 14:2  
 
  Tahpanhes; see note on  Jeremiah 43:7 . 
 
  Noph; the same as "Moph," (English version,"Memphis,")  Hosea 9:6 ; a large city of ancient Egypt on the west bank of the Nile, a little above Cairo.

title: Jeremiah 44:2
text:
vv 2-10. 
 
When wicked men refuse to take warning from the punishment of those who have practised the same sins before them, it is a great aggravation of their guilt.

title: Jeremiah 44:9
text: Have ye forgotten the wickedness--in the land of Judah, and in the streets of Jerusalem?  have ye forgotten the judgments which I brought upon you for your wickedness there?

title: Jeremiah 44:11
text:
vv 11-14. 
 
God's wrath follows the wicked into every place whither they flee for safety, and overthrows all their vain confidences.  It is only by repenting and returning to him that they can escape destruction.

title: Jeremiah 44:15
text:
Their wives had burned incense; their wives were leaders in idolatry.  Probably some of them were of heathen origin.  Compare  Deuteronomy 17:17 I Kings 11:1 I Kings 11:4 I Kings 15:13 . 
 
vv 15-23. 
 
Wicked men are prone to impute their misfortunes to every other cause, rather than the true one; nay, more, to seek a return of prosperity from those very practices which have brought ruin upon them.

title: Jeremiah 44:24
text:
vv 24-30. 
 
They who will no longer hear reproof are in the road to speedy destruction; God will fight against them and their helpers, and both shall perish together.

title: Jeremiah 44:26
text: Shall no more be named in the month of any man of Judah; because all shall be destroyed except a small remnant.   Jeremiah 44:27-28

title: Jeremiah 44:30
text: Pharaoh-hophra; the reigning monarch of Egypt, called "Apries" by the Greeks.  He was defeated by Nebuchadnezzar at Carchemish, and afterwards dethroned and strangled by his own troops.

title: Jeremiah 45:1
text:
In the fourth year of Jehoiakim; see  Jeremiah 36:1-32 .  This prophecy belongs to an earlier date than those recorded in the preceding eight chapters. 
 
It is well to count before hand the cost of God's service, and to hold ourselves ready to endure hardships in the performance of it.  We ought never to set our hearts on personal ease and preferment; but in times of general public calamity this is peculiarly improper; we should then be content with the continuance of our lives, and our opportunities to labor in behalf of God's cause.

title: Jeremiah 45:3
text: Woe is me now; Baruch was dismayed in view of the sufferings to which he was exposed in consequence of writing the roll mentioned in  Jeremiah 36:1-32 , as well as of the calamitous condition of his country.

title: Jeremiah 45:5
