text: And seekest thou great things for thyself? in a time of general desolation, Baruch must not set his heart on temporal ease, honor, and affluence.

title: Jeremiah 46:1
text: The word of the Lord--against the Gentiles; here begins a series of prophecies against the heathen nations, extending through the remainder of the book, with the exception of the last chapter.  The present verse constitutes a preface to the whole series.

title: Jeremiah 46:2
text:
Against Egypt; that is, as immediately explained, against Pharaoh's expedition against the Chaldees.  He made two expeditions against Carchemish; in the first of these he slew Josiah,  II Chronicles 35:20-24 , and afterwards defeated the Chaldeans and took the city; in the second, his army was defeated with great loss, as here predicted. 
 
Nations that know not God are subject to his providential control.  He makes all their movements subservient to the interests of his church, exalting one to power and overthrowing another, according to his pleasure.

title: Jeremiah 46:3
text: Order ye the buckler; addressed to the Egyptians, as much as to say, All your preparations for war shall end in your own destruction.

title: Jeremiah 46:4
text:
Get up, ye horsemen; go up against Assyria.   Jeremiah 46:7   But many render, "Mount, ye horsemen." 
 
  Brigandines; coats of mail.

title: Jeremiah 46:5
text:
vv 5-6. 
 
  Wherefore have I seen--they shall stumble and fal; the prophet sees in vision the terror and flight of the Egyptians by the Euphrates. 
 
When God fights against a people, no array of human might can avail; he will turn all its plans for conquering others to its own destruction.

title: Jeremiah 46:7
text:
vv 7-8. 
 
  Who is this--will cover the earth; the prophet returns now to the preparations of the Egyptians.  He compares their vast armies to the overflowing waters of the Nile.

title: Jeremiah 46:9
text: Lydians; here probably an African tribe.  Compare  Ezekiel 30:5 .

title: Jeremiah 46:10
text:
The day of the Lord God of hosts; when he gathers together the armies of Egypt to destroy them. 
 
  A sacrifice; a great slaughter of the Egyptians. 
 
  In the north country; in the land of the Chaldeans.  See note on  Jeremiah 1:14 .

title: Jeremiah 46:11
text: Gilead; the land of balm.   Jeremiah 8:22   The meaning is, Though thou gather the balm of Gilead, thou canst not be healed of thy wounds.

title: Jeremiah 46:13
text: The word that the Lord spake; these words introduce a second prophecy against Egypt, referring to the invasion of the land by Nebuchadnezzar, which took place some years after Pharaoh-necho's disastrous expedition against the Chaldees.

title: Jeremiah 46:14
text: Stand fast--prepare thee; a mighty conqueror is coming: let Egypt prepare to resist him, if she can.

title: Jeremiah 46:16
text: They said; the hired troops of the Egyptians.

title: Jeremiah 46:17
text:
There; in the land of their nativity, after their return home. 
 
  Passed; that is, has let pass. 
 
  The time appointed; or, the set time.  By this, some understand the time set for meeting and sustaining his allies; others, the opportunity of success. 
 
Since all the power of kings and rulers comes from God, none of them can shield transgressors against his wrath.  Sinners who confide in their promises of help, will find them to be "but a noise" without substance.

title: Jeremiah 46:18
text: As Tabor--as Carmel--shall he come; Nebuchadnezzar shall come with the strength and majesty of Tabor and Carmel, the two most prominent mountains in north Palestine.

title: Jeremiah 46:19
text: Daughter dwelling in Egypt; Egypt is personified as a delicate female.

title: Jeremiah 46:21
text:
Her hired men; see note on  Jeremiah 46:16 . 
 
  Like fatted bullocks; they are well fed and lusty, but flee in wild confusion before the enemy.

title: Jeremiah 46:22
text:
The voice thereof; literally, "her voice," Egypt's voice. 
 
  Shall go like a serpent; as a serpent retreats with hissing and terror before the woodman. 
 
  Against her; against Egypt.

title: Jeremiah 46:23
text:
Her forest; her armies and people. 
 
  Though it cannot be searched; though its trees are of vast extent and innumerable.

title: Jeremiah 46:25
text: No; the celebrated capital of Egypt, in Upper Egypt, on both sides of the Nile.   Nahum 3:8

title: Jeremiah 46:26
text: Afterward it shall be inhabited; the desolation of Egypt by Nebuchadnezzar was only temporary.  Compare  Ezekiel 29:11-15 .

title: Jeremiah 46:27
text:
vv 27-28. 
 
The nations of the world rise to power and perish in rapid succession; but in the midst of all thise changes, God's kingdom is continually advancing under his own immediate superintendence.  All the afflictions which befall his people have the effect, not to destroy, but to purify them, and thus prepare them for increased prosperity.

title: Jeremiah 47:1
text:
Before that Pharaoh smote Gaza; this is mentioned simply as a date; or the prophecy relates to the desolation of Philistia, not by Pharaoh, but by Nebuchadnezzar. 
 
God's judgments upon wicked nations often come like an overflowing flood which nothing can resist, and which sweeps away every thing. Before them the great and the mighty find themselves utterly helpless, having no power either to resist or to escape.  How terrible will be that great day of judgment which shall destroy for ever "all the proud, yea, and all that do wickedly, that it shall leave them neither root nor branch."

title: Jeremiah 47:2
text:
Waters; a symbol of overflowing and desolating armies. 
 
  Out of the north; out of Babylon.   Jeremiah 1:14   Nebuchadnezzar besieged and took Tyre,  Jeremiah 27:3 Jeremiah 27:6 Ezekiel 26:7-14 ; and afterwards conquered Egypt.   Ezekiel 29:17-20   It was during this expedition that his armies overran Philistia.  Compare  Jeremiah 47:4 .

title: Jeremiah 47:3
text:
The fathers shall not look back to their children; shall not concern themselves about their safety. 
 
  Feebleness of hands; the effect of extreme terror.

title: Jeremiah 47:4
text:
From Tyrua and Zidon; see note on  Jeremiah 47:2 . 
 
  Every helper that remaineth; every one who could help them against the common invader. 
 
  Caphtor; the original country of the Philistines: according to some, Cappadocia; according to others, the island of Crete.

title: Jeremiah 48:1
text:
Against Moab; in this prophecy Jeremiah makes a free use of the earlier prophecy of Isaiah.  The reader may consult the notes on  Isaiah 15:1-16:14 , where will be found an account of many of the places mentioned in this chapter, and also an explanation of many of its peculiar expressions.  The overthrow of Moab, however, which Isaiah predicted, was not the same as that which is here foretold.  The former took place in connection with the captivity of the ten tribes, and in Isaiah's day,  Isaiah 16:14 ; the latter, as also that of the nations mentioned in the following chapters, was accomplished by Nebuchadnezzar. 
 
  Kiriathaim; in the northern part of Moab, west of Medebah. 
 
The sins of the Moabites which brought upon them God's displeasure were their great pride and arrogance, manifested in trusting to their own defences and treasures, and in maginifying themselves against the Lord,  Jeremiah 48:7 Jeremiah 48:14 Jeremiah 48:29 Jeremiah 48:42 ; also their hatred and contempt of God's people, leading them to help forward and exult over their calamities.  Jeremiah 48:27 Jeremiah 48:30   For these sins God made Moab "a derision and a dismaying to all them about him."   Jeremiah 48:26 Jeremiah 48:39   Since the principles of God's government are unchangeable, all who follow the example of Moab, whether nations or individuals, must expect to receive punishment at God's hand.

title: Jeremiah 48:2
text: They have devised evil; the enemies of Moab have devised; in allusion to the signification of the word Heshbon, that is, "device," as it is rendered in  Ecclesiastes 9:10 .

title: Jeremiah 48:6
text: Be like the heath in the wilderness; that is, solitary and desolate.   Jeremiah 17:6

title: Jeremiah 48:7
text: Chemosh; the national god of the Moabites.  I Kings 11:7 II Kings 23:13

title: Jeremiah 48:10
text: Cursed be he; he among the executioners of God's wrath upon Moab.

title: Jeremiah 48:11
text: Settled on his lees; as the flavor of wine is increased by leaving it to stand on the lees, so long tranquility had increased the strength and riches of Moab, and with these his pride.

title: Jeremiah 48:12
text: Wanderers, that shall cause him ot wander; better, "emptiers, that shall empty him."  The original word means to empty by laying a vessel over on its side.

title: Jeremiah 48:13
text: Of Beth-el; that is, of the golden calf which they worshipped there.   I Kings 12:29

title: Jeremiah 48:15
text: Gone up out of her cities; or, "her cities are gone up," that is, in smoke.

title: Jeremiah 48:17
text: The strong staff--beautiful rod; the sceptre of his power.

title: Jeremiah 48:18
text: Daughter; a metaphor for the inhabitants of Dibon, as "virgin daughter of Babylon," etc.   Isaiah 47:1

title: Jeremiah 48:19
text: Aroer; on the northern bank of the Arnon.  Its inhabitants come out to inquire of the fugitives that pass through it in their flight, "What is done?"

title: Jeremiah 48:24
text: Bozrah; this seems to have been Bozrah in the Hauran, on the border of the Arabian desert, and not the Bozrah which is mentioned in  Jeremiah 49:13 , as belonging to Edom; the latter lay south-east of the Dead sea.

title: Jeremiah 48:26
text:
Make ye him drunken; with the wine-cup of God's wrath.  Jeremiah 25:15-27  
 
  He also; that is, as well as Israel.   Jeremiah 48:27

title: Jeremiah 48:27
text:
A derision unto thee; when carried into captivity by the Assyrians. 
 
  Was he found among thieves? that is, was he detected by Moab in such a crime as made him a just object of his derision?  Compare  Jeremiah 2:26  
 
  Spakest of him; of his calamities.

title: Jeremiah 48:28
text: Be like the dove; hide yourselves in dens and caves from the enemy. Compare  Isaiah 2:19-21 .

title: Jeremiah 48:30
text: Not be so; as he purposes.  Compare  Isaiah 16:6 .

title: Jeremiah 48:31
text: Kir-heres; the same as Kir-hareseth.   Isaiah 16:7

title: Jeremiah 48:32
text:
vv 31-32. 
 
  I wll weep for thee--no shouting; see notes on  Isaiah 16:8-9 . 
 
  The sea of Jazer; of this nothing further is known. 
 
  Their shouting shall be no shouting; their joyous vintage-shout shall become a battle-shout, shall become a cry of distress.

title: Jeremiah 48:34
text:
From the cry of Heshbon--uttered their voice; the cry of distress which begins at Heshbon extends to Elealeh and Jahaz. 
 
  From Zoar even unto Horonaim; supply, "they have uttered their voice." 
 
  A heifer of three years old; see note on  Isaiah 15:5  
 
  The waters--of Nimrim shall be desolate; see note on  Isaiah 15:6 .

title: Jeremiah 48:38
text: Like a vessel wherein is no pleasure; compare  Jeremiah 22:28 .

title: Jeremiah 48:40
text: He shall fly; the conqueror.

title: Jeremiah 48:45
text:
They that fled; the Moabites who fled before the invading army. 
 
  Stood under the shadow of Heshbon; sought protection within its walls. 
 
  Because of the force; because of the invading force; but many render these words, "without strength." 
 
  A fire--out of Heshbon; the conqueror shall send forth thence his bands to ravage the country. 
 
  Sihon; that is, the city of Sihon; the same as Heshbon.  See the history of this city,  Numbers 21:26-30 , from which passage this and  Jeremiah 48:46  are taken. 
 
  The tumultuous ones; the boastful warriors of Moab.

title: Jeremiah 48:47
text: Bring again the captivity of Moab; the desolation of Moab and several other countries involved in the general overthrow by Nebuchadnezzar, should be but temporary,  Jeremiah 49:6 Jeremiah 49:39 ; but of others perpetual,  Jeremiah 49:33 .

title: Jeremiah 49:1
text:
Hath Israel no sons--no heir? the Ammonites are reproached for taking possession of the territory of Israel east of the Jordan, after its conquest by the Assyrians. 
 
  Their king; or, "Milcom," the god of the Ammonites.   I Kings 11:5  
 
  Gad; whose lands lay on the east of Jordan, adjacent to Ammon.  Numbers 32:33-36  
 
vv 1-2. 
 
God is greatly displeased with those who take advantage of the weakness of their neighbors to rob them of their just possessions, and he will not fail to reward them according to their deeds.

title: Jeremiah 49:2
text: Rabbah; the capital of the Ammonites.

title: Jeremiah 49:3
text:
Howl, O Heshbon; Heshbon belonged to Moab.  It is here exhorted to howl for the taking of Ai, because thus the way was prepared for invading it. 
 
  Ai; here a city of the Ammonites, different from the Ai mentioned in  Joshua 8:1-35 .

title: Jeremiah 49:4
text: In the valleys; the fertile valleys of thy territory.

title: Jeremiah 49:7
text:
Concerning Edom; compare the prophecy of Obadiah, between which and this there is a remarkable agreement. 
 
  Teman; a city and region on the eastern border of Edom.  The Temanites were celebrated for their wisdom, but this should avail them nothing in the present calamity. 
 
The highest wisdom of men is to fear God and do righteousness; when they depart from him, and put their trust in wickedness, no sagacity or skill can shield them against his anger.

title: Jeremiah 49:8
text:
Dwell deep; that is, take refuge from the enemy in deep caverns. 
 
  Dedan; an Arabian tribe bordering on Edom.

title: Jeremiah 49:9
text:
Leave some gleaning grapes; not utterly destroy thee, as thy foes shall now do. 
 
  Till they have enough; that is, only till their wants are satisfied.

title: Jeremiah 49:11
text: Leave thy fatherless choldren--let thy widows trust in me; a solemn intimation that all the adult makes of Edom should be destroyed, so that their widows and orphans should be thrown upon God's mercy alone for protection.

title: Jeremiah 49:12
text:
They whose judgment was not to drink; the covenant people of God, who might have hoped for exemption from the general calamity.  Compare  Jeremiah 25:28 Obadiah 1:16 . 
 
The severity with which God chastises his offending people, is a solemn warning to his enemies of the utter destruction that awaits them.  If he spare not his own household, what shall be the end of those who are strangers and foreigners to it?   I Peter 4:17-19

title: Jeremiah 49:15
text:
vv 15-16. 
 
It is God's unalterable purpose to abase all the proud, whether they be nations, families, or individuals.

title: Jeremiah 49:16
text: In the clefts of the rock; in the rocky fortresses for which Edom was celebrated.  Compare  Obadiah 1:3-4 .

title: Jeremiah 49:19
text:
He shall come up; Nebuchadnezzar. 
 
  The swelling of Jordan; see note on  Jeremiah 12:5  
 
  The strong; the strong shepherd; that is, the king of Edom.  The reference is to the great natural strength of the country. 
 
  But I will suddenly; rather, "for I will suddenly." 
 
  Make him run; the strong one just mentioned. 
 
  From her; from his land. 
 
  Who is a chosen man--appoint over her? or, "him who is a chosen one," that is Nebuchadnezzar, "I will appoint over her," over Edom. 
 
  Appoint me the time; for trial; that is, call me into judgment.

title: Jeremiah 49:20
text: The least of the flock shall draw them out; the feeblest of the invading host shall drag out the Edomites to slaughter.  But many render, "he," the enemy, "shall drag them out like weak sheep."

title: Jeremiah 49:23
text:
Hamath--Arpad; see note on  Isaiah 10:9 . 
 
  On the sea; in Damascus, which is compared to an agitated sea.

title: Jeremiah 49:25
text: How is the city--of my joy; this is the exclamation of Damascus, bewailing the desolation of her capital.

title: Jeremiah 49:28
text:
Kedar; see note on  Isaiah 21:16 . 
 
  Hazor; there were several places of this name: one in the north of Palestine,  Joshua 11:1 ; and one in Benjamin,  Nehemiah 11:33 .  But Hazor here seems to have been an Arabian tribe bordering on Kedar.

title: Jeremiah 49:31
text:
Arise; an exhortation to the Chaldean armies. 
 
  Unto the wealthy nation; that is, to Hazor. 
 
  Dwelleth without care--alone; as being remote from the common path of armies. 
 
vv 31-32. 
 
The security that follows long continued prosperity is often the occasion of men's destruction, as it leads them to neglect the necessary means of protection.

title: Jeremiah 49:34
text: Elam; Persia, which lay east of Babylon.

title: Jeremiah 50:2
text:
Set up a standard; the tidings of Babylon's fall are to be spread by signals as well as words. 
 
  Bel--Merodach; idols of Babylon. 
 
  Her idols are confounded; they are put to shame, because they could not save those who trusted in them.

title: Jeremiah 50:3
text: A nation; the Medes and Persians, whose country lay to the north-east of Babylon.

title: Jeremiah 50:4
text:
The children of Israel shall come, they and the children of Judah together; the ten tribes who had been carried captive by the Assyrians, at least a remnant of them, united themselves with the Jews on their return to Palestine under Cyrus.  Thus was fulfilled the prophecy of Ezekiel,  Ezekiel 37:15-22 ; though a still higher fulfilment of it may be reserved for the future. 
 
It is when God's people seek his face with weeping and supplication that he interposes for their deliverance, accomplishing with infinite ease the mightiest overthrows in their behalf, and restoring them to more than their former prosperity.   Daniel 9:20-21

title: Jeremiah 50:7
text: Since wicked men are moved by hatred and malice to persecute God's church, he will hold them guilty for all the sufferings which they inflict upon her; while at the same time he uses them as a rod for chastisement and correction.   Isaiah 10:5-12

title: Jeremiah 50:8
text: As the he-goats before the flocks; this is addressed especially to the Jewish rulers and leaders.

title: Jeremiah 50:9
text: All the nations of the earth move in accordance with God's eternal counsels; while they are intent upon the accomplishment of their own selfish schemes, he is bringing to pass, through their instrumentality, his wise and good purposes for the chastisement of Zion, or for her deliverance and enlargement.

title: Jeremiah 50:12
text: Your mother--she that bare you; that is, Babylon, considered as the mother of the people.

title: Jeremiah 50:15
text: She hath given her hand; surrendered herself as vanquished.

title: Jeremiah 50:16
text: They shall turn; the foreigners in Babylon.

title: Jeremiah 50:18
text: As I have punished the king of Assyria; Assyria, with Nineveh its capital, had already fallen in the days of Jeremiah, and was now subject to the Chaldeans.

title: Jeremiah 50:20
text: The outward deliverance of God's people is connected with their inward penitence and return to duty.   Nehemiah 1:4-11 Nehemiah 2:1-8

title: Jeremiah 50:21
text: Merathaim--Pekod; symbolical names: the first, double rebellion, indicating the character; the second, visitation, the fate of Babylon.

title: Jeremiah 50:23
text:
vv 23-34. 
 
Sometimes God allows wicked nations to accumulate vast power and wealth, so that it seems as if they would be able to trample under foot and break in pieces the whole earth without end.  But he can at any moment open his armory against them, and overwhelm them with the weapons of his indignation.  The examples on record of the sudden fall of mighty monarchies, are a standing manifestation of God's supreme power over all that is called powerful among men.

title: Jeremiah 50:26
text: Cast her up as heaps; heaps of sheaves at the threshing-floor.

title: Jeremiah 50:34
text: To the land; the land of Israel.

title: Jeremiah 50:36
text: Liars; diviners, who deceived the people with lies.

title: Jeremiah 50:37
text: Mingled people; mingled mass of foreigners made up of men of different nations.   Jeremiah 25:20 Jeremiah 25:24

title: Jeremiah 50:42
text: They who have oppressed and destroyed their fellow men without mercy, whether natins or individuals, shall be destroyed in like manner.  James 2:13

title: Jeremiah 50:44
text: Behold--before me; see note  Jeremiah 49:19 .

title: Jeremiah 50:45
text: Shall draw them out; see note  Jeremiah 49:20 .

title: Jeremiah 50:46
text: Haughty and powerful oppressors shall be visited by God with terrible judgments, such as shall fill the inhabitants of the earth with awe and terror.

title: Jeremiah 51:1
text: Babylon was one of the mightiest empires which the world ever saw, and it made itself conspicuous above all other nations of ancient times by persecuting God's covenant people.  For this reason it stands in the Scriptures as the representative of all organized forms of persecution, whether secular or spiritual.  Its terrible overthrow, so complete and so perpetual, is both a proof of God's power, and a pledge of his purpose to destroy and break in pieces every thing that exalts itself against the kingdom of his Son, however great may be its power and resources.  All who join themselves to his enemies shall perish; but "blessed are all they that put their trust in him."

title: Jeremiah 51:5
text: Though their land was filled with sin; more literally, "for their land," the land of the Babylonians, "is filled."

title: Jeremiah 51:7
text:
Babylon--a golden cup; the wine-cup of God's wrath.  She is called a golden cup to indicate her great wealth. 
 
  Have drunken of her wine; have suffered divine inflictions through her agency.  In  Revelation of John 17:4 , the figure is used in a different way, to express the intoxication of error and sin.

title: Jeremiah 51:9
text: We would have healed Babylon; the allies of Babylon speak.

title: Jeremiah 51:12
text: Upon the walls of Babylon; or, "against the walls of Babylon."

title: Jeremiah 51:13
text: The measure of thy covetousness; it is full for punishment. Compare  Genesis 15:16 .

title: Jeremiah 51:14
text: With men; that is, troops of enemies.

title: Jeremiah 51:15
text:
vv 15-19. 
 
  He hath made--his name; repeated from  Jeremiah 10:12-16 .

title: Jeremiah 51:20
text:
Thou art my battle-axe; that is, Babylon, as the instrument which God has employed to punish the nations,  Jeremiah 51:25 ; but some understand these words of Cyrus. 
 
  Will I break in pieces; or, "I have broken in pieces."

title: Jeremiah 51:25
text: O destroying mountain; Babylon is here compared to a volcanic mountain, which has sent forth desolating streams of fire over all the nations.  But she shall be thrust down from her high position, and made a mass of burnt and broken fragments.

title: Jeremiah 51:27
text: Ararat, Minni, and Ashchenaz; provinces of Armenia, or of adjacent regions.

title: Jeremiah 51:31
text: At one end; literally, "at the end."  The armies of Cyrus marched into Babylon at both ends, through he channel of the Euphrates, the waters of which they had turned off while the Babylonians were engaged in feasting.

title: Jeremiah 51:32
text:
The passages; probably those which connected the two parts of the city. 
 
  The reeds; literally, "the marshes;" probably marshes covered with tall reeds, that impeded the march of the enemy.

title: Jeremiah 51:34
text: Cast me out; from my own land.  Zion is the speaker.  Jeremiah 51:35

title: Jeremiah 51:36
text: Dry up her sea; this seems to be a prophetic allusion to the way in which the city was taken, by the drawing off of the waters of the Euphrates, so as to afford a passage to the army of Cyrus through its channel.

title: Jeremiah 51:39
text:
In their heat; whole they are inflamed with wine.  See note on  Jeremiah 51:31 . 
 
  I will make their feasts; Jehovah will himself prepare for them another banquet, even a deadly cup; that is, destruction by the armies of Cyrus. 
 
  Rejoice; rave, after the manner of the drunken.

title: Jeremiah 51:41
text: Sheshach; see note on  Jeremiah 25:26 .

title: Jeremiah 51:42
text: The sea; the desolating armies of the Medes. Compare  Isaiah 8:7-8

title: Jeremiah 51:46
text: And lest your heart faint, and ye fear; better, "And let not your heart faint, that ye should fear."  In such a time of confusion many discouraging rumors would reach the ears of the returning exiles; these they are exhorted to disregard.

title: Jeremiah 51:51
text: We are confounded; the prophet here speaks in the name of God's covenant people.

title: Jeremiah 51:55
text: The great voice; the tumult of her vast population, which is compared to the roaring of the waves of the sea.   Revelation of John 17:15

title: Jeremiah 51:58
text:
The broad walls--high gates; according to Herodotus, the walls of Babylon were four-square, three hundred and fifty feet high, and eighty-seven thick, with twenty-five gates of solid brass on each side. 
 
  In the fire; or, "for the fire."  They shall gather wealth only to be consumed by fire.

title: Jeremiah 51:61
text: Read all the words; to the captive Jews residing there.

title: Jeremiah 51:64
text:
They shall be weary; the Babylonians shall sink down exhausted and powerless.   Jeremiah 51:58  
 
  Thus far are the words of Jeremiah; the following chapter seems to have been added to the book by some inspired writer, perhaps Ezra.

title: Jeremiah 52:1
text: This chapter is mostly a repetition of  II Kings 24:18-25:30 , where see the notes.

title: Jeremiah 52:27
text: Thus Judah was carried away captive; in the three captivities mentioned in  Jeremiah 52:28-30 .

title: Jeremiah 52:28
text: Three thousand--three and twenty; to these must be added seven thousand soldiers, making the whole number of captives in this first captivity, in round numbers, ten thousand, as in  II Kings 24:14  compared with  II Kings 24:16 .

title: Jeremiah 52:30
text: Seven hundred forty and five--all the persons were four thousand and six hundred; adding the seven thousand soldiers, we have, for the total number of adult males, eleven thousand six hundred. Reckoning women and children, the number may have been fifty thousand or more.

title: Lamentations 1:1
text: The great and terrible reverses that have so often befallen nations for their sins, are standing memorials to the world of God's supreme control over human affairs, and his determination to punish all, however high and powerful, that persist in disobeying him.

title: Lamentations 1:2
text:
Her lovers; her heathen allies. 
 
When God turns to be our enemy, all human helpers and comforters fail us.

title: Lamentations 1:3
text: Between the straits; where escape was impossible.

title: Lamentations 1:4
text: Those calamities are especially to be deplored which interrupt the stated worship of God, and cause the ways of Zion to be unfrequented.

title: Lamentations 1:5
text:
vv 5-6. 
 
It is easy for God to take away, from both princes and people, all strength and counsel, and make them a prey to their enemies.

title: Lamentations 1:7
text: The adversaries saw her, and did mock at her sabbaths; rather, mocked at her desolations.  The word in the original is not the same as that elsewhere used for "sabbath."

title: Lamentations 1:8
text: The way of transgression ends in ignominy; and the dishonor and derision which God brings upon his enemies here, is but an earnest of the "shame and everlasting contempt" which awaits the impenitent in the future world.

title: Lamentations 1:12
text:
vv 12-17. 
 
God attaches supreme value to the holiness of his people, and he regards no infliction of suffering upon churches or individuals as too great which has the effect of purifying them from sin, and making them abound in the fruits of righteousness.

title: Lamentations 1:14
text: They are wreathed; that is, my transgressions, as a chain.

title: Lamentations 1:18
text: In all our sorrows it is both our duty and our privilege to acknowledge our ill desert, and justify God's dealings with us before our fellow men.

title: Lamentations 1:20
text: Is turned within me; is writhed with anguish.

title: Lamentations 1:21
text:
The day that thou hast called; the day of their punishment. 
 
vv 21-22. 
 
Wicked men, instead of exulting over the humiliation which God brings upon his people for their sins, ought to see in it the manifestation of his infinite holiness, which makes their own destruction inevitable.  I Peter 4:17-18

title: Lamentations 2:1
text:
vv 1-10. 
 
None can know the power of God's anger.  The nation that presumes to provoke him by persisting in transgression will find that he is able to visit it with calamity upon calamity, till its resources ae utterly exhausted, and it sinks in hopeless misery and ruin.

title: Lamentations 2:3
text: Hath drawn back his right hand from before the enemy; refused to use it against them, and thus allowed them to prevail.

title: Lamentations 2:6
text: Of a garden; which is only temporary, and is taken away when the fruit is gathered.   Isaiah 1:8

title: Lamentations 2:7
text: As in the day of a solemn feast; the number and tumultuous shouting of the enemy is compared to that of the Israelites assembled at Jerusalem to celebrate their solemn feasts.

title: Lamentations 2:8
text: Stretched out a line; measured out Jerusalem for destruction.  II Kings 21:13 Isaiah 34:11

title: Lamentations 2:11
text:
My liver is poured; that is, my gall; the effect of excessive grief. 
 
As good men are the first to lift up their warning voice against the sins which destroy men's bodies and souls, so are they the first to mourn over the misery which men bring upon themselves by refusing to listen to reproof; they who have been most hated and persecuted for their faithful reproofs, often shed most tears over the calamities which these reproofs were intended to avert.

title: Lamentations 2:12
text: It is a universal law of God's providential government that none sin for themselves alone; they involve those who are connected with them in the consequences of their transgressions.  Especially does this law hold good in the relation of parents to children.   Exodus 20:5

title: Lamentations 2:13
text: What thing--witness for thee; what example can I bring that shall meet thy case, and thus be a source of consolation to thee?

title: Lamentations 2:14
text:
Not discovered thine iniquity, to turn away thy captivity; not declared to thee faithfully thine iniquity, that so, by bringing thee to repentance, they might prevent thy captivity. 
 
  False burdens and causes of banishment; pretended communications from God, that flattered men in sin by lying words, and so became causes of banishment.  But others render, "false burdens and seductions," that is, seducing prophecies. 
 
The worst enemies of both nations and individuals are "false prophets," who flatter sinners with the hope of impunity in sin, instead of faithfully warning them of its guilt and ruin.

title: Lamentations 2:15
text:
vv 15-19. 
 
Good men mourn over the calamities which befall God's people, and pour out their hearts in prayer for their removal; but wicked men exult over them, and make them the occasion of blaspheming God's name.  By this test the friends and the enemies of God may be known.

title: Lamentations 2:22
text: Hast called--my terors round about; hast called together terrors against me on every side, as men are called together in a solemn feast.

title: Lamentations 3:1
text:
The subject of this chapter is the prophet's own afflictions in connection with his prophetical office, and the calamities which befell his country. 
 
vv 1-36. 
 
In times of great corruption and accompanying public calamity, they whom God has set for the defence of the truth, are often exposed to persecution and reproach; and when they receive no present fruit of their faithful labors, but only protracted suffering, they are strongly tempted to indulge in despondency and unavailing lamentations; but in such dark times God is accomplishing his own wise and good ends through the ministry of his word, and his servants who "hope and quietly wait" for him, shall see his salvation.

title: Lamentations 3:4
text: Hath broken my bones; crushed and overwhelmed my spirit with affliction.  Compare  Isaiah 38:13 .

title: Lamentations 3:5
text: Builded against me; builded ramparts against me as against a besieged city.

title: Lamentations 3:8
text: Shutteth out my prayer; delays answering it, as if he had refused to hear it.

title: Lamentations 3:9
text:
Inclosed my ways with hewn stone; imprisoned me within walls of hewn stone; that is, shut up every way of escape. 
 
  Made my paths crooked; led me into perplexity and difficulty.

title: Lamentations 3:11
text: Turned aside my ways; seen note on  Lamentations 3:9 .

title: Lamentations 3:14
text: A derision;  Jeremiah 20:1

title: Lamentations 3:19
text: Remembering; rather, "Remember thou."

title: Lamentations 3:21
text: This; that the Lord's mercies fail not.   Lamentations 3:22-23

title: Lamentations 3:27
text:
Bear the yoke; have trials laid upon him for his discipline, and the purification of his corrupt nature. 
 
  In his youth; this was the case with Jeremiah.  Compare  Jeremiah 1:6-8 .

title: Lamentations 3:28
text:
vv 28-30. 
 
  He sitteth--he is filled; or, "that he should sit," etc.; that is, it is good that he should bear the trials enumerated in these verses.

title: Lamentations 3:37
text: God's control over all human affairs is unlimited; no counsel of men can be accomplished which is contrary to his high purpose.

title: Lamentations 3:40
text:
vv 40-41. 
 
In the deepest affliction it is good to remember that God chastens us less than our iniquities deserve, and that we have occasion, not for complaint, but for adoring gratitude.  This view will lead to earnest self-examination and repentance, and thus to the restoration of God's favor.

title: Lamentations 3:42
text:
vv 42-47. 
 
In our meditations and prayers, we should not separate the sufferings which come upon us and upon God's people, from the sins which have been the occason of them, but should unite humble confession with our complaints and supplications.

title: Lamentations 3:48
text:
vv 48-51. 
 
Good men do not confine their prayers and complaints before God to their own personal trials and sufferings: with them the common welfare of their country, and especially of God's church, are objects of the deepest solicitude.

title: Lamentations 3:53
text:
vv 53-54. 
 
  In the dungeon--I am cut off; Jeremiah probably refers to his various imprisonments.   Jeremiah 37:15-16 Jeremiah 38:6   Yet his language must be, in part at least, figurative.

title: Lamentations 3:55
text:
vv 55-57. 
 
In times of the deepest gloom, when earthly helpers have failed us, God is present to hear and save, and we never call upon him in vain.

title: Lamentations 3:56
text: At my breathing; or, "for my enlargement."

title: Lamentations 3:58
text:
vv 58-66. 
 
All the injuries which God's servants receive for the truth's sake he regards as done to himself, and he will visit them with a heavy retribution.

title: Lamentations 3:63
text:
Their sitting down, and their rising up; that is, their whole demeanor towards me,  Psalms 139:2 , which is that of mockery and derision. 
 
  Music; an object of derisive songs.

title: Lamentations 4:1
text:
How is the gold become dim! how is the glory of Jerusalem, and the honor in which her people were once held, turned to shame. 
 
vv 1-2. 
 
They who honor God by obeying his commands, shall be exalted by him to true honor and strength; but all who despise him, and trample under foot his law, he will make weak and contemptible before their fellow men.   I Samuel 2:30

title: Lamentations 4:3
text: Is become cruel; hunger has driven her to cruel deeds.  Lamentations 4:10

title: Lamentations 4:5
text: The ease and frequency with which God's judgments reach the high and luxurious, reducing them to a condition of extreme want and wretchedness, ought to be a warning to all parents against the common error of bringing up children in habits of luxury and self-indulgence. Such habits not only tempt to sin in many ways, but disqualify them for the endurance of those hardships which, amid the many vicissitudes of life, will very probably fall to their lot.

title: Lamentations 4:7
text: Nazarites; persons specially consecrated or set apart.  For the law of the Nazarites, see  Numbers 6:1-21 .  They were in high honor with the people, and paid especial attention to purity of person.

title: Lamentations 4:10
text: The unnatural cruelty to which the horrors of famine so often impelled Jewish mothers, was a striking fulfilment of God's prophetic denunciations by Moses,  Leviticus 26:29 Deuteronomy 28:53-57 ; at the same time it showed the weakness of mere natural affection to resist the pressure of extreme suffering.

title: Lamentations 4:14
text:
They have wandered; the prophets and priests, with the people whom they had seduced into sin. 
 
  With blood; the blood of the people of Jerusalem slaughtered by the enemy to avenge the righteous blood which they had shed.  Compare  Revelation of John 16:6 .  The city was so filled with this, that the living could not avoid polluting their garments with it.

title: Lamentations 4:15
text:
They cried; all whom they met. 
 
  Depart ye; that is, keep at a distance from us as unclean. 
 
  Fled away and wandered; from their own land into captivity. 
 
  Sojourn there; dwell in their own land.

title: Lamentations 4:16
text:
Divided; dispersed.   Genesis 49:7  
 
  They respected not; that is, the enemy.

title: Lamentations 4:17
text: A nation; Egypt.   Jeremiah 37:7

title: Lamentations 4:20
text:
The breath of our nostrils, the anointed of the Lord; our king.  He is called the breath of their nostrils because their life as a nation is bound up in his. 
 
  Taken in their pits; like a wild beast.   Jeremiah 52:9  
 
  Under his shadow--among the heathen; there had been two previous capitivities, and many of the Jews were already dispersed among the heathen.  So long as Zedekiah remained at peace with Nebuchadnezzar, they trusted to his influence to secure them from oppression.

title: Lamentations 4:21
text:
Rejoice and be glad; that is, if thou wilt; but thy joy shall be short. 
 
  The cup; the cup of God's wrath. 
 
vv 21-22. 
 
God chastises his own people for their profit, not for their destruction; the calamities that come upon them will be in due time overpast; but the enemies of Zion, who desire her destruction, and rejoice in her misfortunes, shall fall to rise no more.

title: Lamentations 4:22
text: Is accomplished; that is, shall soon be accomplished.

title: Lamentations 5:1
text:
In the darkest days of adversity, when all around us is gloom and desolation, we ought still to maintain our confidence in God, and to seek his presence and salvation by humble confession and supplication, united with sincere repentance and obedience.  If we do this, we may rest assured that our present sorrows, and those of God's people, will end in joy and gladness, even as God, at the appointed time, turned again the captivity of the Jews and restored them to their own land. 
 
The darkest eras in the history of both churches and individuals, often prove to be the seed-time of a glorious future harvest of holiness and prosperity.

title: Lamentations 5:6
text:
Given the hand; yielded up ourselves. 
 
  Assyrians; here used for the Chaldeans, of whose empire Assyria was now a part.  The Jews were at this time partly in Egypt, and partly under the Chaldeans.   Jeremiah 44:1

title: Lamentations 5:7
text: Our fathers--borne their iniquities; a common proverb among the Jews,  Jeremiah 31:29 Ezekiel 18:2 ; here used of the children who had imitated the sins of their fathers.  Compare  Exodus 20:5 .

title: Ezekiel 1:1
text:
In the thirtieth year; this was also "the fifth year of king Jehoiachin's captivity,"  Ezekiel 1:2 , and consequently the fifth year of Zedekiah's reign, or five hundred and ninety-five years before Christ.  Reckoning back from this date thirty years, we come to the eighteenth year of Josiah, when he repaired the temple and solemnly renewed the worship of God; and also to the first year of Nabopolassar, the father of Nebuchadnezzar, who made Babylon independent of the Assyrian monarchy, and thus established a new era.  It is uncertain from which of these events the prophet reckons, but the latter is the most probable. 
 
  Among the captives; whom Nebuchadnezzar had carried away with Jehoiachin.   II Kings 24:10-16  
 
  The river of Chebar; generally supposed to be the stream which now bears the name of Khabour, a river of Mesopotamia flowing into the Euphrates from the north-east.  But this is not absolutely certain. 
 
  The heavens were opened; to impart divine revelations.  Compare  Matthew 3:16 Acts 10:11 Revelation of John 4:1 Revelation of John 19:11 . 
 
vv 1-3. 
 
God was with his ancient people in captivity, and revealed himself to them there for their warning, instruction, and consolation; so his is with his churches now in the darkest days of adversity and sorrow, preparing them, if they will listen to his voice, for returning prosperity and gladness.

title: Ezekiel 1:3
text: The hand of the Lord--upon him; the same as, "the Spirit of God came upon him," enabling him to prophesy.  Compare  II Kings 3:15 .

title: Ezekiel 1:4
text:
Whirlwind--great cloud--fire; the symbols of God's presence,  Exodus 19:16-18 Job 38:1 Psalms 50:3 . 
 
  Infolding itself; forming a continuous rolling mass. 
 
  Amber; here a compound metal of great brillancy. 
 
vv 4-28. 
 
All the powers of heaven and earth are from God as their author, and at his absolute disposal as their governor, to do whatsoever he will: nothing can thwart or hinder the execution of his purposes.  Psalms 115:3 Psalms 135:6 Matthew 26:53

title: Ezekiel 1:5
text:
Came; that is, appeared.  The word is supplied by the translators. 
 
  They had the likeness of a man; their general form was that of a man with four faces.

title: Ezekiel 1:7
text: Like the sole of a calf's foot; rounded on every side alike, so that no one part was more front than another, and they could move in every direction without turning.  Compare   Ezekiel 1:9 Ezekiel 1:12 Ezekiel 1:1

title: Ezekiel 1:8
text: The hands of a man--on their four sides; each had four hands, one under each of his four wings.

title: Ezekiel 1:9
text:
Joined one to another; their position was four-square, each having one wing opposite to the wing of his fellow on two sides; these two opposite wings were stretched forth so as to meet each other. 
 
  They turned not when they went; they went every one straight forward; they had each four fronts, and the figure which they formed had also four fronts, so that they could move alike in every direction without turning.  This denotes their absolute readiness to execute the divine will, whithersoever it required them to go.

title: Ezekiel 1:10
text: They four had the face of a man--the face of an eagle; by a change of punctuation this passage will be made clearer, thus: "They four had the face of a man; and the face of a lion on the right side: and they four had the face of an ox," etc.  All four had the face of a man in front, that is, on the south, since the vision came from the north; the face of an eagle in the rear; the face of a lion on the right side, and of an ox on the left.  The four faces, corresponding to the four principal divisions of living creatures among the Hebrews, seem to represent the fulness of their endowments.

title: Ezekiel 1:11
text: Covered their bodies; a token of reverence.

title: Ezekiel 1:12
text: Whither the spirit was to go, they went; one spirit animated both the living creatures and the wheels, so that they all moved together.

title: Ezekiel 1:14
text:
Ran and returned; that is, moved all together with the wheels and firmament above them. 
 
  As the appearance--lightning; in respect to both brightness and velocity.

title: Ezekiel 1:15
text:
By the living creatures; that is, by each of the four. 
 
  With his four faces; see note on  Ezekiel 1:10 .

title: Ezekiel 1:16
text: A wheel in the middle of a wheel; a second wheel at right angles with the first. Thus the four half circles made four faces or sides.

title: Ezekiel 1:17
text:
Went upon their four sides; went in the direction of any one of their four sides, whithersoever the spirit directed them. 
 
  Turned not; the prophet does not mean that they did not revolve, but that having four sides, they moved every way without the necessity of turning about to change their course.

title: Ezekiel 1:18
text:
Rings; rims, felloes. 
 
  Full of eyes; denoting intelligence.  The wheels were prevaded by the spirit of the living creatures,  Ezekiel 1:20 .  The meaning is, that all the movements of divine Providence are pervaded and directed by infinite intelligence.

title: Ezekiel 1:22
text:
Living creature; here used collectively of the four. 
 
  The terrible crystal; dazzling and amazing by its splendor.

title: Ezekiel 1:23
text: Straight; stretched out horizontally so as to touch each other,  Ezekiel 1:9 .

title: Ezekiel 1:24
text: Let down their wings; as ceasing to fly.

title: Ezekiel 1:26
text: Above the firmament--appearance of a man; compare  Exodus 24:10 .

title: Ezekiel 1:28
text:
The bow;  Revelation of John 4:3 Revelation of John 10:1 
  The glory of the Lord; the prophet saw in vision the Lord enthroned in glory upon the firmament above the cherubim.  The cherubim with their wheels, moving every way like a flash of lightning, seem to denote all the agencies by which God administers his government over the world, which are absolutely at his command, and execute with unerring certainty all his high purposes.

title: Ezekiel 2:1
text: I will speak unto thee; the prophet now receives his commission.

title: Ezekiel 2:3
text:
vv 3-5. 
 
God's servants must deliver his messages to the rebellious and stiff-hearted, as well as to the obedient; not omitting any part of them through fear of persecution, but holding themselves ever ready after the example of their great Master, to suffer reproach and persecution for their fidelity to the truth.

title: Ezekiel 2:6
text: Wicked men show their enmity to God's truth by persecuting those who proclaim it: the faithful preacher must expect to find them briers and thorns in his side and scorpions in his path; but if he puts his trust in God and does his duty, he will be delivered from all their evil devices.

title: Ezekiel 2:9
text: A roll of a book; a book in the form of a roll, after the ancient custom.

title: Ezekiel 2:10
text:
Spread it; by unrolling it. 
 
  Within and without; that is, on both sides, to denote the fulness of its contents.  Compare  Revelation of John 5:1 .  Rolls were generally written only on the inner side. 
 
For those who persist in sin, God has no messages but those of evil.  I Kings 22:8 Psalms 11:6 Isaiah 3:11

title: Ezekiel 3:1
text: Eat this roll; this symbol denotes the inward willing reception of the prophetical messages committed to him.  Compare  Ezekiel 3:10 .

title: Ezekiel 3:3
text:
As honey for sweetness; he received the divine revelations with holy delight, although their contents of "lamentations, and mourning, and woe" were bitter to him.  Compare  Revelation of John 10:9-10 . 
 
That we may be prepared to proclaim God's truth to others, we must first receive it with holy obedience and joy into our own hearts, and make it our daily food and strength.

title: Ezekiel 3:5
text:
Of a strange speech--a hard language; that is, speaking a foreign tongue unintelligible to him. 
 
In the work of making known God's truth to our own neighbors and countrymen we enjoy many advantages above the foreign missionary, who goes to people of strange customs and a strange speech; these advantages ought to excite us to great zeal and diligence in the performance of this duty.

title: Ezekiel 3:6
text:
They would have hearkened; compare  Matthew 11:21-24 . 
 
vv 6-7. 
 
None are so hardhearted and desperately wicked as those who have enjoyed and abused great religious privileges.   Matthew 11:20-24

title: Ezekiel 3:8
text:
vv 8-9. 
 
When God appoints his servants to any work, he gives them the strength and grace which they need for its performance.

title: Ezekiel 3:12
text:
Took me up; "lifted me up between the earth and the heaven," and took me away to Tel-abib; compare  Ezekiel 3:14  and 8.3.  This, however, was not bodily, but in prophetic vision; for he afterwards went thither by his own proper act, as is plain from  Ezekiel 3:11 Ezekiel 3:15 . The vision indicated a duty which he immediately performed. 
 
  A voice of a great rushing; the sound of the cherubim and wheels in motion, for "whithersoever the spirit was to go, they went."  Ezekiel 1:20

title: Ezekiel 3:13
text: The noise of the wings; compare  Ezekiel 10:5 .

title: Ezekiel 3:14
text:
I went in bitterness, in the heat of my spirit; full of grief and holy anger.  The spirit of prophecy brought his feelings towards his countrymen into harmony with those of God. 
 
A burning zeal for the glory of God, united with "great heaviness" of heart in view of men's perverseness and rebellion, have been in all ages the marks of God's true servants.  Exodus 32:19 Exodus 32:20 Exodus 32:31 Exodus 32:32 Psalms 119:136 Jeremiah 9:1 Jeremiah 9:2 Jeremiah 20:9 John 2:17 Romans 9:1-3

title: Ezekiel 3:15
text:
Astonished; in view of the solemn office committed to me. 
 
Silent meditation and prayer are among the best means of preparation for a great and difficult service.   Acts 9:8 Acts 9:9 Acts 9:11 Acts 9:15

title: Ezekiel 3:16
text: At the end of seven days; Ezekiel, like Saul of Tarsus, was left, for a period after his call, to his own meditations.

title: Ezekiel 3:17
text:
vv 17-21. 
 
God holds the preacher responsible for the faithful delivery of his messages: when this is done, it is both the preacher's duty and his privilege to leave the consequences with God.

title: Ezekiel 3:20
text: A stumbling-block; any occasion of sin which comes to men through God's providence for their trial.

title: Ezekiel 3:25
text: They shall put bands upon thee; that is, thou shalt be bound at my command.  This is probably to be understood figuratively of a divine restraint at certain times from the exercise of the prophetical office, as is explained in the following verses.

title: Ezekiel 3:26
text:
vv 26-27. 
 
  Will make thy tongue cleave--when I speak; he is to keep silence, except when God's Spirit moves him to speak; the perverseness of he people makes this reserve necessary. 
 
God sometimes, in his displeasure, withdraws his admonitions from the perverse and incorrigible, and leaves them to their own ways.  Isaiah 1:5

title: Ezekiel 4:1
text:
A tile; the large tiles of Babylon were commonly used for inscriptions and drawings. 
 
When nations and cities refuse to be corrected by God's chastisements, he will multiply his judgments against them until they are utterly destroyed.  No human power can avail to loose the bands which he lays upon the workers of iniquity.

title: Ezekiel 4:2
text: Lay siege against it; that is, portray a siege.  The final siege of Jerusalem is here meant.  Ezekiel began to prophesy in the fifth year of Zedekiah; consequently six years before the last capture of the city by Nebuchadnezzar.  With the exception of his vision of the temple,  Ezekiel 40:1-48:23 , the great body of his prophecies was delivered during the intervening period.  It is not till  Ezekiel 33:21  that he records his reception of the news that the city was smitten.

title: Ezekiel 4:3
text: For a wall of iron; this seems to be a symbol of God's wrath arrayed against Jerusalem in the form of a siege.  For the meaning of iron as a symbol, see  Daniel 2:40 .

title: Ezekiel 4:4
text:
vv 4-6. 
 
  Lie thou; the prophet himself now represents the people of Israel and Judah. 
 
  The years of their iniquity--the number of the days; the meaning is, that each day represents a year. 
 
  Three hundred and ninety days--forty days; the interpretation of these numbers is uncertain. According to some, the forty days correspond to the forty years' wandering of the Israelites in the wilderness, and the sum of the two numbers, four hundred and thirty days, to the four hundred and thirty years of servitude in Egypt,  Exodus 12:40 ; meaning that God will repeat to his covenant people the chastisements inflicted upon their fathers.  Others understand by the three hundred and ninety days, the three hundred and ninety years from the establishment of idolatry in Israel by Jeroboam to the destruction of Jerusalem by Nebuchadnezzar; and by the forty days, forty of the last years of the kingdom of Judah, when idolatry abounded in it.

title: Ezekiel 4:7
text: Uncovered; as ready for hostile action against Jerusalem.  Here, as in  Ezekiel 4:1-3 , the prophet acts as God's representative.

title: Ezekiel 4:8
text: Lay bands upon thee; to signify that Judah and Israel cannot escape the coming judgments which the prophet thus represents.

title: Ezekiel 4:10
text:
vv 10-11. 
 
  By weight--by measure; a scanty allowance of food and drink, dealt out by weight and measure, as in time of famine.  A shekel was something more than half an ounce; a hin was about ten pints.

title: Ezekiel 4:12
text: With dung; that is, dung for fuel; indicating the extreme scarcity of fuel in the city.  By using this unclean substance for fuel, the bread itself would become defiled, that is, unclean, according to the distinctions of the Mosaic law.  Compare  Ezekiel 4:14 .

title: Ezekiel 4:15
text: Cow's dung; a common fuel in eastern countries.

title: Ezekiel 5:2
text: Burn with fire--smite about it--scatter in the wind; the meaning of these symbols is explained in  Ezekiel 5:12 .

title: Ezekiel 5:3
text:
Bind them in thy skirts; a sign of God's preserving care. 
 
vv 3-4. 
 
In the severity of God's dealings with the remnant of his ancient people, we have at once an affecting proof of the desperate wickedness of the human heart, which makes so much suffering necessary, and also a solemn pledge of God's purpose to purify his church from time to time, and make her fruitful in righteousness to the glory of his own name.

title: Ezekiel 5:4
text: Take of them again; take some ot the hairs bound in thy skirt.  The remnant that is spared needs a new purification.  See note on  Isaiah 6:13 .

title: Ezekiel 5:5
text:
vv 5-17. 
 
God has set his people for the light of the world; he would have them, by their holy example, bring their fellow men to the knowledge and obedience of the truth.  When they change his judgments into wickedness, and become leaders in sin to the world without, he will punish them with a severity proportioned to their guilt, and make them "a reproach and a taunt, an instruction and an astonishment" to those who are about them, that all may learn to fear his holy name.

title: Ezekiel 5:6
text: Changed my judgments into wickedness; or, "wickedly rebelled against my judgments."

title: Ezekiel 5:7
text: According to the judgments of the nations; they had not adhered as steadfastly to the worship of the true God, as the nations did to their idols.  Compare  Jeremiah 2:11 .

title: Ezekiel 5:13
text: Be comforted; by the manifestation of my justice towards them.

title: Ezekiel 5:15
text: It shall be; that is, my dealing with thee shall make thee a reproach, etc., thus manifesting the evil of sin, and how fearful a thing it is to fall under God's displeasure.

title: Ezekiel 6:3
text:
Rivers; beds of torrents, which are dry except in the rainy season. 
 
  High places; for sacrificing to idols.

title: Ezekiel 6:5
text: In the punishment of sinners, God will so order events as to make the folly of their vain confidences manifest to all men.   Ezekiel 6:13

title: Ezekiel 6:6
text: Your idols may be broken--abolished; the object of these severe judgments is here given, the extirpation of idolatry.

title: Ezekiel 6:9
text:
vv 9-10. 
 
When God's chastisements have brought us to see ourselves as he sees us, and to loathe ourselves for the evils which we have done, they have accomplished their proper object, and he will soon remove them.

title: Ezekiel 6:12
text:
Far off; from the invading army. 
 
  Remaineth; in the city.  No situation shall secure the sinful people from God's wrath.

title: Ezekiel 6:14
text: Diblath; perhaps the same as Dablathaim,  Jeremiah 48:22 ; according to some, Riblah, on the north-eastern border of Palestine.

title: Ezekiel 7:1
text:
vv 1-13. 
 
God bears long with sinners, "not willing that any should perish, but that all should come to repentance;" yet if they persist in disregarding his warnings, he will execute upon them all his threatened judgments without mitigation.

title: Ezekiel 7:4
text: Thine abominations shall be; that is, the recompense of thine abominations shall come.

title: Ezekiel 7:6
text: Watcheth for thee; or waketh up against thee, as an enemy intent on thy destruction.

title: Ezekiel 7:7
text:
The morning; the morning of the day of trouble.  So also  Ezekiel 7:10 . 
 
  Not the sounding again of the mountains; the resounding of the mountains with joyous shouts.  It is a cry of trouble, and not of gladness.

title: Ezekiel 7:10
text: Pride hath budded; into a rod.  The pride and violence of the people have grown into a rod which Jehovah will use to punish their wickedness.  Compare  Proverbs 5:22 .

title: Ezekiel 7:12
text: Buyer rejoice--seller mourn; because in the approaching day of captivity buyer and seller will be alike poor and miserable.

title: Ezekiel 7:13
text:
Return to that which is sold; return at the year of the jubilee to the possession of his inheritance which he has sold.  Leviticus 25:10 Leviticus 25:25-28  
 
  Although they were yet alive; although the sellers were yet alive at the year of jubilee; for the land shall be in the possession of the enemy.  This is added to make the picture of the desolation of the land complete. 
 
  Is touching the whole multitude thereof; threatens not a partial, but a universal devastation of the land.

title: Ezekiel 7:14
text:
They have blown the trumpet; the Jewish leaders, to summon the people to battle against their enemies. 
 
  None goeth to the battle; God's wrath has taken from the people all their courage.   Ezekiel 7:17  
 
When God will destroy a people for their iniquity, he takes from them courage and counsel in the day of trouble, and gives them up to terror and confusion.   Ezekiel 7:17

title: Ezekiel 7:16
text: Like doves of the valleys; with allusion to the mourning noise of doves.   Isaiah 38:14 Isaiah 59:11

title: Ezekiel 7:19
text:
Cast their silver in the streets; in their flight. 
 
  Shall be removed; or, "shall become an unclean thing;" that is, be cast away as an unclean thing. 
 
  Satisfy their souls; with their wealth.  God's judgments shall reduce rich and poor to a common level. 
 
The wealth of wicked men is no protection against God's judgments. With infinite ease he can destroy them and their possessions together.

title: Ezekiel 7:20
text:
The beauty of his ornament; the temple, or the land of Palestine, which was "the glory of all lands." 
 
  He set it; God set it. 
 
  Set it far from them; or, "made it to them an unclean thing." Compare  Ezekiel 7:22 .

title: Ezekiel 7:22
text:
From them; from my people. 
 
  They shall pollute; the robbers immediately mentioned; that is, foreign enemies. 
 
  My secret place; my sanctuary. 
 
vv 22-25. 
 
God would not spare his ancient people when they sinned against him, on account of their "holy and beautiful temple," with its divinely appointed ordinances; neither will he spare unfaithful churches now, on account of their outward relations and privileges.   Jeremiah 7:4 Jeremiah 7:12-15

title: Ezekiel 7:23
text: Make a chain; or binding the rebellious Jews and leading them into captivity.

title: Ezekiel 7:26
text: They who will not listen when God graciously calls them to repentance and obedience, shall call upon him in the time of trouble, but receive no answer.   Proverbs 1:24-28

title: Ezekiel 8:1
text:
In the sixth year; of Jehoiachin's captivity,  Ezekiel 1:2 . 
 
vv 1-14. 
 
God's holy eyes continually behold all the abominations which are practised by the wicked in secret places; and so far as he chooses, he reveals them to the view of others.

title: Ezekiel 8:2
text:
A likeness; "a likeness as the appearance of a man,"  Ezekiel 1:26 . 
 
  Amber; see note to  Ezekiel 1:4 .

title: Ezekiel 8:3
text:
In the visions of God; he was carried to Jerusalem only in a vision, not bodily; but the idolatrous rites there represented to him actually existed. 
 
  The inner gate; next to the temple lay the inner court, or court of the priests; then the outer, or court of the Israelites.  The gate here named seems to have led from the inner to the outer court on the north side; but the exact determination of the various localities named in this chapter is difficult.

title: Ezekiel 8:11
text: Ancients; elders, who ought to have been foremost in maintaining the purity of God's worship.

title: Ezekiel 8:14
text: Women weeping for Tammuz; Tammuz answers to the Adonis of the Greeks, a deified mortal, whose death the women annually lamented with idolatrous rites.

title: Ezekiel 8:16
text:
The inner court; that of the priests, whence it appears that these men were priests. 
 
  Their backs toward the temple--worshipped the sun; the priests were appointed by God to minister at his altar, and intercede with him for the people.   Joel 2:17   That these should worship the sun, with their backs towards God's temple, was the crowning act of wickedness.

title: Ezekiel 8:17
text:
Put the branch to their nose; after the manner of the ancient Parsees, who worshipped the rising sun holding in their left hand a bundle of twigs. 
 
vv 17-18. 
 
When they who are set for the defence of true religion become leaders of the people in superstition and wickedness, the community becomes speedily corrupted in every part, and ripe for God's desolating judgments.

title: Ezekiel 9:1
text:
Cause them that have charge over the city--weapon in his hand; that is, the destroying angels charged to execute my wrath upon it; these, however, represent here not so much literal angels, as all the ministries and agencies which God employs to execute punishment upon the wicked. 
 
In the most corrupt periods, God has a faithful remnant who sigh and cry for the abominations that surround them; he knows the names of all of these, and is abundantly able to protect and deliver them while he destroys his enemies.  But the perfect separation of the righteous from the wicked is reserved for the last great day, when every one of his friends shall receive complete and eternal salvation, and all his enemies be destroyed utterly and for ever.

title: Ezekiel 9:2
text:
Toward the north; where the seat of idolatry is, there also the punishment begins. 
 
  One man among them; a seventh man among these six.

title: Ezekiel 9:3
text:
Was gone up; the temple was Jehovah's earthly dwelling-place; and here he presides over the execution of his judgments. 
 
  The cherub; here, and in  Ezekiel 10:2 Ezekiel 10:4 , used collectively of the four cherubim.  These are the same as the "living creatures,"  Ezekiel 1:1-28 .

title: Ezekiel 9:4
text: Set a mark; that the destroying angels may recognize them and spare them.  There seems to be an allusion here to the mark of blood on the houses of the Israelites in Egypt,  Exodus 12:22-23 .

title: Ezekiel 9:6
text: Begin at my sanctuary; the sanctuary was the dwelling-place of God's holiness; thence the judgment proceeded, and it fell first upon those who were nearest to God in their official character, and also first in guilt.  Compare  I Peter 4:17 .

title: Ezekiel 10:1
text: God is ever present among his people, disposing all the events which befall them to his own glory and the advancement of the cause of righteousness; the most terrible calamities come immediately from his hand, and are directed by his providence.  It is his will that we recognize him alike in mercies and judgments, and act habitually under a sense of his presence and absolute power to save or to destroy.

title: Ezekiel 10:2
text:
Under the cherub; that is, under the wings and hands of the four cherubim which were above the wheels. 
 
  Coals of fire--scatter them; a symbol of the pouring out of God's wrath upon Jerusalem.  Compare  Revelation of John 8:5 .

title: Ezekiel 10:3
text: The right side; that is, the south, as the temple faced the east. Thus the prophet's view of the threshold was unobstructed.

title: Ezekiel 10:4
text:
Went up from the cherub; see note on  Ezekiel 9:3 . 
 
  The court; the inner court,  Ezekiel 10:3 .

title: Ezekiel 10:5
text: To the outer court; where the prophet was stationed, for he could not stand in the inner court by reason of the cloud.  Compare  I Kings 8:11 Revelation of John 15:8 .

title: Ezekiel 10:8
text: Under their wings; one under each wing.

title: Ezekiel 10:13
text: O wheel; they were addressed as possessing intelligence, and able to obey God's command.  Compare  Ezekiel 1:21 .

title: Ezekiel 10:14
text:
Every one; of the cherubim. 
 
  The face of a cherub; this answers to "the face of an ox," in  Ezekiel 1:10 .  Hence some have inferred that the cherubim over the ark of the covenant had the face of an ox.  These cherubim were symbolic beings, and not real angels.

title: Ezekiel 10:20
text: The living creature; that is, the fourfold living creature.

title: Ezekiel 11:1
text: Five and twenty men; these seem to represent the rulers of Judah.

title: Ezekiel 11:2
text:
vv 2-3. 
 
Carnal security and contempt of God's threatenings prepare the way for wicked counsels and mischievous devices.

title: Ezekiel 11:3
text:
It is not near; the destruction of Jerusalem threatened by Jeremiah.  But we may better render the first clause by of the verse thus: "The time is not near to build houses," that is, in Babylon, according to the advice of Jeremiah.   Jeremiah 29:5   They scornfully reject the idea of a long captivity in Babylon. 
 
  This city is the caldron, and we be the flesh; as the flesh remains in the caldron till cooked, so we shall remain till death in Jerusalem. We shall not be removed prematurely by captivity.  Compare  Ezekiel 11:7 Ezekiel 11:9 Ezekiel 11:11 , where God threatens to bring them out of Jerusalem.

title: Ezekiel 11:6
text:
vv 6-12. 
 
God has appointed rulers for the defence of the innocent and the punishment of the guilty.  When they become the oppressors and destroyers of the people, he will take the cause of justice into his own hands, and destroy them and their possessions together.

title: Ezekiel 11:7
text:
Your slain--are the flesh; Jehovah gives a new turn to their figure.  The city boiling with violence and bloodshed is the caldron, and the murdered are the flesh in it. 
 
  Bring you forth; that is, violently and prematurely.

title: Ezekiel 11:10
text: In the border of Israel; the princes of Judah were slain at Riblah, on the borders of Palestine.   Jeremiah 52:10

title: Ezekiel 11:13
text:
Died; the prophet sees in vision the death of Pelatiah, a leader among the Jewish princes--a sure token that they shall all be destroyed. 
 
We ought to be filled with fear and trembling in view of God's threatenings, knowing that he will execute them upon all who persevere in sin, without respect of persons.

title: Ezekiel 11:15
text:
Thy brethren--the men of they kindred; thy fellow-captives of the Jewish nation. 
 
  Get you far from the Lord; literslly, "Be far from the Lord." Those who remain in Jerusalem despise their countrymen who have gone into captivity, as far removed from God's presence, and no longer the objects of his care.  But God assures the prophet that he will bless the latter, while he destroys the former.  Compare  Jeremiah 24:1-10 . 
 
vv 15-16. 
 
The Jews who remained at Jerusalem in Ezekiel's day, gloried in their outward privileges and relations to God, and despised their brethren who had gone into captivity; but God destroyed the former, while he blessed the latter, and restored them at the appointed time to their own home.  So he deals with man, abasing the proud and exalting the humble.

title: Ezekiel 11:16
text: A little sanctuary; little, answering to the fewness of their number.  Some render, "a sanctuary for a short time," that is, till their return from captivity.

title: Ezekiel 11:17
text:
vv 17-21. 
 
God's own glory is concerned in the perpetuation from age to age of his true worshippers.  The same judgments which destroy the wicked he will make efficacious for the purification of the "remnant according to the election of grace," and their increase in the fruits of righteousness.

title: Ezekiel 11:20
text: My people; the remnant, to whom the promises contained in  Ezekiel 11:20-21  are made, represent "the Israel of God."  The fulfilment of these promises belongs not to any one period of time.  It began in the restoration under Ezra, Zerubbabel, and others, but its full accomplishment belongs to "the last days" of Zion's glory.

title: Ezekiel 11:23
text: The mountain--on the east side of the city; the mount of Olives.

title: Ezekiel 12:2
text: It is not from the want of means to know God's will that sinners perish, but from unwillingness to use the means which he furnishes them.  Their ignorance is voluntary and inexcusable.

title: Ezekiel 12:3
text:
Stuff for removing; literally, "equipments for exile," such as the king and his princes will presently prepare in their flight from Jerusalem,  Ezekiel 12:10-12 . 
 
When one method of admonition fails, we must employ others; not intermitting our efforts to reclaim and save sinners, so long as God prolongs to them the day of grace.

title: Ezekiel 12:5
text: Dig thou through the wall; to represent the flight of the king and his princes.  They fled "by night, by the way of the gate between the two walls, which was by the king's garden,"  Jeremiah 52:7 , doubtless by opening a passage there that had been kept closed during the siege.

title: Ezekiel 12:6
text:
In the twilight; in the darkness of night.  See note on  Ezekiel 12:5 . 
 
  Cover thy face; as a sign of mourning and humiliation.

title: Ezekiel 12:13
text:
My net--will I spread upon him; God's net was the army of the Chaldees, which pursued after him and overtook him.   Jeremiah 52:8  
 
  Bring him to Babylon--yet shall he not see it; remarkably fulfilled in the case of Zedekiah, whose eyes were put out before he was carried to Babylon.   Jeremiah 52:11  
 
Zedekiah enjoyed the faithful instructions of Jeremiah, but he would not listen to them, and therefore all the calamities which the prophet had foretold came upon him.  Led in chains to Babylon with his eyes put out, he became a sad and awful example of the end of those who harden themselves against God's reproofs.

title: Ezekiel 12:14
text: When God is against a sinner, all his human confidences fail him.

title: Ezekiel 12:16
text: May declare all their abominations; the abonimations of their brethren whom God has destroyed, and on account of which they themselves have been carried captive, that thus the heathen may understand the reason of their destruction.

title: Ezekiel 12:22
text:
The days are prolonged; the days for executing the judgments threatened by the prophets. 
 
  Faileth; proves false.  From God's delay they take encouragement to disbelieve his threatenings.   II Peter 3:4  
 
vv 22-28. 
 
God delays the execution of his threatenings, that men may have time for repentance; but they take occasion from this to harden themselves in unbelief and rebellion to their destruction.   Ecclesiastes 8:11 Romans 2:4-5

title: Ezekiel 12:24
text: Vain vision--flattering divination; the flatteries of the false prophets were the chief cause why the predictions of the true prophets were disregarded.  While God destroys the former, he will fulfil the words of the latter.

title: Ezekiel 13:2
text:
vv 2-7. 
 
In all ages of the church, God's true messengers have exposed themselves to reproach and persecution for the truth's sake; while false teachers have made themselves rich and powerful by flattering men in their sins.   Luke 6:22 Luke 6:23 Luke 6:26

title: Ezekiel 13:4
text: Deserts; rather, "ruins," as of walls.

title: Ezekiel 13:5
text:
The gaps; of the broken walls. 
 
  Hedge; here in the sense of a fence, or rampart. 
 
  The day of the Lord; of his wrath upon Israel for their sins. Instead of repairing the broken walls, and standing there for the defence of Israel, they have used them as foxes use ruins, to burrow in; that is, instead of laboring to reform the people, and thus avert from them God's judgments, they have made themselves rich and powerful by flattering them in their sins.

title: Ezekiel 13:6
text: Have made others to hope that they would confirm the word; or, "have made men to hope for the establishment of the word;" that is, of the flattering promises made by them to the people.

title: Ezekiel 13:8
text:
vv 8-16. 
 
No flatteries of corrupt teachers can hinder the execution of God's threatenings against the wicked; and when his judgments come like an overflowing stream, they will sweep away together both the prophets of lies and those who put their trust in them.

title: Ezekiel 13:9
text:
Shall not be in the assembly; because they shall be destroyed by God's judgments. 
 
  Written in the writing; enrolled among those who return from captivity.

title: Ezekiel 13:10
text: Wall--mortar; the wall and the mortar denote the vain plans of the people to escape destruction without repentance and faith in Jehovah, and the encouragement which the false prophets gave to them.

title: Ezekiel 13:17
text:
The daughters of thy people; the false prophetesses are now addressed. 
 
vv 17-21. 
 
The flatteries and seductions of ungodly women exert a great influence to corrupt the faith and practice of communities, and God will punish them in a way corresponding to their sins.   Isaiah 3:1-25

title: Ezekiel 13:18
text:
To all armholes--upon the head of every stature; rather, "or all armholes," "for the heads of every stature," that if, of men of every stature.  The pillows and kerchiefs, (according to some, bolsters,) seem to denote figuratively the flatteries with which they quieted the minds of those who consulted them. 
 
  Hunt the souls; their false prophecies destroyed souls. 
 
  Save the souls alive--unto you; or, "save your own souls alive."

title: Ezekiel 13:19
text:
Pollute me; bring me into dishonor by pretending to prophesy in my name. 
 
  For handfuls of barley--pieces of bread; the wages of these parasites. 
 
  To slay the souls--by your lying; their prophecies strengthened the wicked, and stirred up deadly persecutions against the righteous. Compare  Ezekiel 13:22 .

title: Ezekiel 13:20
text: To make them fly; perhaps, to make them fly away to the other world; but some explain the whole clause thus: I am against your pillows, etc., that I may deliver them, namely, the souls which ye hunt.  This interpretation is favored by the following verse.

title: Ezekiel 13:22
text: The false teacher may be distinguished from the true by the effect of his doctrine, which is to make the heart of the righteous sad, and strengthen the hands of the wicked.

title: Ezekiel 14:1
text: Came certain of the elders of Israel; that is, "to inquire of the Lord."  Compare  Ezekiel 20:1 .

title: Ezekiel 14:3
text:
In their heart--before their face; they loved their idols,and continued to worship them. 
 
  Stumbling-block of their iniquity; this was their idolatry, over which they stumbled to their destruction. 
 
vv 3-8. 
 
God takes no pleasure in the outward form of worship when it is connected with a wicked heart and life.  He cannot be deceived by those who come to inquire of him, and he will not suffer them to mock him by serving himself and idols at the same time.  If they love iniquity and secretly practise it, he will answer them in wrath, and not in mercy.

title: Ezekiel 14:4
text: According to the multitude of his idols; with punishment answerable to his multiplied idolatries.

title: Ezekiel 14:5
text: Take; detect and punish.

title: Ezekiel 14:7
text: By myself; not by a message of words alone, through the prophet, but by deeds, that is, by judgments proceeding from myself.

title: Ezekiel 14:9
text:
The prophet be deceived; the false prophet. 
 
  I the Lord have deceived; given over him and his followers to delusion.  Compare  Psalms 81:11-12 II Thessalonians 2:10-12 . 
 
vv 9-10. 
 
God punishes those who love falsehood rather than truth, by leaving them to believe and follow it to their destruction.  Thus false teachers and their disciples perish together.

title: Ezekiel 14:11
text: That the house of Israel may go no more astray; the destruction of the false prophets and their followers shall result in the purification and prosperity of the surviving remnant.

title: Ezekiel 14:12
text:
vv 12-21. 
 
It is only by hearing and obeying the instructions of righteous men, that either nations or individuals can be profited by them.  They who reject their holy example and wise counsels, bring upon themselves deeper guilt and severer punishment.  Hence we see the folly of trusting to the merits of saints on earth or in heaven, as if these could take the place of our own personal repentance and faith in Christ.

title: Ezekiel 14:14
text:
Daniel; he had now been fourteen years in captivity, from the third year of Jehoiakim, who reigned eleven years, to the sixth of Zedekiah.  Ezekiel 8:1 Daniel 1:1 2zki 23.36| All the prophecies  Ezekiel 8:1-19:14 , were delivered during the sixth year of Zedekiah. 
 
  Deliver but their own souls; the people must not hope for deliverance in their impenitence and rebellion against God for the sake of the few eminently pious among them.

title: Ezekiel 14:19
text: In blood; that is, in the destruction of life.

title: Ezekiel 14:22
text:
Be brought forth; from Jerusalem, to join the captives among whom Ezekiel dwells. 
 
  Comforted concerning the evil--upon Jerusalem; by seeing its justice, and acquiescing in it. 
 
vv 22-23. 
 
Sinners are generally blind to their own wickedness, and therefore disposed to justify themselves, and complain of God's severity; but all whose hearts are right can see in their character and conduct the justice of God's dealings.

title: Ezekiel 14:23
text: Comfort you; be the occasion of your being comforted.

title: Ezekiel 15:1
text: God values his churches, not for their worldly wealth, rank, or influence, but for their fruits of holiness.  When these fail, they become abominable in his sight, and he casts them out of his favor, and gives them over to weakness and ruin.

title: Ezekiel 15:2
text: What is the vine-tree more than any tree; the value of the vine lies in its fruit.  When this ceases, or is changed into "wild grapes,"  Isaiah 5:2 , it becomes the most worthless of all trees.  So the excellence of God's people consisted in their fruits of righteousness. When these were changed to iniquity, they became as fuel fit for the burning.  Compare  John 15:1-6 .

title: Ezekiel 15:5
text:
When it was whole; when Israel remained unbroken, as in the days of David and Solomon. 
 
  Was meet for no work; was valuable only as bearing fruit. 
 
  When the fire hath devoured it; an allusion to the destruction of Israel, which was already complete, and that of Judah, which was now in progress.

title: Ezekiel 16:1
text: In this chapter Jerusalem is set forth under the allegory of a lewd woman.  Her history represents the whole history of God's covenant people from the beginning.

title: Ezekiel 16:3
text:
