Thy birth and thy nativity is of the land of Canaan; the Jews gloried in their descent from Abraham; but their history proved them to have been from the beginning Canaanites in character. 
 
  Thy father was an Amorite, and thy mother a Hittite; Jerusalem is described as a Canaanite on the side of both parents, that is, of unmixed Canaanitish descent.  The Canaanitish tribes are chosen to represent her origin, because these were the vilest of the heathen, and devoted by God to destruction.  The great truth which this allegory teaches is, that no human descent can give holiness of heart and a title to God's favor.  "That which is born of the flesh is flesh."  John 1:13 John 3:6

title: Ezekiel 16:4
text: Thy nativity--nor swaddled; the words describe the birth of a wretched infant, cast out and ready to perish.

title: Ezekiel 16:5
text:
vv 5-6. 
 
  None eye pitied thee--I said unto thee--Live; in themselves, the Israelites were from the beginning utterly helpless; all the privileges which distinguished them from their heathen neighbors were God's free gift.   Deuteronomy 7:7-8 Deuteronomy 8:17-18  
 
The Christian should continually remember that all which distinguishes him from the vilest of men he owes to the grace and providence of God, and not to any goodness or merit of his own.  So also those nations which God has made great and powerful, should glory, not in their own wisdom and might and riches, but in God's unmerited favor, which has raised them from small beginnings to their present eminence.

title: Ezekiel 16:6
text: No language is too strong to describe the vileness and wretchedness of that state in which Christ found the believer, and from which his grace has raised him to whatever holiness and blessedness he now possesses.

title: Ezekiel 16:8
text:
vv 8-14. 
 
The consideration of the unspeakable goodness of our Redeemer, in bestowing upon us so many and so great mercies, is well adapted to make us ashamed of our past inconstancy, and to unite us more closely to him in the bonds of love and gratitude.

title: Ezekiel 16:15
text:
Playedst the harlot; by the worship of the gods of the heathen, which is spiritual fornication, and was generally connected with literal impurity. 
 
vv 15-34. 
 
The history of God's ancient people is a sad but true picture of the course of events in those Christian nations that have been most highly favored with the means of grace; every Christian also will see in it, with deep shame and godly sorrow, much that agrees with his own past life and conduct.

title: Ezekiel 16:24
text: An eminent place; selected for prostitution, that is, idolatrous worship.  See note on  Ezekiel 16:15 .

title: Ezekiel 16:26
text: With the Egyptians; here, as in  Ezekiel 16:28 , there is an allusion to the unlawful alliances of the Jews with Egypt and Assyria, which were made in the spirit of idolatry, and connected with idolatrous practices, and for which they were often reproved by the prophets.   Isaiah 30:1-2 Isaiah 31:1 II Kings 16:7 Hosea 5:13 Hosea 7:11 Hosea 14:3

title: Ezekiel 16:35
text:
vv 35-43. 
 
God will turn all the vain confidences of those who forsake him against themselves, and make them the means of their destruction.

title: Ezekiel 16:41
text: In the sight of many women; meaning, in the sight of the surrounding heathen nations, who are, like God's covenent people, represented under the symbol of women.

title: Ezekiel 16:42
text: My fury--to rest; by satisfying my justice in thy punishment.  This verse contains not a promise, but a threatening, as the following verses show.

title: Ezekiel 16:46
text:
Thine elder sister is Samaria--thy younger sister--Sodom; Samaria represents the ten tribes, who apostatized from God's service in the days of Jeroboam, as Sodom does the heathen world.  Both these are sisters to Jerusalem in character.  The terms "elder" and "younger" refer not to age, but to relative dignity. 
 
  At thy left hand; to the north of Jerusalem, the east being the front. 
 
  At thy right hand; to the south-east, probably where the southern bay of the Dead sea now lies.

title: Ezekiel 16:47
text: Corrupted more than they; compare  Matthew 11:21-24 .

title: Ezekiel 16:48
text: God estimates the guilt of transgressors by the light which they have enjoyed, and the means which have been used to bring them to repentance.  At the last day he will regard and treat as the greatest sinners those who have rebelled against the most faithful instruction and reproof.

title: Ezekiel 16:51
text:
Half of thy sins; in comparing the guilt of Jerusalem with that of Samaria, God has regard to the greater privileges and mercies bestowed upon the former city.  Compare  John 15:22 John 15:24 . 
 
  Hast justified thy sisters; hast shown them to be comparatively innocent.

title: Ezekiel 16:52
text: Hast judged thy sisters; compare  Romans 2:1 .

title: Ezekiel 16:53
text: The captivity of Sodom and her daughters; not literally, but figuratively, by the conversion of the heathen nations whom she represents.  Even in the restoration of Jerusalem, God humbles her by likening her to Samaria and Sodom.  This prophecy is fulfilled in Christ, who has abolished the distinction between Jew and Gentile.  Romans 10:12

title: Ezekiel 16:56
text: Was not mentioned by thy mouth; thou disdainedst to mention her.

title: Ezekiel 16:57
text: Reproach of the daughters of Syria; proceeding from them.  The terrible judgments of God upon Jerusalem exposed her sickedness, and made her a byword to the surrounding nations.   Ezekiel 5:14-15

title: Ezekiel 16:60
text: I will remember my covenant with thee; this promise is made to the true Zion, the church of God, which Jerusalem represents.

title: Ezekiel 16:61
text:
Give them unto thee for daughters; by their conversion and incorporation into the church. 
 
  Not by thy covenant; not for thy faithfulness in keeping thy covenant with me. 
 
God will assuredly save his church, and gather all nations into her. But this work he will accomplish in such a way that his own name shall be glorified, and she deeply humbled in view of her past inconstancy and unfaithfulness.

title: Ezekiel 17:1
text:
vv 1-16. 
 
Every covenant which we make with others in lawful things must be faithfully kept, though they be wicked and unreasonable men, and though it seem greatly for our present interest to break our word.  God will listen to no plea of expediency, but will punish perfidy towards our fellow men as falsehood to himself; for he is the God of truth, and demands of us truth in all our dealings.

title: Ezekiel 17:3
text:
A great eagle; Nebuchadnezzar. 
 
  The highest branch of the cedar; Jehoiachin, whom Nebuchadnezzar dethroned and carried to Babylon.

title: Ezekiel 17:4
text:
A land of traffic; Chaldea. 
 
  A city of merchants; Babylon.

title: Ezekiel 17:5
text: Of the seed of the land; that is, of "the king's seed,"  Ezekiel 17:13 , meaning Zedekiah, son of Josiah, whom Nebuchadnezzar made king in the place of Jehoiachin.  See the narrative,  II Kings 24:8-17

title: Ezekiel 17:6
text:
Of low stature; not a lofty cedar, as before, but a low vine; that is, a tributary king.  Compare  Ezekiel 17:12-13 . 
 
  Turned towrd him; towards Nebuchadnezzar, as dependent upon him.

title: Ezekiel 17:7
text:
Another great eagle; Pharaoh. 
 
  Did bend her roots toward him; turning away its confidence from Nebuchadnezzar to Pharaoh.

title: Ezekiel 17:9
text:
Shall he not pull; that is, the first eagle. 
 
  All the leaves of her spring; literally, all the fresh leaves of her springing; that is, all her fresh and green foliage. 
 
  Without great power--roots thereof; or without [the employment of] great power and many people to pluck her up from her roots.  The work of plucking up the vine of Judah from the place where it grew shall not require a numerous force.

title: Ezekiel 17:10
text: The east wind; a symbol of the Chaldean invasion, bringing with it desolation.

title: Ezekiel 17:13
text: Taken the mighty of the land; taken them away to Babylon.  II Kings 24:12

title: Ezekiel 17:15
text: Rebelled against him;  II Kings 24:20 II Chronicles 36:1

title: Ezekiel 17:16
text: In the midst of Babylon he shall die;  II Kings 25:7 Jeremiah 52:1

title: Ezekiel 17:17
text:
vv 17-21. 
 
They who violate their obligations to God and their fellow men, in the hope of some present advantage, generally meet with disappointment and shame in the present life, and they must incur God's wrath and curse in the life to come.

title: Ezekiel 17:21
text: Toward all winds;  II Kings 25:1

title: Ezekiel 17:22
text:
Of the highest branch of the high cedar--a tender one; the Messiah, as the context shows, who is here, as elsewhere, compared to a branch of God's planting. 
 
vv 22-24. 
 
God exalts and abases earthly kingdoms as he chooses; but his kingdom of grace stands fast amid all the changes of time, and shall in the end cover the world with its glory.

title: Ezekiel 17:24
text:
Brought down the high tree; abased Zedekiah and his princes, who are here the representatives of all who exalt themselves against God. 
 
  Exalted the low tree--made the dry tree to flourish; that is, exalted athe Messiah in his stead.  Compare  Isaiah 53:2 .

title: Ezekiel 18:2
text:
vv 2-3. 
 
God will in the end make the justice of his dealings with men so apparent that "every mouth shall be stopped, and all the world become guilty" before him.   Romans 3:4 Romans 3:19

title: Ezekiel 18:4
text:
vv 4-23. 
 
God bestows upon children many blessings through the piety of their fathers, and sends upon them many evils through their wickedness,  Exodus 20:5 Exodus 20:6 ; but no sinner will be saved for the goodness of his forefathers, nor any righteous man condemned for their wickedness.  At the final reckoning, every one will be called to an account for the deeds he has himself done, whether they be good or bad.   II Corinthians 5:10

title: Ezekiel 18:6
text:
Eaten upon the mountains; eaten sacrificial offerings to idols. 
 
  Lifted up his eyes; in worship, with confidence and longing desire. Compare  Psalms 121:1 .

title: Ezekiel 18:7
text: Restored--his pledge; see  Exodus 22:26-27 .

title: Ezekiel 18:8
text: Usury--increase; see  Exodus 22:25 .

title: Ezekiel 18:20
text:
The son shall not bear; be punished for. 
 
  Shall be upon him; he alone shall be rewarded or punished for it.

title: Ezekiel 18:26
text: It is only perseverance in holiness to the end that can secure eternal life.  Past deeds of righteousness cannot benefit the man who turns from them to the practice of iniquity.  Matthew 24:12-13 Galatians 6:9 Hebrews 6:4 Hebrews 6:6 Hebrews 6:11 Hebrews 6:12 Hebrews 10:36 Revelation of John 2:26

title: Ezekiel 18:27
text:
vv 27-28. 
 
No sinner, who is willing to repent and turn to God, need be discouraged on account of his past transgressions.   Isaiah 55:7

title: Ezekiel 19:1
text: When we compare the weakness and helpless dependence of the royal family of Judah in the days of Jeremiah and Ezekiel, with its glory and strength in the time of David and Solomon, we have an affecting proof of God's supreme power over nations, as well as of his unalterable determination to destroy every people that persists in transgressing his laws.

title: Ezekiel 19:2
text:
Thy mother; Jerusalem, as representing the Jewish state; the address is to Israel in the general sense, not to the ten tribes alone, as distinct from the two. 
 
  A lioness; compare  Genesis 49:9 .

title: Ezekiel 19:3
text: One of her whelps; Jehoahaz, whom Pharaoh-necho deposed and carried into Egypt.   II Kings 23:30-34 II Chronicles 36:1-4

title: Ezekiel 19:5
text: Another of her whelps; the three kings who succeeded Jehoahaz were all carried to Babylon by Nebuchadnezzar.  Of these some understand here Jehoiakim, as the immediate successor of Jehoahaz; others Jehoiachin, because he alone of the three was raised to the throne by the people.  But probably the fate of this second whelp represents that of "the princes of Israel" generally after Jehoahaz.

title: Ezekiel 19:10
text:
Is like a vine; or, "was like a vine," propserous and flourishing. 
 
  In thy blood; in thy vigor and strength.  The prophet here repeats what he has just said, under a new image.

title: Ezekiel 19:14
text: Out of a rod of her branches; Zedekiah's rebvellion against the king of Babylon became a consuming fire, which destroyed his kingdom and "the princes of Israel" together.   II Kings 24:20

title: Ezekiel 20:1
text:
vv 1-44. 
 
Though God will be inquired of by his people for the blessings which he promises, yet the hope of his cause rests not on their constancy, but upon his own unchangeable fidelity to his promises and zeal for his great name.  For his own glory he has begun and will carry forward the work of redemption, separating the wicked who are among his people from the righteous by his repeated judgments, and thus continuing and enlarging his kingdom from age to age.

title: Ezekiel 20:7
text: And defile not yourselves with the idols of Egypt; when God came to deliver his people from Egypt, he found them pollute with the worship of its idols, and deserving of his wrath.  How deep was this moral infection appears from the narrative of the golden calf,  Exodus 32:1-35 .

title: Ezekiel 20:23
text: Would scatter them among the heathen;  Leviticus 26:1-46 Deuteronomy 28:1-34:12

title: Ezekiel 20:25
text: I gave them also statutes--not good; in a permissive sense.  Psalms 81:12 Acts 7:42

title: Ezekiel 20:26
text:
Caused to pass through the fire; as burnt-offerings to their gods,  Ezekiel 20:31 . 
 
  All that openeth the womb; all their first-born children; a horrid perversion of the divine ordinance,  Exodus 13:2 .

title: Ezekiel 20:29
text: What is the high place whereunto ye go? a question of indignant remonstrance.

title: Ezekiel 20:35
text: The wilderness of the people; figuratively spoken, a wilderness consisting of exile and oppression among foreigners, in which the wheat shall be sifted from the chaff.  In restoring his people from captivity, God will repeat to them the discipline to which he subjected their fathers in the literal wilderness, and by which he destroyed the rebellious from among them.

title: Ezekiel 20:37
text: To pass under the rod; as shepherds do their flocks, thus numbering and reviewing each sheep of the fold, and separating the evil from the good.

title: Ezekiel 20:38
text: I will bring them forth--shall not enter into the land of Israel; another allusion to the exodus from Egypt: God will deal with the rebels among the captives as he did with the rebellious generation whom he brought out of Egypt.  Compare  Numbers 14:22-23 .

title: Ezekiel 20:39
text: Go ye, serve--with your idols; be wholly devoted to your gods, or serve me wholly: mix not your idolatrous rites with my worship.  I Kings 18:21

title: Ezekiel 20:40
text:
vv 40-44. 
 
  For in my holy mountain--your corrupt doings; a promise to the purified remnant, to be progressively fulfulled from age to age.  See note on  Ezekiel 11:20 .

title: Ezekiel 20:45
text:
The word of the Lord came unto me; the remainder of this chapter properly belongs to the following. 
 
vv 45-48. God would not spare his own chosen city Jerusalem from the devouring flame and from captivity, when she persisted in rebelling against him; neither will he spare any of his churches at the present day who follow her example, on account of the greatness of the privileges which he has conferred upon them in times past, or on account of the piety of their forefathers.

title: Ezekiel 20:46
text: The forest of the south field; Jerusalem, with the region dependent upon her,  Ezekiel 21:2 .  The multitude of her people is represented under the similitude of a forest.  Compare  Isaiah 9:18-19 Isaiah 10:18-19 Jeremiah 21:14

title: Ezekiel 20:47
text: Green tree--dry tree;  Ezekiel 21:3 Luke 23:1

title: Ezekiel 21:3
text: Cut off from thee the righteous and the wicked; that is, take away from thee every class of persons.  Such men as Jeremiah and Baruch, Ezekiel and Daniel, were among the removed.

title: Ezekiel 21:4
text: From the south to the north; of the land of Israel.

title: Ezekiel 21:6
text:
vv 6-7. 
 
God's resources to bless and to curse are alike unlimited.  When he draws his sword of vengeance against a people for their sins, resistance is vain, nor can any endure its terrible power.

title: Ezekiel 21:7
text: The tidings; of God's avenging sword.

title: Ezekiel 21:9
text: Furbished; made bright.

title: Ezekiel 21:10
text:
Then make mirth; instead of mourning for our sins.  Compare  Isaiah 22:12-13 . 
 
  It contemneth--every tree; or, "the sceptre of my son disdaineth every tree."  The sceptre of God's son is the reigning family of Israel, represented by Zedekiah and his princes.  "Every tree," is put metaphorically for the princes of other kingdoms.  These the king and princes of Jerusalem disdain, as not able to destroy the holy city. 
 
Sin has a dreadful power to blind men's minds so that they fail to discern the approach of God's judgments, and are overtaken by them, like the generation before the flood, in the midst of their mirth and revelry.

title: Ezekiel 21:12
text: Terrors--my people; rather, they are delivered to the sword with my people.

title: Ezekiel 21:13
text: Because it is a trial--shall be no more; or, "For a trial is made; and what if the disdainful sceptre," that is, of Israel, "should be no more?"  The trial consists of God's judgments through Nebuchadnezzar.

title: Ezekiel 21:16
text: One way or other; the verse contains a command to the sword to ravage in every direction.

title: Ezekiel 21:18
text:
vv 18-24. 
 
God's providence extends to all events, so that nothing takes place but in accordance with his wise and holy counsels.  Even the foolish divinations of heathen kings are so overruled by him, that through them he accomplishes his own purposes.

title: Ezekiel 21:19
text:
Appoint thee two ways; represent them by a picture or drawing. Compare  Ezekiel 4:1 . 
 
  That the sword--may come; that is, it may come by either of these ways. 
 
  One land; Babylon. 
 
  Choose; more literally, "make," that is, mark in the picture. 
 
  At the head of the way to the city; where the road to Jerusalem leaves that to Rabbath, both being the same for a certain distance from Babylon.  The words intimate that Nebuchadnezzar shall first assail Jerusalem, afterwards Ammon.  Compare  Ezekiel 21:28 .

title: Ezekiel 21:20
text: May come; may come to either city, according to the route upon which the king of Babylon shall decide.

title: Ezekiel 21:21
text:
To use divination; for the purpose of determining which road he should take.  Probably he was on his way to Egypt, and wished to take either Jerusalem or Rabbath on the road. 
 
  Made his arrows bright; or, "shook his arrows;" that is, in the urn, that when they flew out their direction might decide his course. 
 
  Looked in the liver; a common mode of taking auguries.

title: Ezekiel 21:22
text:
At his right hand was the divination for Jerusalem; that is, the lot which fell upon the right hand road, which led to Jerusalem. 
 
  To appoint captains--to build a fort; these words give the result to Jerusalem of his decision.

title: Ezekiel 21:23
text:
Unto them; to the people of Jerusalem. 
 
  As a false divinatin; they shall treat the report of it as false. 
 
  Oaths; of allegiance to the king of Babylon.   II Chronicles 36:16  
 
  He will call; Nebuchadnezzar will call. 
 
  The iniquity; of the king and princes of Judah in breaking their oath.

title: Ezekiel 21:25
text:
Prince of Israel; Zedekiah. 
 
  When iniquity shall have an end; literally, "in the time of the iniquity of he end;" that is, iniquity which brings and end to his kingdom.

title: Ezekiel 21:26
text: This shall not be the same; this dignity shall not remain unchanged.

title: Ezekiel 21:27
text:
He come whose right it is; the Messiah. 
 
  Will give it; will give him the diadem and crown.   Ezekiel 21:26  
 
God is in all the commotions and revolutions of the world, and through them he is steadily preparing the way for the universal dominion of his Son, to whom he has given all power in heaven and on earth.

title: Ezekiel 21:28
text:
The Ammonites; though for the present passed by, their turn will soon come. 
 
  Their reproach; upon Jerusalem, over whose destruction they exulted. 
 
vv 28-32. 
 
The punishment of sinners may be long delayed by the course of God's providence; but, if they persist in their transgressions, it will come at last with overwhelming power, and destroy them root and branch.  Malachi 4:1

title: Ezekiel 21:29
text:
They see vanity; the false prophets of Ammon. 
 
  Upon the necks of them that are slain; to cause thee to lie prostrate upon them in death.  This was the result to Ammon of their flatteries.

title: Ezekiel 22:2
text: The messengers whom God sends to men must deal honestly with their consciences, not withholding the truth through fear or favor, but faithfully setting forth before them all their sins.

title: Ezekiel 22:4
text:
Thy days--thy years; to be destroyed. 
 
When we see a community giving itself up to the practice of iniquity of every kind without restraint, we may be certain, from the sure testimony of God, that its days of punishment are near.

title: Ezekiel 22:7
text: The oppression of the weak and defenceless is a most heinous sin.  In the present catalogue God places it by the side of Sabbath-breaking, extortion, bribery, murder, and adultery.

title: Ezekiel 22:10
text: For pollution; that is, on accouint of her uncleanness.  Leviticus 18:19

title: Ezekiel 22:13
text:
Smitten my hand; as a sign of indignation. 
 
vv 13-16. 
 
The curse of God rests upon wealth gained by sinful practices.  It brings upon its owners trouble and misery instead of profit in this life, and exposes them to his wrath in the life to come.

title: Ezekiel 22:17
text:
vv 17-22. 
 
When men grow worse instead of better under God's chastisements, it is a token that they are reprobate, and that their destruction is nigh at hand.

title: Ezekiel 22:18
text: Become dross; in my efforts to refine them I have found them to be only dross and as dross I will consume them.

title: Ezekiel 22:24
text:
vv 24-31. 
 
When wicked princes unite with wicked prophets and priests to spoil a nation and corrupt its faith and practice by false doctrines, ungodliness and iniquity will soon pervade the mass of the people, and they, with their rulers and teachers, will become like briers and thorns ready to be consumed by the fire of God's wrath.

title: Ezekiel 22:28
text: Daubed them with untempered mortar; see  Ezekiel 13:10-16 .

title: Ezekiel 22:30
text: Make up the hedge--the gap; see note on  Ezekiel 13:5 .

title: Ezekiel 23:1
text:
In this chapter the adulteries of the two sisters, Aholah and Aholibah, represent not only the idolatrous practices which Samaria and Jerusalem borrowed from the heathen nations, but also, and especially, their unlawful alliances with them; for these were formed in an idolatrous spirit, and they led to literal idolatry. 
 
For the instructions on this chapter the reader is referred to those on  Ezekiel 16:1-63 , the contents of which are very similar.

title: Ezekiel 23:3
text: Committed whoredoms in Egypt; worshipped the gods of the Egyptians.

title: Ezekiel 23:4
text:
Aholah; that is, "her tent," namely, that of Samaria. 
 
  Aholibah; that is, "my tent is in her."  The meaning is, that Samaria has her own idolatrous tabernacle, while God's tabernacle is in Jerusalem. 
 
  Were mine; espoused to me,  Ezekiel 16:8 .

title: Ezekiel 23:14
text: Men--images; these seem to have been the images of gods and deified heroes portrayed upon the walls of the Babylonian palaces.  The description agrees perfectly with the figures now found graven upon the stone slabs that abound in the ruins of Nineveh and Babylon.

title: Ezekiel 23:16
text:
vv 16-17. 
 
  Sent messengers--the Babylonians came; she introduced the worship of these Chaldean deities into Jerusalem. 
 
  Was alienated from them; the Chaldeans, whose idolatrous images she had learned to worship, became to he objects of terror and aversion when she turned from them to Egypt.

title: Ezekiel 23:19
text: Calling to remembrance the days of her youth, wherein she had played the harlot; remembering and renewing her early fornications with the Egyptians.  The prophet refers to the alliances which the Jews sought with the Egyptians against the power of the Chaldeans.

title: Ezekiel 23:32
text: Thy sister's cup; cup of my wrath which she has drunk.

title: Ezekiel 23:34
text:
Break; here in the sense of gnawing, as a wild beast a bone. 
 
  Pluck off thine own breasts; tear them, from anguish and madness.

title: Ezekiel 23:40
text: Sent for men to come from far--deckedst thyself; made friendship with foreigners, and adopted their idolatrous practices.

title: Ezekiel 23:41
text:
Bed; her a couch for reclining at meals. 
 
  A table prepared before it; this table was spread in honor of the idols worshipped, and afterwards the worshippers feasted upon its provisions.

title: Ezekiel 24:2
text: Set himself against Jerusalem; by laying siege to it.  This was made known to the prophet n captivity by immediate revelation.  He writes the name of the day in the presence of the people, as a testimony to them when they shall hear of the event by human report.

title: Ezekiel 24:3
text:
vv 3-5. 
 
  Set on a pot--seethe the bones; the pot is Jerusalem, the pieces in it are the inhabitants, and the fire under it is God's wrath.

title: Ezekiel 24:6
text:
Scum; rather, filth, adhering to the pot itself, as is plain  Ezekiel 24:11 , polluting it and all in it. 
 
  Bring it out; the flesh.  This signifies the removal of the people from Jerusalem by death and captivity. 
 
  Let no lot fall upon it; lot to determine who shall be destroyed, and who saved: the meaning is, that all shall perish without distinction.

title: Ezekiel 24:7
text:
Her blood; the blood which she has shed. 
 
  Set it upon the top of a rock; shed it in the most open way. 
 
vv 7-8. 
 
God will make the punishment of bold transgressors as conspicuous as their crimes.

title: Ezekiel 24:8
text: I have set her blood--not be covered; as she has shed blood openly, God will avenge it openly.

title: Ezekiel 24:9
text:
vv 9-13. 
 
No amount of suffering inflicted upon transgressors is sufficient of itself to remove the desperate wickedness of the human heart.  Though God send upon them judgment after judgment, they will still continue to rebel against him.  The power of his Spirit alone can change the heart of stone to flesh and purify the inner man.

title: Ezekiel 24:10
text: Spice it well; some prefer to render "stir it well."

title: Ezekiel 24:11
text: Then set it empty; after the pot is emptied of its contents, it is still further to be exposed to a fierce heat, that its filth may be molten out of it.  The meaning is, that after Jerusalem has been emptied of her inhabitants, the city itself is to be burned to the ground.

title: Ezekiel 24:13
text: Purged thee; that is, assayed to purge thee.

title: Ezekiel 24:16
text:
The desire of thine eyes; the prophet's wife,  Ezekiel 24:18 . 
 
God sometimes inflicts upon his most faithful servants great sufferings for the instruction of others.

title: Ezekiel 24:17
text:
Tire; that is, turban.  This and the shoes were laid aside in mourning. 
 
  Lips; or beard, as the word is rendered in  II Samuel 19:24 .  This was covered as a sign of mourning. 
 
  The bread of men; of common men, that is, coarse bread, as in a time of mourning. 
 
vv 17-18. 
 
The interests of truth often require us to suppress those outward signs of grief which would be in other circumstances right and proper.

title: Ezekiel 24:21
text: Pitieth; here in the sense of loveth with tenderness.

title: Ezekiel 24:22
text:
vv 22-23. 
 
  Shall not cover--shall not mourn; the calamity will be so general and overwhelming, that all the customary signs of mourning will be omitted.

title: Ezekiel 24:23
text: Public calamity, long continued and general, has a tendency to harden the feelings of wicked men, so that they omit the customary expressions of grief and sympathy, and pine away in sullen despair.  From so dreadful a chastisement let every community seek deliverance from God by earnest prayer joined with hearty repentance.

title: Ezekiel 24:26
text: To hear it; the desolation which I have made in Jerusalem: this expresses the certainty of the event in God's purpose.

title: Ezekiel 24:27
text: Be opened--be no more dumb; Ezekiel now closes, by divine direction, his prophecies to his own people till the capture of Jerusalem shall be reported to him,  Ezekiel 33:21-22 .  His intervening prophecies were directed against the Gentiles.

title: Ezekiel 25:1
text: The four nations mentined in this chapter all lay on the borders of God's covenant people; they had been from the beginning their enemies, and now exulted in their captivity.

title: Ezekiel 25:3
text:
vv 3-7. 
 
They who exult with malicious joy over the calamities of others, will soon be compelled to mourn and weep over their own calamities.  Proverbs 17:5 Proverbs 24:17-18

title: Ezekiel 25:4
text: The men of the east; the Arabian tribes of the desert, which lay east and south of Palestine.

title: Ezekiel 25:5
text: Rabbath; the same as "Rabbath of the Ammonites,"  Ezekiel 21:20 , in the mountainous region east of the Jordan.  Its ruins are used by the Arabs at the present time as a lodging-place for camels.

title: Ezekiel 25:8
text:
And Seir; he first mentions the common sin of Moab and Seir, or Edom, and then utters a separate prophecy against each. 
 
  Like unto all the heathen; has perished like all the other nations, notwithstanding the peculiar protection of Jehovah which it enjoyed. Thus they reproach the God of Israel. 
 
vv 8-11. 
 
God is jealous for his own glory.  He will not give over his people to final weakness and ruin; but will in due time appear for their deliverance, and the destruction of those who have rejoiced in their humiliation.

title: Ezekiel 25:9
text: I will open the side of Moab from the cities--the glory of the country, Beth-jeshimoth, Baal-meon, and Kiriathaim; render, "I will open the side of Moab in the region of the cities, of the cities on his frontier, which are the glory of the country; namely, Beth-jeshimoth," etc.  The three places named all lay on the northern frontier of Moab, north of the Arnon.  This has been from ancient times a celebrated pasture-ground.

title: Ezekiel 25:10
text: The men of the east with the Ammonites; that is, at the same time that I open the country of the Ammonites to the men of the east, I will also open to them the land of the Moabites.

title: Ezekiel 25:12
text:
vv 12-17. 
 
Hatred and revenge are at all times heinous sins, which provoke God to wrath; but they are peculiarly offensive to him when exercised towards others in times of deep distress.

title: Ezekiel 25:13
text:
Teman; a district of Edom on the south-east. 
 
  Of Dedan; better, "unto Dedan."  This was apparently on the north-east of Edom.  There was, as is generally thought, another Dedan on or near the Persian gulf, mentioned in  Ezekiel 27:15 .

title: Ezekiel 25:16
text:
The Cherethim; another name for the Philistines.  Compare  I Samuel 30:14-16 . 
 
  The remnant of the sea-coast; the Philistines lay along the sea-coast at the south-west of Palestine.

title: Ezekiel 26:2
text:
Tyrus; the celebrated emporium of ancient Phoenicia. It was originally a long rocky island, parallel to the shore of the Mediterranean, and less than half a mile distant from it.  When Alexander the Great besieged it he extended a causeway to it, and thus made it a peninsula. 
 
It is unlawful for us to seek our own aggrandizement by the ruin of our neighbors, or to rejoice in the calamities which befall others, because they bring profit to ourselves.

title: Ezekiel 26:5
text: The wonderful accuracy with which the ancient prophets of Judah foretold the present condition of cities and empires that were then great and powerful, is a sure proof that they spoke not of themselves, but as they were moved by the Holy Ghost.

title: Ezekiel 26:7
text:
Nebuchadrezzar; he besieged Tyre for thirteen years. 
 
vv 7-14. 
 
God makes use of the agency of wicked as well as of good men for the accomplishment of his purposes, and when he has any work for man to perform, he gives him strength and resources sufficient for its execution.

title: Ezekiel 26:8
text: Thy daughters in the field; the cities dependent upon Tyre.

title: Ezekiel 26:14
text: Like the top of a rock--a place to spread nets; the present condition of Tyre answers exactly to this description. Nebuchadnezzar's assault was followed by a series of other calamities, which finally reduced it to utter desolation.

title: Ezekiel 26:15
text:
The isles; the islands and coasts of the Mediterranean on the west of Tyre, and then the western regions generally.  They are named on account of the rich commerce which Tyre carried on with them. 
 
  Shake; tremble from terror and amazement.  Compare  Ezekiel 26:18 , and  Ezekiel 27:35 . 
 
vv 15-21. 
 
By his great and mighty judgments, God is continually humbling haughty and strong nations, and all who put their trust in them; and teaching the world that he reigns supreme over all men, and that in himself alone are to be found prosperity and salvation.

title: Ezekiel 26:16
text: All the princes of the sea; the princes of the colonies founded by Tyre, and enriched by her merchandise, seem to be especially intended. See note on  Isaiah 23:8 .

title: Ezekiel 26:19
text: Bring up the deep upon thee; the meaning is, that God will destroy her as by a deluge.  We need not interpret these words altogether in a literal sense, yet it is remarkable that the western coast of the peninsula of Tyre is strewed with the ruins of the ancient city lying beneath the waves.

title: Ezekiel 26:20
text:
Shall bring thee down--into the pit; Tyre is represented as descending like an individual into the regions of the dead. 
 
  The low parts--places desolate of old; a poetic description of the abode of the dead, as one of darkness and desolation.  Compare  Job 10:21-22 . 
 
  Set glory; make Jerusalem again an ornament and a praise.

title: Ezekiel 27:1
text:
In this chapter the countries that have traded with Tyre and been enriched by her are enumerated, with their various articles of merchandise,  Ezekiel 27:1-25 ; then their terror and distress for her destruction are described,  Ezekiel 27:26-36 . 
 
The strength and safety of a nation lie not in the extent of its commerce, the vastness of its treasures, and the multitude and variety of luxuries which its citizens can command, but in that righteousness which secures the divine presence and blessing.  That prosperity and splendor which have not their foundation in justice and truth will soon vanish away, and want, ignominy, and despair come in their stead.

title: Ezekiel 27:6
text:
The company of the Ashurites--ivory; rather, "they have made thy benches of ivory inlaid in box." 
 
  The isles of Chittim; Cyprus, with the adjacent islands and coasts.

title: Ezekiel 27:7
text: The isles of Elishah; the southern peninsula of Greece with its adjacent islands.

title: Ezekiel 27:8
text: Arvad; a small rocky island of the Mediterranean north of Tripolis, and about two miles from the shore.

title: Ezekiel 27:9
text: Gebal; a city and district of Phoenicia on the shore of the Mediterranean under mount Lebanon.

title: Ezekiel 27:10
text: Lud--Phut; African tribes.

title: Ezekiel 27:12
text: Tarshish; see note on  Isaiah 23:1 .

title: Ezekiel 27:13
text:
Javan; Ionia, and in a more general sense Greece. 
 
  Tubal and Meshech; between the Black sea and the Caspian.  This region has always been celebrated for its trade in slaves.

title: Ezekiel 27:14
text: Togarmah; probably Armenia.

title: Ezekiel 27:15
text:
Dedan; probably an island of the Persian gulf. 
 
  Horns of ivory; that is, tusks of elephant, so called from their resemblance to horns.

title: Ezekiel 27:17
text: Minnith; a city on the borders of the Ammonites,  Judges 11:33 .

title: Ezekiel 27:18
text: Helbon; the city now called Aleppo; or, a large valley on the east of Anti-lebanon.

title: Ezekiel 27:19
text: Dan also and Jovan; generally considered to be Arabian tribes, the Javan here mentioned differing from that in  Ezekiel 27:13 .  Some render, "Wedan and Javan."

title: Ezekiel 27:20
text: Dedan; probably an Arabian tribe, different from the Dedan mentioned  Ezekiel 27:15 .

title: Ezekiel 27:21
text: Kedar; an Arabian tribe, as were also those mentioned in  Ezekiel 27:22 .

title: Ezekiel 27:23
text:
Haran--Canneh--Eden; cities of Mesopotamia.  Canneh seems to be the same as Calneh.  See note on  Isaiah 10:9 . 
 
  Asshur; Assyria proper, lying east of the Tigris.  Chilmad is unknown.

title: Ezekiel 27:26
text: Thy rowers; that is, thy rulers, Tyre being compared to a ship.

title: Ezekiel 27:30
text:
vv 30-36. 
 
  Shall cause their voice to be heard against thee, and shall cry bitterly; compare the passage,  Revelation of John 18:15-19 , where the fall of the mystic Babylon is described in similar terms.

title: Ezekiel 28:1
text:
vv 1-10. 
 
God is jealous for his own glory, and will be acknowledged as supreme over nations, as well as families and individuals.  When any people become proud of their wisdom and skill to get wealth, of the vastness of their resources, or of the strength of their armies and fleets, and vainly imagine that their destiny is in their own hands, God will teach them by his mighty judgments, coming upon them irresistibly and in unexpected ways, how easy it is for him to break them in pieces as a potter's vessel; and will turn all their boasting into shame and confusion.

title: Ezekiel 28:10
text: The uncircumcised; the uncircumcised here represent those who are aliens from God's covenant, and unclean in heart and life, and as such doomed to destruction.  Compare  Ezekiel 31:18 Ezekiel 32:21 , etc; and  Isaiah 52:1 .

title: Ezekiel 28:11
text:
vv 11-19. 
 
Great and long-continued prosperity has a tendency to lift up the hearts of nations with pride, and thus make it necessary that God should humble them in the sight of all men.

title: Ezekiel 28:12
text: Sealest up the sum; rather, "sealest up the measure;" that is, makest the measure of thy wisdom and beauty complete.  A seal is set to that which is finished.

title: Ezekiel 28:13
text:
Hast been in Eden; thy abode has been as it were in Eden, where all was beauty and excellence. 
 
  Every precious stone--gold; there seems to be an allusion here to the precious stoned and gold of Eden.   Genesis 2:12

title: Ezekiel 28:14
text:
Anointed; consecrated to the kingly office, of which anointing was the sign.   I Samuel 10:1 I Samuel 16:13 . 
 
  Cherub; the king of Tyre seems to be called a cherub in respect to the fulness of gifts which God bestowed upon him.  See note on  Ezekiel 1:10 . 
 
  That covereth; the allusion is to the cherubim that covered the mercy-seat with their wings.   Exodus 25:20  
 
  Upon the holy mountain; Zion, where the ark with its cherubim abode.  The meaning is, thou wast exalted to the highest dignity. 
 
  Stones of fire; the precious sparkling stones mentioned in  Ezekiel 28:13 .

title: Ezekiel 28:15
text:
Wast perfect in thy ways; acting uprightly as a nation and enjoying continual prosperity. 
 
  Wast created; founded as a nation. 
 
  Till iniquity was found in thee; till, through the corruption of thy wealth, thou ceasedst to act uprightly.  This was the occasion of the ruin which the prophet now foretells.

title: Ezekiel 28:16
text: I will cast thee--out of the mountain of God; see note to  Ezekiel 28:14 .

title: Ezekiel 28:20
text:
vv 20-23. 
 
God will so order the chastisements which he inflicts upon men that his justice shall be thereby manifested, and his great name glorified.

title: Ezekiel 28:21
text: Zidon; the most ancient town of Phoenicia, north of Tyre.

title: Ezekiel 28:23
text: Shall be judged; rather, "shall fall."

title: Ezekiel 28:24
text:
Shall be no more a pricking brier; the design of God's judgments on the heathen nations around Israel, is the peace and prosperity of his covenant people.  This promise, with those which follow in  Ezekiel 28:15-16 , is made not to "Israel according to the flesh," but to "the Israel of God."   Galatians 3:9  
 
vv 24-26. 
 
God governs the world for the good of his own people.  All the calamities which he sends upon the nations, he will make subservient to their welfare and enlargement; and will put honor upon them in the presence of all who have despised them.

title: Ezekiel 29:1
text:
vv 1-10. 
 
God will not suffer his people to withdraw their confidence from himself, and give it to any arm of flesh; but will destroy all their vain alliances, as he did in Egypt of old when the Jews looked to it instead of himself for help and salvation.

title: Ezekiel 29:3
text:
Dragon; that is, crocodile, here used as a symbol of the king of Egypt. 
 
  His rivers; the various arms of the Nile. 
 
  My river; he boasts of his river, because upon that the fertility of Egypt depends.

title: Ezekiel 29:4
text: The fish of thy rivers; these represent the people over whom the king of Egypt ruled.

title: Ezekiel 29:6
text: A staff of reed; disappointing those who trust in it; compare  II Kings 18:21 .  The prophet dwells at such length upon the punishment of Egypt and her kings, because the Jews relied on their help against Nebuchadnezzar.  See  Ezekiel 17:15-17 .

title: Ezekiel 29:7
text:
Rend; that is, tear by piercing. 
 
  To be at a stand; or, "to shake," as in  Psalms 69:23 .

title: Ezekiel 29:10
text:
From the tower of Syene; "from Migdol to Syene."  Migdol was in the extreme north of Egypt,  Exodus 14:2 , and Syene in the extreme south. 
 
  Ethiopia; which lay south of Egypt.

title: Ezekiel 29:11
text:
vv 11-16. 
 
The times for the exaltation and humiliation of nations are appointed by God with reference to the welfare of his kingdom of grace; he will make manifest his sovereign power over them both in lifting them up to strength and honor, and in abasing them, that all may learn to fear him, and feel their dependence upon him.

title: Ezekiel 29:14
text: Pathros; Upper Egypt.

title: Ezekiel 29:15
text: Basest of the kingdoms; a prophecy which has been strikingly fulfilled to the present hour.

title: Ezekiel 29:16
text:
Bringeth their iniquity to remembrance; their old iniquity, of leaning on Egypt instead of Jehovah.  So long as Egypt was in a flourishing condition, it brought their iniquity to remembrance; that is, excited the Israelites to practise it anew. 
 
  Look after them; when the Israelites should look after the Egyptians, as their allies and helpers.

title: Ezekiel 29:17
text:
In the seven and twentieth year; seventeen years after the date of the preceding prophecy, and sixteen years after that recorded in  Ezekiel 30:20-26 .  It is therefore an appendix to the first of these prophecies, made by the prophet himself. 
 
vv 17-21. 
 
God overrules the plans of wicked nations for the accomplishment of his own holy and good purposes, often raising one of them to great power, and subduing others before it; but all his counsels shall in the end advance the welfare of his true Israel.

title: Ezekiel 29:18
text:
A great service; the siege of Tyre, foretold in  Ezekiel 26:7-14 , which had now become history.  This cost Nebuchadnezzar thirteen years of toil. 
 
  Yet had he no wages; the spoils of Tyre furnished no adequate reward for his trouble.

title: Ezekiel 29:21
text:
In that day; in connection with these judgments upon both the enemies of God's church and her heathen allies in whom she puts confidence.  This prophecy, like many others relating to the progress of God's kingdom, has a progressive fulfilment, and should not be limited to any one exact date.  See note on  Isaiah 4:2 . 
 
  The horn of the house of Israel to bud forth; more literally, "a horn to bud forth for the house of Israel;" that is, the Messiah.  But under him are included the human deliverers also whom God raises up from time to time for his church; for these all receive from Christ the Head their life and strength.

title: Ezekiel 30:1
text: When God has determined to overthrow a people for their sins, no human alliances can save them.  His wrath will consume them and their helpers together, and put to shame all who have looked to them, instead of their Maker, for help and deliverance.

title: Ezekiel 30:2
text: Woe worth the day; literally, "Woe to the day;" that is, the day of vengeance upon Egypt.

title: Ezekiel 30:3
text: The time of the heathen; the time of their punishment.

title: Ezekiel 30:5
text:
Lydia; here an African people. 
 
  Mingled people; foreigners of different nations, perhaps employed as hired soldiers in the Egyptian armies.  See  Ezekiel 27:10 . 
 
  In league; in league with Egypt; the allies of Egypt are meant.

title: Ezekiel 30:6
text: From the tower of Syene; see note on  Ezekiel 29:10 .

title: Ezekiel 30:9
text:
From me; as the author of Egypt's destruction.  Jehovah sends them, not directly by revelation, but indirectly by his providence. 
 
  In ships; ascending the Nile in light ships or boats.  Compare  Isaiah 18:2 , with the note.

title: Ezekiel 30:12
text: Make the rivers dry; figuratively spoken of the destruction of Egypt by Nebuchadnezzar's armies, because its fertility depended on the waters of the Nile.

title: Ezekiel 30:13
text:
vv 13-18. 
 
  Noph; Memphis, the ancient capital of Lower Egypt.  It was situated not far from the modern Cairo. 
 
  Zoan; Tanis, on the eastern side of the delta of the Nile. 
 
  No; Thebes, the ancient capital of Upper Egypt, a city of vast extent and splendor, whose ruins are yet visible. 
 
  Sin; Pelusium, on the eastern branch of the Nile, a few miles below Memphis. 
 
  Pi-beseth; in Lower Egypt, on the eastern branch of the Nile. 
 
  Tehaphnehes; the same as Tahapanes,  Jeremiah 2:16 .  It lay near Pelusium. 
 
All these ancient cities of Egypt are now in ruins, according to the prophet's word.

title: Ezekiel 30:21
text: A roller; that is, a bandage.

title: Ezekiel 30:22
text: The strong, and that which was broken; the breaking of one arm has been already foretold,  Ezekiel 30:21 ; God will complete his destruction by breaking the other; that is, he will utterly destroy his power.

title: Ezekiel 31:1
text: When God destroys great and mighty empires for their pride and wickedness, he sets them forth as an example to those that come after them, that they may fear his power and depart from evil; but if they will not give heed to the oft-repeated warning, they also must perish in like manner.  We of the United States ought to consider this, and tremble; remembering that if we make ourselves like Assyria and Egypt in character, God will make us like them in shame and ruin.

title: Ezekiel 31:3
text: Shroud; here used of a mass of dark foliage.

title: Ezekiel 31:4
text: Set him up on high; made him a lofty tree by supplying water for his roots.

title: Ezekiel 31:6
text: All the fowls of heaven--great nations; the fowls and beasts represent the multitudes of people that were under his care and protection.  Compare  Daniel 4:12 .

title: Ezekiel 31:8
text:
In the garden of God; in Eden, where the loftiest cedars may be supposed to have flourished.  Compare  Ezekiel 31:9 . 
 
  Hide him; that is, conceal him by overtopping him.

title: Ezekiel 31:10
text: Thou; the Assyrian king, who is directly addressed in this clause.

title: Ezekiel 31:11
text:
vv 11-12. 
 
  The mighty one of the heathen--the terrible of the nations; the conquerors and destroyers of Nineveh, the capital of the Assyrian empire; namely, Cyaxares king of Media, assisted by the victory of Babylon, then a province of Assyria, who had revolted against his master.  This happened about six hundred years before Christ.

title: Ezekiel 31:14
text:
All that drink water; imbibe water from the earth,  Ezekiel 31:16 ; that is, prosper by God's blessing. 
 
  They are all delivered; all the trees that exalt themselves as did this Assyrian cedar. 
 
  In the midst of the children of men; that is, along with all other mortals, notwithstanding their greatness and power.

title: Ezekiel 31:15
text:
Covered the deep; with mourning apparel. 
 
  Restrained the floods thereof--were stayed; dried p the streams of the great deep, so that they ceased to flow.  The waters here dried up are those which had made the Assyrian cedar great.   Ezekiel 31:4-5

title: Ezekiel 31:16
text:
All the trees of Eden; that is, all the mighty men of the earth who have descended into the pit before him. 
 
  Shall be comforted; because he is reduced to the same condition with themselves.

title: Ezekiel 31:17
text:
With him; that is, in like manner as he. 
 
  His arm; his allies and dependencies.

title: Ezekiel 31:18
text: To whom art thou thus like; the prophet addresses these words to Pharaoh, to whom he now makes the application of what has been said concerning the Assyrian king.  The implied answer to the question is: Thou art like to this Assyrian cedar in glory and greatness, and shalt fall as he has fallen before thee.

title: Ezekiel 32:1
text: Time and death are mighty levellers.  How do they bring down into the dust the strength and riches and beauty in which men pride themselves. Great and terrible empires, like Assyria, Babylon, and Rome; rich and noble families that have long surrounded themselves with pomp and luxury; renowned warriors, statesmen, and orators; these, with every thing else on which the men of this world set their hearts, sink into the earth together, uncared for and forgotten.  The immortal soul alone, with the deeds which it has done in the body, survives, and goes to God's tribunal, to be rewarded according to its works.

title: Ezekiel 32:2
text:
A whale in the seas; see note on  Ezekiel 29:3 . 
 
  With thy rivers; rather, "in thy rivers."

title: Ezekiel 32:3
text: With a company of many people; as my servants to draw the net.

title: Ezekiel 32:5
text: With thy height; with the mass of thy dead carcass.

title: Ezekiel 32:6
text: Full of thee; of thy blood.

title: Ezekiel 32:7
text:
vv 7-8. 
 
  Put thee out--set darkness upon thy land; the destruction of kingdoms is often compared in Scripture to the darkening of the heavens, and the extinction of their lights.  See  Isaiah 13:10 , with the note and references.

title: Ezekiel 32:9
text: Bring thy destruction--into the countries; either the report of Pharaoh's destruction, or the broken fragments of his people.

title: Ezekiel 32:10
text: For thee; in view of my judgments upon thee.

title: Ezekiel 32:13
text: Trouble them; trouble the waters of Egypt by passing through them.

title: Ezekiel 32:14
text: Make their waters deep; rather, "settle their waters."  The waters of Egypt, being left without man or beast, shall flow clear and smooth; that is, the land shall be utterly desolated.   Ezekiel 29:8-12  Others, however, understand these words as a promise of returning quiet and prosperity to Egypt when by God's chastisements she shall have been made to know that he is the Lord,  Ezekiel 32:15 .  Compare  Ezekiel 29:13  and  Isaiah 19:25 .

title: Ezekiel 32:16
text: The daughters of the nations; that is, the nations themselves. Compare the expressions, "daughter of Jerusalem," "daughter of Babylon," etc.

title: Ezekiel 32:17
text: Of the month; apparently of the twelfth month,  Ezekiel 32:1 ; that is, fourteen days after the preceding prophecy.

title: Ezekiel 32:18
text:
Cast them down; to the pit, that is, declare their casting down in a solemn lamentation. 
 
  Her, and the daughters of the famous nations; in the lamentation, or song, that follows, Pharaoh with his people is represented as going down to the pit, to join the great multitude of princes and warriors that have descended thither before him.  By a bold poetic figure, the spirits of these are represented as gathered in the lower world, while the graves of their bodies stand around them. Compare  Isaiah 14:9-11 .

title: Ezekiel 32:19
text: Whom dost thou pass in beauty? in this question God rebukes Egypt for glorying in her superior beauty, and at the same time intimates that this shall not save her from perishing with the other uncircumcised nations.

title: Ezekiel 32:20
text:
They shall fall; the Egyptians. 
 
  Draw her; drag her down to the pit.

title: Ezekiel 32:21
text:
Shall speak; in amazement at his fall.  Compare  Isaiah 14:10 . 
 
  To him--with them that help him; to Pharoah and his allies. 
 
  They are gone down; "the strong among the nations," whom the prophet afterwards enumerates.

title: Ezekiel 32:22
text: His graves are about him; the spirits of the king of Assyria and his warriors are in the pit, by the graves of their bodies.  See note on  Ezekiel 32:18 .

title: Ezekiel 32:23
text: Caused terror in the land of the living; the prophet contrasts their present weakness with the terror they caused while yet alive.

title: Ezekiel 32:24
text:
Elam; Persia. 
 
  Borne their shame; the shame of being slain and sent down to the pit. 
 
  With them; that is, along with the rest of the nations: they are reduced to a common level with them.

title: Ezekiel 32:25
text:
Have set her; have appointed for Elam. 
 
  Round about him; about her king; and so  Ezekiel 32:26 . 
 
  He is put; the king of Elam.

title: Ezekiel 32:26
text: Meshech, Tubal; see note on  Ezekiel 27:13 .

title: Ezekiel 32:27
text:
They shall not lie--the land of the living; more plainly thus: "They shall not lie with the mighty that are fallen of the uncircumcised, who have gone down to hell with their weapons of war, and they have laid their swords under their heads: but their iniquities shall be upon their bones, because they were the terror of the mighty in the land of the living." 
 
  Shall not lie; Meshech and Tubal shall not lie in their graves honorably buried.  A poetical burial in the lower world has been ascribed to them,  Ezekiel 32:26 ; but here a literal burial on earth is denied them. 
 
  With their weapons of war; there is here a blending of the literal with the figurative.  Because their weapons of war have been deposited with them in their graves, they are figuratively represented as having taken them with them to the lower world, just as their graves are figuratively represented as being there with their souls. 
 
  But their iniquities; the iniquities of Meshech and Tubal. 
 
  Shall be upon their bones; their bones shall be left unburied, as a punishment for their violence in the land of the living.

title: Ezekiel 32:31
text: Shall be comforted; see note on  Ezekiel 31:16 .

title: Ezekiel 32:32
text: I have caused my terror; another reading of the original is, "I have caused his terror," that is, I have permitted Pharaoh to spread terror.

title: Ezekiel 33:1
text:
vv 1-9. 
 
God's government is one of personal responsibility.  No man can perform his neighbor's duty for him, and no man will be excused for neglecting his own duty because his neighbor has failed in his.  The preacher will be called to a strict account for the manner in which he has delivered the message intrusted to him by God; and if any have perished through his unfaithfulness, their blood will be upon him; but this will not excuse the sinner himself, who had God's law written on his conscience, and knew that he was doing wrong.   Romans 2:15

title: Ezekiel 33:10
text:
Be upon us; if punishment be exacted of us for them. 
 
  In them; in suffering the punishment of them.  They represent themselves as doomed to destruction, without any hope of forgiveness or restoration.  The prophet had declared that they should pine away for their iniquities,  Ezekiel 24:23 ; but this presupposed their continuance in sin. 
 
vv 10-11. 
 
It is alike wicked on the one hand to flatter ourselves with the hope of going unpunished while we persevere in sin, and on the other, to take a despairing view of God's mercy, as if he were determined to destroy us however we humbled ourselves before him.  Presumption and despondency grow out of the same evil root of unbelief.

title: Ezekiel 33:12
text:
vv 12-20. 
 
No man has a right to consider himself in the way to heaven any farther than he is rendering to God present obedience; and no man who is willing to turn with hearty repentance from his past transgessions, need despair of forgiveness and salvation.

title: Ezekiel 33:22
text: In the evening--until he came to me in the morning; the spirit of prophecy fell upon Ezekiel the evening before the arrival of the escaped, so that he began again to speak to the people; but the special message that follows was received after the news of the taking of the city.  See note on  Ezekiel 24:27 .

title: Ezekiel 33:24
text:
They that inhabit those wastes; the remnant of Israel and Judah, that had not yet gone into captivity. 
 
  Abraham was one--we are many; if Abraham, who was but one, inherited the land, much more shall we inherit it, seeing we are many. But they forgot that the land of Canaan was given to Abraham for his faith, not for his might. 
 
vv 24-29. 
 
The children of believers have no right to encourage themselves on account of God's favors shown to their fathers, any further than they follow their holy example.

title: Ezekiel 33:25
text: Eat with the blood;  Genesis 9:4 Leviticus 7:26-27:1

title: Ezekiel 33:26
text: Stand upon your sword; rely on violence.

title: Ezekiel 33:30
text:
Against thee; rather, "of thee." 
 
vv 30-33. 
 
To praise the preacher for his fervor and eloquence, and show much love to his person, instead of obeying his words, is a very common practice. But God will reckon all such hearers among the rebellious and perverse; and will teach them, by the fulfilment of his threatened judgments, that they have rejected not his messengers, but himself.   Luke 10:16

title: Ezekiel 33:31
text: As the people cometh; as the people come to worship God and be instructed in his will: they have the form of godliness.

title: Ezekiel 33:33
text: When this cometh to pass; the evil threatened.

title: Ezekiel 34:1
text: "The shepherds of Israel" spoken of in this chapter, are all their rulers and guides, as well in political as in religious matters.

title: Ezekiel 34:2
text:
vv 2-3. 
 
It is the business of rulers and religious teachers to seek the welfare of those committed to their care, not their own pleasure and emolument. They who use the holy office of the ministry as a means of advancing their worldly interests, and are more anxious to find good places for themselves than to "feed the flock of God," are hirelings, and not true shepherds.  God will be against them, and will give their work to others who will perform it faithfully,  Ezekiel 34:10

title: Ezekiel 34:4
text: Christ's ministers ought, after the example of their great Master, to bestow special labor upon "men of low degree," carefully seeking out the poor and friendless, the feeble-minded, the ignorant, and the erring; remembering in all their ministrations that Christ has sent them "to seek and save that which was lost."

title: Ezekiel 34:5
text:
vv 5-6. 
 
When pastors are unfaithful, "seeking their own, not the things which are Jesus Christ's," their flocks are soon scattered, a prey to the destroyer.

title: Ezekiel 34:7
text:
vv 7-22. 
 
God will see that his church is provided with faithful shepherds.  If those whom he has set over her neglect their work, and seek their own pleasure, profit, or honor, he will take from them the kingdom of heaven, and give it to pastors after his own heart.  Jeremiah 3:15 Matthew 21:43

title: Ezekiel 34:10
text: Require my flock at their hand; call them to an account for its destruction.

title: Ezekiel 34:17
text: I judge--he-goats; more exactly, I judge cattle against cattle, against rams and he-goats; I judge and protect the lean cattle against the fat cattle; namely, against the rams and he-gaots: that is, I defend my humble worshippers against their proud oppressors.  See  Ezekiel 34:20 .

title: Ezekiel 34:23
text:
One Shepherd--my servant David; the Messiah, who is "the good shepherd,"  John 10:14 . 
 
vv 23-24. 
 
The Lord Jesus is the great Shepherd and Prince of the churches.  From him alone all the under-shepherds receive grace to perform their sacred office aright; and to him alone must his people look, in times of declension and destitution, for a supply of faithful pastors.

title: Ezekiel 34:25
text:
vv 25-31. 
 
Whatever may be the general state of Christ's church, he supplies all the wants of those who make him the Shepherd and Bishop of their souls; defends them from every enemy, makes all their trials work together for their good, and finally gathers them into his heavenly fold, where they shall no more hunger or thirst for ever.  He will in due time extend his church universal over all the earth, and fill all nations, through her, with light and peace and blessedness.

title: Ezekiel 34:29
text: A Plant of renown; the same as "a righteous Branch,"  Jeremiah 23:5 ; that is, the Messiah.  The fulfilment of the promises recorded in this chapter extends through the whole history of the true church to the end of time.

title: Ezekiel 35:1
text: When God's people fall before their enemies, he will raise them up again; but when he destroys the enemies of his people, they perish utterly and for ever.  Where ancient Edom now is, there will be all who hate and persecute Christ's disciples, and think to enrich themselves by their calamities.

title: Ezekiel 35:5
text:
Had a perpetual hatred; the hatred of Edom towards Israel and Judah, and his malicious exultation over the calamities which came upon them, is the chief sin laid to the charge of this nation.  Compare  Ezekiel 25:12 Amos 1:11 Obadiah 1:10-15 . 
 
  Their iniquity had an end; see note on  Ezekiel 21:25 .

title: Ezekiel 35:6
text: Thou hast not hated blood; hast loved to shed blood  Ezekiel 35:5 .

title: Ezekiel 35:10
text:
These two nations; Judah and Israel. 
 
  The Lord was there; made the land of Judah and Israel, which he had given to Abraham's seed, his peculiar dwelling-place.

title: Ezekiel 35:15
text: Idumea; the same as Edom.

title: Ezekiel 36:1
text:
This and the following chapter contain a prophecy of the restoration of the remnant of both houses of Israel to their own land.  But with this the spirit of prophecy connects the whole future increase and prosperity of the church, of which the deliverance from Babylon was the sure pledge.  In and through that deliverance, God revealed to the prophet still higher blessings reserved for "the last days." 
 
vv 1-15. 
 
When God's people are unfaithful to him, he will chastise them and humble them before the world; yet he will not allow their enemies to triumph in their destruction, but will, for his own name's sake, have mercy upon them, restore them to more than their former prosperity and strength, and put to shame all who hate them.

title: Ezekiel 36:2
text: The enemy hath said; see  Ezekiel 35:10 .

title: Ezekiel 36:6
text: Shame; reproach,  Ezekiel 36:3 .

title: Ezekiel 36:8
text: Are at hand to come; shall speedily return from their captivity. In respect to promises of this kind, compare  II Peter 3:8-9 .

title: Ezekiel 36:13
text: Devourest up men; thy people are continually wasted by war, pestilence, and famine.

title: Ezekiel 36:16
text:
vv 16-24. 
 
When God visits and revives his people after a season of declension and weakness, they should remember that he does this, not for their sake, but for the glory of his own name.  They have deserved only evil at his hand.  He has mercy upon them, because he will magnify himself in their salvation.   Ezekiel 36:33

title: Ezekiel 36:23
text: Sanctify; make holy and honorable.

title: Ezekiel 36:25
text:
Then will I sprinkle; the glorious promise that follows is fulfilled to the church from age to age, in the sanctifying grace which God bestows upon her.  Its highest fulfilment belongs to the Christian dispensation. 
 
vv 25-27. 
 
The beginning of all true reformation is the inward cleansing of the soul by God's Spirit.  His power alone can change the heart of stone to flesh.  When this is done, men will render willing obedience to all God's statutes and judgments.  It is by "the washing of regeneration and renewing of the holy Ghost," that God continues to his church, from age to age, a seed of spiritual worshippers.

title: Ezekiel 36:28
text:
vv 28-30. 
 
Hearty repentance, with works meet for repentance, brings a return of peace and prosperity to churches and to individuals.   Ezekiel 36:33-35

title: Ezekiel 36:31
text: The effect of God's forgiving love upon true believers is not to lift them up with pride, but to humble them.  The more mercies he bestows upon them, the more they loathe themselves in view of their vileness and unworthiness.

title: Ezekiel 36:36
text: God will make his presence and power so manifest in his church, that her enemies without shall be compelled to see and acknowledge that he is with her, as her almighty Friend and Helper.

title: Ezekiel 36:37
text: It is through fervent prayer alone that God's people can obtain of him the rich blessings which he has promised them.

title: Ezekiel 36:38
text: Holy flock; brought to Jerusalem for sacrifice.

title: Ezekiel 37:1
text:
By a vision of the resurrection of dry bones, God represents to the prophet the restoration of his people from their present depraved condition,  Ezekiel 37:1-14 ; by another symbol, he sets forth the reunion of Judah and Israel in one body,  Ezekiel 37:15-22 .  From this event he then passes immediately to the future enlargement of the spiritual Israel under the reign of the Messiah, of which the restoration of the literal Israel was an earnest, and for which it prepared the way. 
 
vv 1-14. 
 
God is the eternal and uncreated source of all life, natural and spiritual.  No condition, this side of the prison of despair, is beyond the reach of his saving power.  He who will restore the bodies of all his saints to life and immortality "in a moment, in the twinkling of an eye, at the last trump," and grant them everlasting victory over death and the grave, is well able, here on earth, to deliver them in every extremity, however desperate it may appear in the judgment of man.

title: Ezekiel 37:11
text: We are cut off for our parts; more literally, "as for us, we are cut off."

title: Ezekiel 37:15
text:
vv 15-28. 
 
Schisms and divisions in the household of faith are not of God, but of the wicked one.  Our Saviour's last prayer for his disciples was, that all might be one in himself and the Father, as the Fatehr and he are one.  This prayer must be fulfilled in the reunion of God's divided family, before she can reach that glorious state of enlargement and prosperity which is promised in the last days.

title: Ezekiel 37:16
text:
For Judah--his companions; that is, for the kingdom of Judah and that part of Israel that belongs to it, namely, the two tribes of Judah and Benjamin. 
 
  For Joseph; a mode of designating the kingdom of Israel, after the separation of the ten tribes, because its principal tribes, Ephraim and Manasseh, were descended from Joseph.   Amos 5:15 Amos 6:6

title: Ezekiel 37:17
text: One stick--in thy hand; the healing of the great schism between the kingdoms of Judah and Israel, by the reunion, after the captivity, of the remnant of the ten tribes with the two tribes of Judah and Benjamin, is here foretold.  Compare  Ezekiel 37:19 Ezekiel 37:22 .  But Ezekiel does not stop with this auspicious event.  He goes on, after the usual manner of the prophets, to foretell the glorious days that shall follow in the distant future.

title: Ezekiel 37:24
text: David my servant; the Messiah, of David's line, and of whom David was an eminent type.   John 10:11 John 10:16

title: Ezekiel 38:1
text:
This and the following chapter contain a prophecy of the invasion of "the mountains of Israel" by an immense multitude "out of the north parts," assisted by many allies.  It shall take place "in the latter years," after Israel has been "brought back from the sword, and is gathered out of many people," and is dwelling safely in "unwalled villages;" and the invaders shall be overthrown with immense slaughter. It is generally agreed that the fulfilment of this prophecy is yet future.  Perhaps it is the same assault as that predicted in  Revelation of John 20:8-9 , which takes place after the binding of Satan for a thousand years. 
 
So far as the powers of darkness are left at liberty, they will stir up wicked men to persecute God's people.  Hereafter, as in past ages, we may expect mighty combinations of ungodly rulers and corrupt teachers to hinder, and if possible extinguish the light and liberty of the gospel.  But God will turn their counsels into foolishness, and make their mischievous plots the means of their own destruction.

title: Ezekiel 38:2
text: Gog, the land of Magog; Gog seems to be here the leader, and Magog the people.  Magog was descended from Japheth, and is named with other northern tribes,  Genesis 10:2 .

title: Ezekiel 38:4
text:
Hooks into thy jaws; see note on  Isaiah 37:29 . 
 
  Bring thee forth; out of my land.

title: Ezekiel 38:5
text:
vv 5-6. 
 
  Persia--Togarmah; these are the allies of Gog.

title: Ezekiel 38:7
text: Be thou prepared; God is here represented as calling forth Gog, that he may meet his final overthrow,  Ezekiel 38:16 .

title: Ezekiel 38:8
text:
Visited; punished; for his invasion of Israel is the occasion of his overthrow.  But many render, "shall be made chief," that is, of all the invading hosts. 
 
  Land that is brought back; land whose people are brought back. 
 
  Always waste; during the long exile of God's people from them. 
 
  It is brought forth; the same as, "the land that is brought back," that is, the people belonging to it are brought forth.

title: Ezekiel 38:11
text: Land of unwalled villages; these words indicate a long period of peace and security, in which walls have been omitted as unnecessary.

title: Ezekiel 38:12
text: Desolate places; once desolate,  Ezekiel 38:8 .

title: Ezekiel 38:13
text:
Sheba--Dedan--Tarshish; these seem to be the allies of Gog. 
 
  Young lions; princes.

title: Ezekiel 38:17
text: Of whom I have spoken in old time; compare  Isaiah 29:5-8   Joel 3:9-16 Zephaniah 3:8 .  All these prophets represent the final deliverance of God's people as preceded by a general assault of all their enemies upon them.

title: Ezekiel 38:19
text:
vv 19-22. 
 
  A great shaking--hailstones, fire, and brimstone; compare  Isaiah 29:6 Isaiah 30:30 Revelation of John 16:18 Revelation of John 16:21 .  Such descriptions are generally to be understood figuratively of the effects of God's wrath.

title: Ezekiel 39:1
text:
vv 1-7. 
 
God sometimes allows wicked men to mature their plans against his people, and to proceed very far in the accomplishment of them, that in the end they may thus receive a more complete and terrible overthrow, and his own power and justice be more gloriously manifested.

title: Ezekiel 39:8
text:
It is come; the destruction of Gog and his hosts. 
 
vv 8-10. 
 
They who openly seek to destroy and spoil God's people, shall be themselves destroyed and spoiled in the sight of all men.

title: Ezekiel 39:9
text:
Burn them with fire; better, kindle "fire with them, using them" for fuel. 
 
  Seven years; this denotes their immense quantity.

title: Ezekiel 39:11
text:
Valley of the passengers; for the reason of this name, see  Ezekiel 39:14-15 . 
 
  On the east of the sea; the Dead sea; so that it shall be without the limits of the Holy Land. 
 
vv 11-16. 
 
After that the counsels of wicked men have been effectually overthrown, a great work still remains to God's people to purify society from the pollution which their corrupt example and doctrine have introduced. This seems to be symbolized here by the care with which the fallen hosts of Gog are buried.

title: Ezekiel 39:13
text: A renown; for the burial of Gog is a sign of the victory which God has given them over him.

title: Ezekiel 39:14
text: Passing through the land--with the passengers; two classes of persons are employed, one to go through the land and set up signs where they find bones; the other, to bury them.  The reference here is to the scattered bones that shall remain after the seven months in which the whole house of Israel has been employed.  The "passengers" are not travellers, but men appointed to pass through the land, some as discoverers, others as buriers.

title: Ezekiel 39:17
text:
May eat flesh, and drink blood; before the Israelites can bury the slain of Gog, the beasts and birds of prey shall be feasted upon their carcasses.  Compare  Revelation of John 19:17-18 . 
 
vv 17-22. 
 
The terrible destruction which God often brings upon wicked men in this world, is at once an earnest and a solemn emblem of that wrath beyond the tomb which awaits all the finally impenitent.

title: Ezekiel 39:23
text:
vv 23-24. 
 
God will so deal with his offending people that all shall understand that their calamities have come upon them because of their own iniquities, and not through any want of power or faithfulness in him.

title: Ezekiel 39:25
text:
vv 25-29. 
 
It is not for us to determine beforehand "the times and seasons" for the fulfilment of the great events foretold in prophecy.  Curious computations respecting these are in general unsatisfactory and unprofitable.  But of this we may be sure, that God will gloriously fulfil all his promises to his people at the appointed time, give them the victory over all their foes, and establish them in perpetual peace and prosperity.

title: Ezekiel 40:1
text:
GENERAL REMARKS ON THE LAST NINE CHAPTERS OF THIS BOOK  Ezekiel 40:1-48:35  
 
The prophet with his countrymen has now been in captivity a quarter of a century; Jerusalem, with its holy and beautiful temple, and the whole land of Israel, have lain desolate for fourteen years, and all around looks dark and discouraging.  In this situation he sees in vision a new Jerusalem, with its temple, priests, and altar, rise out of the ruins of the former, of a larger extent and in a more glorious form; and the land is again divided out to the returning captives by lot, as it was at the beginning by Joshua. 
 
The general plan of the temple is after the model of Solomon's yet this vision is not to be understood as a mere prophecy of the rebuilding of Solomon's temple with the city in which it stood, and the repossession of the land after the Babylonish captivity.  Several particulars in the description make it plain that it was not intended to be literally understood.  See  Ezekiel 42:15-20 Ezekiel 45:1-8 Ezekiel 47:1-12 Ezekiel 48:1-35 .  It is rather a symbolical representation of the coming deliverance and enlargement of the true spiritual Zion, which is God's church, the same in all ages.  The resettlement of the land of Canaan, and the rebuilding of the city and temple after the captivity, were only a part, and a very small part of the "good things to come" which the vision shadowed forth.  Its fulfilment belongs to the whole history of the church from Ezekiel's day onward, and it will be completed only in her final triumph over the kingdom of Satan, and her establishment in permanent peace and holiness. 
 
As the time had not yet come for the old covenant to pass away, Ezekiel, who was himself a priest under the law of Moses, saw the future revival and enlargement of God's kingdom under the forms of this covenant.  The new Jerusalem which God revealed to him had its temple, priests, altar, and sacrifices.  All these were shadows of Christ's perfect priesthood, of the spiritual temple of which he is the chief corner-stone, and of the spiritual priesthood of his people.  I Peter 2:5-9  
 
In interpreting this vision, we should not curiously inquire after the meaning of every particular chamber and pillar and door, but rather look to the general meaning of the whole.  The angel measures, and the prophet records all the parts of the building.  This signifies, in general, that God's care extends to all parts of his spiritual temple, and that he will see that they are all in due time made perfect. 
 
The new Jerusalem described by the apostle John has much in common with this.  It is in truth a vision of the same spiritual city, "whose builder and maker is God."  But it differs from Ezekiel's vision in two respects.  First, it belongs apparently to the glorified state of the church after the final resurrection; secondly, it has nothing Jewish in it, neither temple nor altar.  All these  shadows have passed away for ever. 
 
vv 1-2. 
 
Many of the most glorious revelations recorded in the Bible were made by God in the darkest days of the church's history, that he might thus encourage the hearts of his servants, and show that he is always present with his people, and attending to their interests.

title: Ezekiel 40:2
text:
A very high mountain; it answers to the hills of Zion and Moriah, on which Jerusalem with its temple stood; yet it is not the literal Zion, nor any other actual mountain.  It exists only in vision, and answers to "the mountain of the Lord's house," which is to be in the last days "exalted above the hills,"  Isaiah 2:2 ; and to the "great and high mountain" which John sees,  Revelation of John 21:10 . 
 
  On the south; on the south to the prophet, as he comes in vision from the north.

title: Ezekiel 40:3
text: Like the appearance of brass; compare  Ezekiel 1:7 , and note.

title: Ezekiel 40:4
text: Whatever God sees good to reveal in any way concerning his kingdom of grace, is a matter of the deepest interest to all his people; and they who receive it should declare it to others with the utmost fidelity.

title: Ezekiel 40:5
text:
The house; that is, the temple with its courts. 
 
  By the cubit and a handbreadth; that is, reckoning the cubit and a handbreadth as one cubit,  Ezekiel 43:13 .  This makes the "great cubit"  Ezekiel 41:8 , of seven handbreadths, which seems to have been used for sacred purposes, and to be the same as the cubit "after the first measure,"  II Chronicles 3:3 .  The common cubit contained but six hand-breadths, or about twenty-one inches. 
 
  The building; that is, the structure of the wall.  It was one reed broad, and one high. 
 
vv 5-49. 
 
God never destroys any thing belonging to his church except for the purpose of rebuilding it again in a nobler and more enduring form.  His earthly temples, built by human hands, may perish; but his spiritual temple, not made with hands, which is Christ and his body the church, shall outlast all changes, and become more beautiful and glorious from age to age.

title: Ezekiel 40:6
text:
Unto the gate which looketh toward the east; the general plan of this temple with its courts is as follows: 
 
First, there is an outer court, lying four-square, and of great extent,  Ezekiel 40:17 Ezekiel 42:16-20 ; with rows of chambers round about, thirty in number,  Ezekiel 40:17 .  This court has three outer gates, one on the east side, one on the north, and one on the south, from each of which a passag-way leads inward with three little chambers on each side of it,  Ezekiel 40:6-26 . 
 
Secondly, there is an inner court, in front of the temple, with various chambers on its sides.  This has also three gates and passage-ways, opposite to and corresponding with those of the outer court.
